children.title: Globally Weakly Convex Objectives
children.top_down_role: Uniform-curvature objectives supporting global proximal-model analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Weakly Convex Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional global weak convexity with a uniform quadratic curvature parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is globally \(\rho\)-weakly convex, for \(\rho\ge 0\), if the function \(x\mapsto f(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert x\rVert^2\) is convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Equivalently, for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), \[f(tx+(1-t)y)\le t f(x)+(1-t)f(y)+\frac{\rho}{2}t(1-t)\lVert x-y\rVert^2.\] The same finite constant \(\rho\) applies throughout the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective is globally weakly convex when adding one fixed quadratic makes it convex everywhere, equivalently when its convexity inequality has a uniform quadratic error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f+(\rho/2)\lVert\cdot\rVert^2\) is convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

children.title: Local Weak-Convexity Lower-Smoothness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-dependent curvature regimes requiring localization.

children.title: Local Weak Convexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-dependent weak convexity across relevant regions of the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Weak Convexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise local weak convexity; the neighborhood and curvature modulus may vary with the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is locally weakly convex on an open set \(O\) if, for every \(\bar x\in O\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), there exist an open convex neighborhood \(U\subset O\) of \(\bar x\) and a finite constant \(\rho_U\ge 0\) such that \(x\mapsto f(x)+(\rho_U/2)\lVert x\rVert^2\) is convex on \(U\). No single modulus or neighborhood is required to work for all points of \(O\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Around every domain point, adding a neighborhood-dependent quadratic makes the objective convex; neither the neighborhood nor the curvature constant must be global.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\bar x\in O\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), there exist \(U\) and \(\rho_U<\infty\) for which \(f+(\rho_U/2)\lVert\cdot\rVert^2\) is convex on \(U\).

notation.meaning: convex neighborhood of the base point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed local definition is plausible and internally precise, but the cited locator concerns weak convexity generally and does not specifically establish this point-dependent neighborhood-and-modulus convention.

children.title: Lower-Smooth Objective Regimes
children.top_down_role: Objectives governed locally by lower-smooth variational structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Smooth Objective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interprets lower-smooth as the standard finite-dimensional lower-\(C^2\) local max representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-valued function \(f:O\to\mathbb{R}\), with \(O\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) open, is locally lower-\(C^2\) if every \(\bar x\in O\) has a neighborhood \(U\subset O\), a compact set \(T\), and functions \(q_t:U\to\mathbb{R}\) such that \[f(x)=\max_{t\in T}q_t(x)\quad(x\in U),\] each \(q_t\) is twice continuously differentiable in \(x\), and \((x,t)\mapsto(q_t(x),\nabla q_t(x),\nabla^2q_t(x))\) is continuous. Compactness yields a uniform lower Hessian bound on smaller compact neighborhoods, hence local weak convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally, the objective is the maximum of a compact, continuously parameterized family of twice-smooth functions, which supplies a local lower-curvature bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) admits the displayed local lower-\(C^2\) representation and is locally weakly convex.

notation.meaning: compact index set of smooth pieces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-C2 representation and its implication of local weak convexity depend on a convention that must be confirmed by an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Curvature Localization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring local curvature control between neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Localization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation between pointwise local and globally uniform weak convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(f(x)=-x^4\). For every bounded interval \(U=(-R,R)\), choosing \(\rho_U=12R^2\) gives \(f''(x)+\rho_U=-12x^2+12R^2\ge 0\) on \(U\), so \(f\) is weakly convex locally. For any finite \(\rho\), however, \(f''(x)+\rho=-12x^2+\rho<0\) whenever \(|x|>\sqrt{\rho/12}\). Thus local curvature moduli that grow with the localization radius do not imply any global weak-convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function minus the fourth power is weakly convex on every bounded neighborhood but admits no finite curvature modulus valid on the whole line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is locally weakly convex but is not globally \(\rho\)-weakly convex for any finite \(\rho\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly separates local from global weak convexity, and failure_boundary is the correct role, but the record supplies neither cited evidence nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Constrained Weakly Convex Objectives
children.top_down_role: Weakly convex objectives combined with simple feasible-set geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Weakly Convex Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex constraints represented by an indicator in the extended-valued objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and lower-semicontinuous, suppose \(C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\ne\varnothing\), and assume that \(f+(\rho/2)\lVert\cdot\rVert^2\) is convex on an open convex set \(O\supset C\), where \(\rho\ge0\). Define \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise, and set \(F=f+\delta_C\). Then \[F(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2+\delta_C(x)\] is convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Hence \(F\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous \(\rho\)-weakly convex objective, and minimizing \(F\) over \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is equivalent to minimizing \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the indicator of a closed convex feasible set preserves the weak-convexity modulus, provided the objective is weakly convex around the feasible set and has at least one feasible domain point.
assumptions_latex: For some open convex \(O\supset C\), the function \(f+(\rho/2)\lVert\cdot\rVert^2\) is convex on \(O\), with \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=f+\delta_C\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}F(x)\).

notation.meaning: extended-valued indicator of the feasible set
open convex neighborhood of the feasible set

children.title: Convex-Composite Representations
children.top_down_role: Convex outer structure coupled to a smooth inner mapping.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Composite Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex globally Lipschitz outer function composed with a smooth map having Lipschitz Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(c:D\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, and suppose its Jacobian is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz on \(D\). Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and globally \(L_h\)-Lipschitz, and define \(F=h\circ c\). Then, for all \(x,y\in D\), \[F(y)\ge h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x)\bigr)-\frac{L_h\beta}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2.\] Consequently, \(F\) is \(L_h\beta\)-weakly convex on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex globally Lipschitz outer function composed with a smooth map having Lipschitz Jacobian is weakly convex and admits a convex linearized-composite model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=h\circ c\) is \(L_h\beta\)-weakly convex on \(D\) and satisfies the displayed model inequality.

children.title: Smooth-plus-Nonsmooth Representations
children.top_down_role: Additive structure supporting proximal-gradient models.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-plus-Nonsmooth Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive composite form underlying deterministic proximal-gradient models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=g(x)+h(x)\), where \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex. The descent lemma gives \[g(y)\ge g(x)+\langle\nabla g(x),y-x\rangle-\frac{L}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2.\] Therefore \(F\) is \(L\)-weakly convex, and its convex local model at \(x\) is \(m_x(y)=g(x)+\langle\nabla g(x),y-x\rangle+h(y)\), with \(F(y)\ge m_x(y)-(L/2)\lVert y-x\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth function with Lipschitz gradient plus a closed convex function is weakly convex and has the standard proximal-gradient linearization model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=g+h\) is \(L\)-weakly convex and obeys \(F(y)\ge m_x(y)-(L/2)\lVert y-x\rVert^2\).

children.title: Finite-Max Representations
children.top_down_role: Finite collections of active branches used to construct local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Max Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maximum of smooth branches with uniform lower curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, and let \(f_i:D\to\mathbb{R}\), for \(i=1,\ldots,p\), be continuously differentiable with \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradients. Define \[F(x)=\max_{1\le i\le p}f_i(x).\] Each \(f_i\) is \(L_i\)-weakly convex on \(D\). Hence, with \(\rho=\max_{1\le i\le p}L_i\), every function \(f_i+(\rho/2)\lVert\cdot\rVert^2\) is convex on \(D\). Their pointwise maximum is \(F+(\rho/2)\lVert\cdot\rVert^2\), so \(F\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open convex domain, the maximum of finitely many smooth branches with Lipschitz gradients is weakly convex, with the largest gradient-Lipschitz constant as a valid modulus.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable with \(L_i\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\max_{1\le i\le p}f_i\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(D\) for \(\rho=\max_{1\le i\le p}L_i\).

children.title: Value-Function Representations
children.top_down_role: Objectives represented through subordinate optimization values.

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactly indexed maximum value function with a uniform weak-convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be compact and let \(\phi:D\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, where \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex. Define the value function \[V(x)=\max_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y).\] If, for every \(y\in Y\), the mapping \(x\mapsto\phi(x,y)\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(D\) with the same finite \(\rho\), then \(x\mapsto V(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert x\rVert^2\) is the pointwise maximum of convex functions. Consequently \(V\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(D\), and compactness ensures that the maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact maximum value function inherits weak convexity when every parameterized branch has the same curvature bound, and an active parameter exists at every point.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is continuous and every \(\phi(\cdot,y)\) is uniformly \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=\max_{y\in Y}\phi(x,y)\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex and has a nonempty argmax set.

children.title: Active-Branch Value Interactions
children.top_down_role: Representation regimes combining branch activity with subordinate values.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Branch Value Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivative and Clarke subdifferential formulas for finite smooth maxima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\max_{1\le i\le p}f_i(x)\), where every \(f_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\), and define the active set \(I(x)=\{i:f_i(x)=F(x)\}\). Then \(F\) is directionally differentiable and locally Lipschitz near \(x\), with \[F'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}\langle\nabla f_i(x),d\rangle\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n,\] and its Clarke subdifferential is \[\partial_C F(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla f_i(x):i\in I(x)\}.\] Thus only value-attaining branches contribute first-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite smooth maximum, directional change is the maximum active gradient pairing, and the Clarke subdifferential is the convex hull of active gradients.
assumptions_latex: Every branch \(f_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F'(x;d)=\max_{i\in I(x)}\langle\nabla f_i(x),d\rangle\) and \(\partial_C F(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla f_i(x):i\in I(x)\}\).

children.title: Prox-Regular Regimes
children.top_down_role: Localized proximal geometries supporting stable nonsmooth models.

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Regular Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise prox-regularity relative to a specified limiting subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is prox-regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) if \(f(\bar x)\) is finite and there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(r\ge 0\) such that \[f(x')\ge f(x)+\langle v,x'-x\rangle-\frac r2\lVert x'-x\rVert^2\] whenever \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<\varepsilon\), \(\lVert x'-\bar x\rVert<\varepsilon\), \(|f(x)-f(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\), and \(v\in\partial f(x)\) satisfies \(\lVert v-\bar v\rVert<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a reference point and subgradient, every nearby subgradient supplies a uniform quadratic lower support inequality for nearby comparison points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed quadratic subgradient inequality holds locally with uniform \(r\) for graph points near \((\bar x,\bar v)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement resembles the standard pointwise definition of prox-regularity, but its precise graph, value-localization, and limiting-subdifferential conventions require an authoritative definition or theorem locator.

children.title: Primal-Lower-Nice Regimes
children.top_down_role: Primal lower regularity settings used by nonconvex bundle constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Lower-Nice Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic lower support with curvature allowed to grow linearly in subgradient norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is primal-lower-nice at \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and a constant \(c\ge 0\) such that, for every \(x,x'\in U\) and every \(v\in\partial f(x)\), \[f(x')\ge f(x)+\langle v,x'-x\rangle-\frac c2\bigl(1+\lVert v\rVert\bigr)\lVert x'-x\rVert^2.\] The defining distinction from a uniform weak-convexity inequality is the permitted linear dependence of the quadratic curvature coefficient on \(\lVert v\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nearby subgradient gives a quadratic lower support, but the allowed negative curvature may grow linearly with that subgradient's norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed lower-support inequality holds on some neighborhood with coefficient \(c(1+\lVert v\rVert)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Primal-lower-nice definitions vary in their subdifferential, neighborhood, and curvature-growth quantifiers. With no authoritative locator, the proposed condition cannot be validated reliably.

children.title: Localized Proximal Stability
children.top_down_role: Shared stability consequences of the two variational regularity regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Localized Proximal Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localized resolvent stability near a reference subgradient of a prox-regular function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). For all sufficiently small \(\lambda>0\), there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x+\lambda\bar v\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that the localized proximal mapping \[P_{\lambda,f}^{V}(z):=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{y\in V}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-z\|^2\right\}\] is single-valued and Lipschitz on \(U\), with \(P_{\lambda,f}^{V}(\bar x+\lambda\bar v)=\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a prox-regular reference pair, sufficiently small proximal steps define a unique, Lipschitz-continuous localized proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\lambda,f}^{V}\) is locally single-valued and Lipschitz, and \(P_{\lambda,f}^{V}(\bar x+\lambda\bar v)=\bar x\).
review_flags: Exact prox-regularity theorem and admissible stepsize require an authoritative locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf and is plausibly standard, but the precise localization, admissible stepsizes, and Lipschitz conclusion require a theorem-level authoritative locator.

children.title: Locally Lipschitz Black-Box Regimes
children.top_down_role: Oracle-access settings with limited structural curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Lipschitz Black-Box Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic local-oracle regime without an exposed analytic decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A locally Lipschitz black-box regime consists of minimizing \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) over a closed set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(f\) is locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(X\), but no formula, decomposition, or global curvature parameter is supplied. At a queried point \(x\in X\), the interface returns \(f(x)\) and at least one generalized gradient \(g\in\partial_C f(x)\). An algorithm may use only these returned quantities, previous queries, and the known description of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective is locally Lipschitz but structurally opaque; algorithms access it only through deterministic values and Clarke generalized gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_f(x)=(f(x),g)\) with \(g\in\partial_C f(x)\), while no additional representation of \(f\) is available.

notation.meaning: Clarke subdifferential of f at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard deterministic locally Lipschitz oracle model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the black-box-regime container, but requiring exact values and Clarke subgradients is a specific oracle convention not established by cited evidence.

children.title: Difference-of-Convex Bundle Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings using paired convex components or difference-of-convex local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Bundle Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional DC objectives represented by paired convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, and let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions with \(X\subseteq\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\). Define \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) by \[f(y)=g(y)-h(y).\] For any \(x\in X\) and \(v\in\partial h(x)\), the convex local model \[m_x(y)=g(y)-h(x)-\langle v,y-x\rangle\] satisfies \(m_x(x)=f(x)\) and \(f(y)\le m_x(y)\) for every \(y\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the convex feasible set, a DC objective is modeled by retaining one convex component and affine-minorizing the subtracted convex component at a specified base point.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_x\) is convex, \(m_x(x)=f(x)\), and \(f(y)\le m_x(y)\) for every \(y\in X\).

children.title: Exact First-Order Oracles
children.top_down_role: Exact objective-value and generalized-gradient access.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact First-Order Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic exact value and generalized-gradient access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and a specified generalized subdifferential \(\partial f\), an exact first-order oracle is a mapping that, at every query \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), returns \[\mathcal O_f(x)=(f(x),g_x),\qquad g_x\in\partial f(x).\] Both the value and the membership assertion are exact: the oracle introduces no numerical, sampling, or deterministic approximation error. When \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), the convention reduces to \(g_x=\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each query returns the exact objective value and an exact member of the chosen generalized subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: A generalized subdifferential \(\partial f\) is fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_f(x)=(f(x),g_x)\) with \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\) exactly.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard deterministic first-order oracle definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the oracle container, but the claim that differentiability forces the returned element to equal the gradient depends on properties of the selected generalized subdifferential. An authoritative oracle definition and subdifferential convention are needed.

children.title: Inexact-Approximate Oracle Family
children.top_down_role: Controlled errors in values, generalized gradients, and subordinate solves.

children.title: Inexact Value Oracles
children.top_down_role: Controlled objective-value errors used in model construction or acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Value Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic absolute-error convention for objective evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and a prescribed tolerance function \(\varepsilon_f:X\to[0,+\infty)\), an inexact value oracle returns \(\widetilde f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\) at each query \(x\in X\) together with the certified bound \[|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\le \varepsilon_f(x).\] Equivalently, the unknown exact value belongs to the reported interval \([\widetilde f(x)-\varepsilon_f(x),\widetilde f(x)+\varepsilon_f(x)]\). The oracle is exact at queries for which \(\varepsilon_f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate objective value is valid when its certified absolute error does not exceed the prescribed query tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\le\varepsilon_f(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard deterministic absolute-error oracle convention
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-error condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but it is one particular inexact-value convention and has no inspectable source locator.

children.title: Approximate Generalized-Gradient Oracles
children.top_down_role: Approximate first-order information for nonsmooth local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Generalized-Gradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-to-subdifferential convention for approximate first-order information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a generalized subdifferential \(\partial f\) for a proper function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). At a query \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\), an approximate generalized-gradient oracle returns \(\widetilde g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \[\operatorname{dist}(\widetilde g,\partial f(x))\le\varepsilon_g.\] Thus there exists \(g\in\partial f(x)\) with \(\|\widetilde g-g\|\le\varepsilon_g\). The case \(\varepsilon_g=0\), with a closed subdifferential value, recovers exact generalized-gradient access.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reported vector is acceptable when its distance from the selected generalized subdifferential is within the certified tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The generalized subdifferential \(\partial f\) and norm are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(\widetilde g,\partial f(x))\le\varepsilon_g\).

children.title: Inexact Subordinate-Solve Oracles
children.top_down_role: Oracle information produced through approximate inner optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subordinate-Solve Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified objective-gap convention for nested optimization solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a query parameter \(x\in X\) define a subordinate problem with feasible set \(Y(x)\ne\varnothing\), objective \(\Phi_x:Y(x)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and finite value \(p(x):=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}\Phi_x(y)\). Given \(\varepsilon_s\ge0\), an inexact subordinate-solve oracle returns \(\widetilde y\in Y(x)\) satisfying \[0\le\Phi_x(\widetilde y)-p(x)\le\varepsilon_s.\] Its associated approximate subordinate value is \(\widetilde p(x):=\Phi_x(\widetilde y)\), so \(p(x)\le\widetilde p(x)\le p(x)+\varepsilon_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested solve is inexactly valid when it returns a feasible point whose subordinate objective gap is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde y\in Y(x)\) and \(0\le\Phi_x(\widetilde y)-p(x)\le\varepsilon_s\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard objective-gap definition of an approximate optimization solution
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-gap condition is coherent and appropriate for the leaf, but no source supports this particular definition of an inexact subordinate-solve oracle.

children.title: Oracle Error Certification
children.top_down_role: Observable controls governing admissible oracle inaccuracies.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Error Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable bounds accompanying deterministic inexact oracle outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a query \(x\), an oracle error certificate is a tuple \(C_x=(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_s)\in\mathbb{R}_+^3\) accompanying outputs \((\widetilde f,\widetilde g,\widetilde y)\). Relative to specified objects \(f\), \(\partial f\), and subordinate problem \((Y(x),\Phi_x)\), it certifies the outputs when \[|\widetilde f-f(x)|\le\varepsilon_f,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(\widetilde g,\partial f(x))\le\varepsilon_g,\qquad \widetilde y\in Y(x),\quad \Phi_x(\widetilde y)-\inf_{y\in Y(x)}\Phi_x(y)\le\varepsilon_s.\] Components corresponding to outputs not requested may be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reported error bounds certify value, generalized-gradient, and subordinate-solve inaccuracies against explicitly specified reference objects.
assumptions_latex: The reference objective, subdifferential, and subordinate problem are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_x\) certifies every displayed oracle error inequality for the returned outputs.
review_flags: A canonical deterministic certification framework and treatment of omitted components need a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf, but the subordinate-gap expression requires a finite subordinate infimum, and the combined optional-component certificate framework lacks an authoritative source.

children.title: Structured Model-Subproblem Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Convex, composite, quadratic, constrained, and tangent-program subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Model-Subproblem Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic proximal interface for structured local models and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a base point \(x_k\in X\), a proper lower-semicontinuous model \(m_{x_k}:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a closed feasible set \(X\), and \(\lambda_k>0\). Compute an exact or certified inexact solution of \[x_{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{y\in X}\left\{m_{x_k}(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.\] Return \(x_{k+1}\), the model value, and any available optimality residual or objective-gap certificate. The interface permits convex, composite, quadratic, constrained, or tangent-program models whenever the displayed subproblem is well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface sends an anchored structured model plus proximal regularization and constraints to a subordinate solver.
assumptions_latex: The displayed subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) solves, or is certified to approximately solve, the regularized structured model subproblem.

children.title: Base-Point-Consistent Models
children.top_down_role: Models anchored to objective information at the current base point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zeroth-order interpolation of an extended-real objective by its anchored model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(m_x\) be a model with \(x\in\operatorname{dom}m_x\). The model is base-point consistent exactly when \[m_x(x)=f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is base-point consistent when it has the same finite value as the objective at its anchor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x(x)=f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Base-Point Value Consistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value Consistency Does Not Imply First-Order Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of base-point value interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)\equiv0\) and \(m_x(y)=|y-x|\). Then \(m_x(x)=f(x)=0\), but for the convex subdifferential, \[\partial m_x(x)=[-1,1]\not\subseteq\{0\}=\partial f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching the objective value at the anchor does not force matching first-order information.
assumptions_latex: The convex subdifferential is used for both functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x(x)=f(x)\not\Rightarrow\partial m_x(x)\subseteq\partial f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Value Consistency Does Not Imply First-Order Consistency
Base-Point-Consistent Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zeroth-order consistency of a local model at its anchor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(x\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(m_x:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a model anchored at \(x\). The model is base-point consistent when \[m_x(x)=f(x).\] If the method also uses first-order consistency, the stronger condition is \(m_x(x)=f(x)\) together with \(\partial m_x(x)\subseteq\partial f(x)\), for the same specified generalized subdifferential. Base-point consistency alone refers only to the displayed value equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is base-point consistent exactly when its value equals the objective value at the anchoring point.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The value-equality condition fits the leaf and is standard, but the record has no source; its additional first-order inclusion convention is also subdifferential-dependent.

children.title: One-Sided Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Models controlled by a one-sided local approximation relationship.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic one-sided upper control of objective error by an anchored model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(m_x\) be a base-point-consistent model at \(x\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). The model has one-sided quadratic accuracy with constant \(\rho\ge0\) on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) when \[f(y)\le m_x(y)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|y-x\|^2\qquad\text{for every }y\in X\cap U.\] Thus the model may overestimate \(f\) arbitrarily, but its underestimation is bounded by a quadratic localization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally, the objective cannot exceed its anchored model by more than a quadratic error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)-m_x(y)\le\frac{\rho}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) for all \(y\in X\cap U\).
review_flags: The selected upper-error orientation should be checked against the chapter's model convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent, but a section on weakly convex functions does not by itself support this generic anchored-model inequality or confirm its chosen orientation and normalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent from One-Sided Accuracy and Proximal Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed descent consequence coupling one-sided accuracy with a stabilized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m_x(x)=f(x)\), \(f(y)\le m_x(y)+(\rho/2)\|y-x\|^2\), and \(y\) minimizes \(m_x(z)+(2t)^{-1}\|z-x\|^2\), then \[f(x)-f(y)\ge(1-\rho t)\bigl(m_x(x)-m_x(y)\bigr)\ge\frac{1/t-\rho}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under one orientation, sufficiently strong proximal stabilization converts model decrease into objective descent.
assumptions_latex: \(t>0\), \(\rho\ge0\), and the subproblem feasible set contains \(x\).
The stated one-sided estimate holds at the trial point.
review_flags: Canonical-home failure: this statement primarily concerns proximal stabilization and an acceptance threshold, not the definition of one-sided model accuracy.
The result is also conditional on the unresolved orientation of the deferred seed.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent from One-Sided Accuracy and Proximal Minimization

Its orientation remains materially ambiguous, so the proposed descent record is deferred as misplaced. children.title: Two-Sided Taylor-Like Model Accuracy Pair
children.top_down_role: Models with stronger symmetric or Taylor-like local fidelity.

children.title: Two-Sided Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Local fidelity controlled from both overestimation and underestimation directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric quadratic fidelity between an objective and its anchored model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(m_x\) be a base-point-consistent model at \(x\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). The model has two-sided quadratic accuracy with constant \(L\ge0\) on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) when \[|f(y)-m_x(y)|\le\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2\qquad\text{for every }y\in X\cap U.\] Equivalently, both \(f(y)\le m_x(y)+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) and \(m_x(y)\le f(y)+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) hold locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective and anchored model differ locally by at most a symmetric quadratic error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f(y)-m_x(y)|\le\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) for all \(y\in X\cap U\).
review_flags: An authoritative locator is needed for the quadratic two-sided convention and normalization factor.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetric quadratic condition fits the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but an authoritative locator is required for this specific two-sided convention and its factor of one half.

children.title: Taylor-Like Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Local model fidelity patterned after higher-quality smooth approximations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical smooth sufficient condition for a quadratically accurate affine Taylor model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be convex and let \(g:U\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. For \(x,y\in U\), define \(m_x(y)=g(x)+\langle\nabla g(x),y-x\rangle\). Then \[|g(y)-m_x(y)|\le\frac L2\|y-x\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz gradient makes the affine first-order Taylor model symmetrically quadratically accurate.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\nabla g(u)-\nabla g(v)\|\le L\|u-v\|\) for all \(u,v\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|g(y)-g(x)-\langle\nabla g(x),y-x\rangle|\le(L/2)\|y-x\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz-Gradient Taylor Fidelity
Taylor-Like Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic two-sided accuracy for a base-point model of a weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and for each \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) let \(f_x:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be a model satisfying \(f_x(x)=f(x)\). The model family has Taylor-like accuracy with constant \(\omega\ge 0\) on \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) when, for every \(x,y\in D\), both values are finite and
\[
\lvert f(y)-f_x(y)\rvert\le \frac{\omega}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2.
\]
Thus the model error vanishes to second order at its base point, without requiring differentiability of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is Taylor-like accurate when it matches the objective at its base point and its absolute error grows at most quadratically with displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_x(x)=f(x)\) and \(\lvert f(y)-f_x(y)\rvert\le (\omega/2)\lVert y-x\rVert^2\) for all \(x,y\in D\).

notation.meaning: model of the objective based at x
region on which accuracy is required

review_flags: Exact model-accuracy convention is not supported by the supplied locators.
A source distinguishing absolute two-sided accuracy from one-sided model accuracy is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, but no citation establishes that this leaf uses symmetric absolute quadratic error rather than a one-sided model-accuracy convention.

children.title: Symmetric Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric settings where stronger two-sided fidelity is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Fidelity Does Not Imply Symmetric Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between one-sided upper control and a symmetric quadratic bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=0\) and \(m_x(y)=|y-x|\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(m_x(x)=f(x)\) and \(f(y)\le m_x(y)\), so the oriented condition \(f(y)\le m_x(y)+(\rho/2)|y-x|^2\) holds with \(\rho=0\). No finite \(L\) satisfies \[m_x(y)\le f(y)+\frac L2|y-x|^2\] throughout any neighborhood of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect one-sided upper control can coexist with a linear reverse error, precluding symmetric quadratic fidelity.
assumptions_latex: The one-sided orientation is stated explicitly in the record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One-sided quadratic accuracy does not imply two-sided quadratic accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Fidelity Does Not Imply Symmetric Fidelity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiability Does Not Ensure Quadratic Taylor Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a quadratic Taylor remainder without locally Lipschitz derivative control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(u)=|u|^{3/2}\), the affine Taylor model at \(0\) is \(m_0(y)=0\). Hence \[|f(y)-m_0(y)|=|y|^{3/2}.\] For every finite \(L\), the inequality \(|y|^{3/2}\le(L/2)|y|^2\) fails at sufficiently small nonzero \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable function need not have a quadratically accurate affine Taylor model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite local symmetric quadratic-fidelity constant exists for \(m_0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Differentiability Does Not Ensure Quadratic Taylor Fidelity
Symmetric Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent upper and lower quadratic envelopes around the modeled objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a model \(f_x\) of \(f\) on \(D\), the symmetric fidelity bound with constant \(\omega\ge0\) is the pair
\[
f_x(y)-\frac{\omega}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\le f(y)\le f_x(y)+\frac{\omega}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2
\]
for all \(x,y\in D\). This pair is equivalent to
\[
\lvert f(y)-f_x(y)\rvert\le\frac{\omega}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2.
\]
At \(y=x\), either formulation forces exact base-point fidelity \(f_x(x)=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective lies between matching lower and upper quadratic envelopes of its model; equivalently, the absolute model error is quadratically bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(f(y)\) and \(f_x(y)\) are finite for all \(x,y\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two quadratic envelope inequalities are equivalent to \(\lvert f(y)-f_x(y)\rvert\le(\omega/2)\lVert y-x\rVert^2\).
review_flags: The algebraic equivalence is standard, but the intended model-framework source is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The envelope/absolute-error equivalence is correct, but the record lacks evidence that these symmetric boundaries are the intended fidelity convention in this model framework.

children.title: Localized-Inexact Model Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-restricted models and models incorporating controlled error.

children.title: Localized Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Model fidelity restricted to specified neighborhoods or trusted regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-dependent quadratic Taylor-model accuracy without a global uniform constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(u)=u^3\) and \(m_x(y)=x^3+3x^2(y-x)\). With \(h=y-x\), \[f(y)-m_x(y)=3xh^2+h^3.\] Therefore, for every \(x\) and \(r_x>0\), \[|f(y)-m_x(y)|\le(3|x|+r_x)|y-x|^2\quad\text{when }|y-x|\le r_x,\] but no finite \(C\) satisfies \(|f(y)-m_x(y)|\le C|y-x|^2\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine Taylor models of the cubic have point-dependent local quadratic accuracy but no global uniform quadratic constant.
assumptions_latex: \(m_x\) is the affine Taylor model of \(f(u)=u^3\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Point-dependent localized quadratic accuracy does not imply global uniform quadratic accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Localized Accuracy Need Not Globalize
Localized Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic model accuracy required only within a base-point-dependent neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\). A model family \(\{f_x:x\in D\}\) has localized quadratic accuracy if there exist \(r>0\) and \(\omega\ge0\) such that, for every \(x\in D\) and every \(y\in D\cap B(x,r)\),
\[
f_x(x)=f(x),\qquad \lvert f(y)-f_x(y)\rvert\le\frac{\omega}{2}\lVert y-x\rVert^2.
\]
A point-dependent version permits positive radii \(r_x\) and locally bounded constants \(\omega_x\), with the same inequality on \(D\cap B(x,r_x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Localized accuracy imposes the quadratic fidelity bound only near each model base point, uniformly or with locally controlled point-dependent constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic model-error bound holds whenever \(y\in D\cap B(x,r)\), or locally with \(r_x\) and \(\omega_x\).

notation.meaning: open ball of radius r centered at x

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies the intended uniform or point-dependent localization convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Uniform-radius and point-dependent localization are distinct conventions. A source is needed to determine which belongs in this exact leaf and what local boundedness means.

children.title: Inexact Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Model fidelity permitting controlled construction or evaluation error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Triangle-inequality transfer from an exact quadratically accurate model to a value-perturbed model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|f(y)-m_k(y)|\le (\omega/2)\|y-x_k\|^2\) and \(|\widetilde m_k(y)-m_k(y)|\le e_k(y)\). Then \[|f(y)-\widetilde m_k(y)|\le \frac{\omega}{2}\|y-x_k\|^2+e_k(y).\] In particular, a uniform bound \(e_k(y)\le\varepsilon_k\) yields a uniform additive allowance, and \(|f(x_k)-\widetilde m_k(x_k)|\le e_k(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbing an exact model by a bounded value error adds that error to its quadratic fidelity bound and controls the resulting anchoring mismatch.
assumptions_latex: The exact-model and perturbation bounds hold at the same admissible trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f(y)-\widetilde m_k(y)|\le(\omega/2)\|y-x_k\|^2+e_k(y)\).

notation.meaning: reference exact model at iteration k

review_flags: This transfer property does not select among uniform, pointwise, or relative inexactness conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation Transfer for Inexact Models
Inexact Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic model fidelity augmented by a deterministic, iteration-dependent error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given base points \(x_k\in D\), models \(f_{x_k}\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), the models have inexact quadratic accuracy with constant \(\omega\ge0\) when
\[
f_{x_k}(x_k)=f(x_k),\qquad
\lvert f(y)-f_{x_k}(y)\rvert\le\frac{\omega}{2}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2+\varepsilon_k
\]
for every admissible trial point \(y\in D\). If base-point evaluation is also inexact, it is instead required that \(\lvert f(x_k)-f_{x_k}(x_k)\rvert\le\varepsilon_k\), with the displayed error bound retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact model permits an additive deterministic tolerance beyond quadratic model error, and may also permit bounded mismatch at the base point.
assumptions_latex: \(f(y)\) and \(f_{x_k}(y)\) are finite at admissible trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert f(y)-f_{x_k}(y)\rvert\le(\omega/2)\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2+\varepsilon_k\).

notation.meaning: model base point at iteration k
model based at the kth iterate

review_flags: Several inequivalent inexactness conventions exist; no supplied locator selects one.
Base-point inexactness convention requires source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error and inexact-base-point alternatives are inequivalent model conventions; no source selects or supports the combined formulation.

children.title: Local Error Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between neighborhood validity and admissible model error.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Error Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decay condition ensuring additive inexactness does not dominate local quadratic fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For accepted trial points \(y_k\) and steps \(s_k=y_k-x_k\), an additive model-error sequence \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\) is locally compatible with quadratic accuracy when
\[
\varepsilon_k=O(\lVert s_k\rVert^2).
\]
It is asymptotically negligible when the stronger condition
\[
\varepsilon_k=o(\lVert s_k\rVert^2)
\]
holds along every subsequence with nonzero \(s_k\to0\). Under the first condition, quadratic model-error estimates retain a bounded effective constant; under the second, the inexact contribution vanishes after normalization by squared step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local compatibility requires additive model errors to decay at least as fast as squared step lengths; little-o decay makes them asymptotically negligible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundedness of \(\varepsilon_k/\lVert s_k\rVert^2\) preserves quadratic order; convergence of this ratio to zero makes inexactness negligible.
review_flags: The compatibility criterion is mathematically natural but unsupported by the supplied source inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The big-O and little-o conditions are mathematically meaningful, but no cited source establishes them as the intended local compatibility conditions for this framework.

children.title: Proximal-Point Models
children.top_down_role: Exact-objective models combined with proximal regularization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates supplied by an exact proximal-point model solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\), \[v:=\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\in\partial f(p),\qquad f(p)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|v\|^2\le f(x),\] and \(p=x\iff0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled proximal step is a subgradient at the new point, certifies descent, and vanishes exactly at stationary points.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the weakly convex proximal-point model hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\in\partial f(p),\quad f(p)+(\lambda/2)\|v\|^2\le f(x),\quad p=x\iff0\in\partial f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Optimality and Descent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-parameter complexity for exact proximal-point model solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is bounded below and \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x_k)\), define \(v_{k+1}=\lambda^{-1}(x_k-x_{k+1})\). Then \[\min_{1\le j\le N}\|v_j\|^2\le\frac{2(f(x_0)-\inf f)}{\lambda N}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact proximal-point iterations obtain an epsilon-small subgradient residual within order epsilon to the minus two solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{1\le j\le N}\|v_j\|^2\le2(f(x_0)-\inf f)/(\lambda N).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-objective model with quadratic proximal regularization.

Proximal-Point Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-objective proximal model for minimizing a proper weakly convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a proper lower-semicontinuous \(\rho\)-weakly convex function \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), an initial point \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and parameters \(\lambda_k\in(0,1/\rho)\), with \(1/0=+\infty\). At iteration \(k\), form the exact-objective proximal model
\[
M_k(y)=f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2
\]
and choose \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}M_k(y)\). Stop under a prescribed stationarity or step-size test and output the last iterate. The parameter restriction makes \(M_k\) strongly convex when \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-point model minimizes the exact weakly convex objective plus a quadratic centered at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}\{f(y)+(2\lambda_k)^{-1}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Subgradient Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine subgradient model stabilized by a quadratic proximal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(x_0\in D\), positive stepsizes \(\alpha_k\), and a function \(f\) admitting a selected subgradient \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). At iteration \(k\), define
\[
M_k(y)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,y-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2
\]
and choose \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in D}M_k(y)\). For \(D=X\), the update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k g_k\); for closed convex \(D\), it is \(x_{k+1}=P_D(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\). Stop by a prescribed iteration, step, or stationarity test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal subgradient model minimizes a subgradient affine approximation plus quadratic stabilization, yielding a subgradient or projected-subgradient step.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional and Euclidean, and \(D\subseteq X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=P_D(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), with \(P_X\) equal to the identity.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Gradient Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive composite model retaining the nonsmooth convex term and linearizing the smooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and let \(F=g+r\), where \(g:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and \(r:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, closed, and convex. For a base point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}r\) and parameter \(t>0\), the proximal-gradient model is
\[
Q_t(y;x)=g(x)+\langle\nabla g(x),y-x\rangle+r(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert y-x\rVert^2.
\]
This model has the unique minimizer
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}Q_t(y;x)=\left\{\operatorname{prox}_{tr}\bigl(x-t\nabla g(x)\bigr)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-gradient model keeps the nonsmooth convex component exact, replaces the smooth component by its affine expansion at the base point, and adds quadratic stabilization. Its unique minimizer is the proximal-gradient point.
assumptions_latex: \(r:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}Q_t(y;x)=\{\operatorname{prox}_{tr}(x-t\nabla g(x))\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically stabilized affine models minimized over a closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(x\in C\). Given \(g\in X\) and \(t>0\), define the projected affine model
\[
Q_t(y;x,g)=\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert y-x\rVert^2+\delta_C(y).
\]
Its unique minimizer is
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}Q_t(y;x,g)=\left\{P_C(x-tg)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, for a direction \(d=-g\), the projected model point is \(P_C(x+td)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected model adds the feasible-set indicator to a quadratically stabilized affine model. Its unique minimizer is the Euclidean projection of the unconstrained trial point onto the closed convex feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in X}Q_t(y;x,g)=\{P_C(x-tg)\}\subseteq C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent optimality characterizations of a projected-model point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex \(C\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), \(p=P_C(z)\) if and only if \(\langle z-p,y-p\rangle\le0\) for every \(y\in C\), equivalently \(z-p\in N_C(p)\). With \(z=x-tg\), this becomes \(0\in g+t^{-1}(p-x)+N_C(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-model point is certified by either a projection variational inequality or a normal-cone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p=P_C(x-tg)\iff0\in g+t^{-1}(p-x)+N_C(p).
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Variational-Inequality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-displacement test for projected affine models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex \(C\), \(x\in C\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(t>0\), \(x=P_C(x-tg)\) if and only if \(0\in g+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected affine model has zero displacement exactly at constrained first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=P_C(x-tg)\iff0\in g+N_C(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Fixed-Point Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the unique projected-model representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed nonconvex set \(C=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb R\), both points minimize \(|y|^2\) over \(C\), and hence \(P_C(0)=\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closedness without convexity does not make projection single-valued.

Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a nonempty closed feasible set, let \(x_0\in C\), and let \(m_{x_k}:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) model the objective at \(x_k\). For parameters \(t_k>0\), compute

Feasibility-Preserving Model Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which model-generated iterates remain feasible without restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq X\) be the feasible set and \(x_0\in C\). A model regime is feasibility-preserving if every accepted update is selected from an inner approximation \(C_k\) satisfying
\[
x_k\in C_k\subseteq C,
\qquad
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C_k}M_k(y).
\]
Provided each subproblem has a minimizer, induction gives \(x_k\in C\) for every \(k\). Exact constrained models use \(C_k=C\); conservative local models may use strict inner approximations. Outer approximations alone do not certify feasibility unless followed by a feasible restoration or projection step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility is preserved when every model subproblem is solved over an inner approximation of the feasible set containing the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: Each model subproblem attains an accepted minimizer in \(C_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in C\) for all \(k\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Euclidean Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic stabilization of a weakly convex local model in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(m_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous model based at \(x\), and suppose that \(m_x\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex for some \(\rho\geq0\). Fixed Euclidean stabilization chooses a parameter \(t>0\), held fixed across outer iterations, such that \(t^{-1}>\rho\), forms
\[\Phi_x^t(y)=m_x(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert y-x\rVert^2,\]
and selects
\[x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\Phi_x^t(y).\]
The stabilized objective is strongly convex and therefore has at most one minimizer; if \(\Phi_x^t\) is level-bounded, its minimizer exists and is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a fixed Euclidean quadratic proximity term whose curvature exceeds the model's weak-convexity modulus, and take the unique minimizer when the stabilized objective is level-bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(m_x\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex for some \(\rho\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\Phi_x^t(y)\) exists uniquely.
