knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniqueness or existence when Euclidean stabilization does not strictly dominate weak convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m_0(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(\rho>0\), and center \(x=0\), the stabilized objective is \[\frac12(t^{-1}-\rho)y^2.\] If \(t^{-1}=\rho\), every point is a minimizer; if \(t^{-1}<\rho\), the objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict curvature domination is sharp: equality can destroy uniqueness, while weaker stabilization can destroy existence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^{-1}\le\rho\text{ does not ensure a unique stabilized minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Curvature Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct comparison of the fixed stabilized step with its center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\in\operatorname{dom}m_x\) and \(x^+\) minimizes \(m_x(y)+(2t)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\), then \[m_x(x^+)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x^+-x\|^2\le m_x(x).\] Hence \(m_x(x^+)\le m_x(x)\); if \(m_x(x^+)\ge L\), then \[\|x^+-x\|\le\sqrt{2t\,[m_x(x)-L]}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblem optimality controls both model decrease and displacement from the fixed center.
assumptions_latex: The stabilized subproblem has a minimizer \(x^+\).

notation.meaning: a lower bound on the model value at the trial point

knowledge_statements.title: Center Comparison and Displacement Bound

children.title: Adaptive Proximal Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Model-responsive adjustment of proximity strength.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backtracking Can Fail without One-Sided Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent rejection when the model error is first order rather than quadratically controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x=0\), let \(f(y)=|y|\) and \(m(y)=-y\). For every \(t>0\), the exact minimizer of \(m(y)+y^2/(2t)\) is \(y_t=t\). The predicted decrease is \(m(0)-m(y_t)=t\), whereas the actual decrease is \(f(0)-f(y_t)=-t\). Thus \[f(0)-f(y_t)<\eta\bigl(m(0)-m(y_t)\bigr)\] for every \(\eta>0\) and every positive \(t\), so repeated contraction never produces an accepted nonzero trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a model underestimates the objective by a first-order error, arbitrarily strong proximal stabilization need not make an actual-versus-predicted reduction test pass.
assumptions_latex: The trial subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No positive trial stepsize satisfies the stated reduction test.

notation.meaning: trial point produced with stepsize t

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Can Fail without One-Sided Fidelity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Backtracking under One-Sided Quadratic Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination and contraction bound for an actual-versus-predicted reduction test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), \(f(y)\le m_k(y)+(\rho/2)\|y-x_k\|^2\), and that \(y_j\) minimizes \(m_k(y)+(2t_j)^{-1}\|y-x_k\|^2\) over a set containing \(x_k\). Let \(t_j=\beta^jt_0\), where \(0<\beta<1\), and accept when \[f(x_k)-f(y_j)\ge\eta\bigl(m_k(x_k)-m_k(y_j)\bigr),\qquad0<\eta<1.\] Every trial with \(\rho t_j\le1-\eta\) is accepted. If \(\rho>0\), termination occurs by an index \[j\le\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log((1-\eta)/(\rho t_0))}{\log\beta}\right\rceil\right\};\] if \(\rho=0\), the initial trial is accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided quadratic accuracy ensures that sufficiently strong proximal stabilization passes the reduction test, with a logarithmic bound on contractions.
assumptions_latex: Every trial subproblem has an exact minimizer and contains \(x_k\) as a feasible comparison point.
The one-sided estimate holds at every trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho t_j\le1-\eta\) implies acceptance and finite termination.
review_flags: This theorem concerns the explicit acceptance rule stated here; the immutable algorithm seed remains deferred as a family-wide convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Backtracking under One-Sided Quadratic Accuracy
Adaptive Proximal Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking adjustment of quadratic stabilization according to model acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), a model \(m_k\), trial parameter \(t_k^{(0)}>0\), contraction factor \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and acceptance constant \(\eta\in(0,1)\), repeat for \(j=0,1,\ldots\): compute
\[y_k^{(j)}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{m_k(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k^{(j)}}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\right\},\qquad t_k^{(j+1)}=\beta t_k^{(j)}\]
until the prescribed model-agreement test \(f(x_k)-f(y_k^{(j)})\geq\eta\bigl(m_k(x_k)-m_k(y_k^{(j)})\bigr)\) holds. Set \(x_{k+1}=y_k^{(j)}\) and retain the accepted \(t_k=t_k^{(j)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack the proximal stepsize until actual objective reduction is at least a fixed fraction of the model-predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: Each trial stabilized subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted step satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\eta\bigl(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_{k+1})\bigr)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the adaptive-stabilization leaf, but the particular actual-versus-model reduction test and the claim implicit in running backtracking require a source for this model family.

children.title: Variable-Metric Bregman Stabilization Family
children.top_down_role: Non-Euclidean or curvature-informed proximity geometries.

children.title: Variable-Metric Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Curvature-informed proximity geometries varying across model subproblems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity condition for a quadratic-metric model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_{k+1}\) minimizes \(m_k(y)+\tfrac12(y-x_k)^{\mathsf T}H_k(y-x_k)\) and the limiting-subdifferential sum rule applies, then \[0\in\partial m_k(x_{k+1})+H_k(x_{k+1}-x_k).\] If the stabilized objective is convex, this inclusion is also sufficient for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric-scaled displacement is a negative model subgradient and certifies the step in the convex regime.
assumptions_latex: For sufficiency, the stabilized objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -H_k(x_{k+1}-x_k)\in\partial m_k(x_{k+1}).
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Optimality Inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degenerating Metric Loses Uniform Proximity Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform norm equivalence when the smallest metric eigenvalue vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(H_k=1/k\), \(x_k=0\), and \(m_k(y)=-y\). The unique stabilized minimizer of \[-y+\frac{1}{2k}y^2\] is \(y_k=k\). Thus every \(H_k\) is positive definite, but \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\downarrow0\) and the displacement diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise positive definiteness does not provide uniform stabilization when the smallest eigenvalue can vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |y_k-x_k|=k\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerating Metric Loses Uniform Proximity Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable quadratic stabilization with an explicit metric convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a model \(m_k\), center \(x_k\), and symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H_k\), define \[\Phi_k(y)=m_k(y)+\frac12(y-x_k)^{\mathsf T}H_k(y-x_k).\] A variable-metric stabilized step is any \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\Phi_k(y)\) when the minimum is attained. Uniform metric control means that fixed constants \(0<\underline h\le\overline h<\infty\) satisfy \[\underline h I\preceq H_k\preceq\overline h I\quad\text{for all }k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilize each model with an iteration-dependent positive-definite quadratic norm; uniform spectral bounds keep these norms uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean norm.
assumptions_latex: Each stabilized objective attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\Phi_k(y).

notation.meaning: uniform lower and upper spectral bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Dependent Quadratic-Metric Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of one positive-definite quadratic subproblem to Euclidean coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H=L^{\mathsf T}L\succ0\) and \(z=L(y-x)\), then \[m(y)+\frac12\|y-x\|_H^2=m(x+L^{-1}z)+\frac12\|z\|^2.\] Thus each fixed positive-definite metric subproblem is a Euclidean stabilized subproblem in invertibly transformed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic metric is Euclidean stabilization after a linear change of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Coordinate Representation
Variable-Metric Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent quadratic stabilization under uniformly controlled positive-definite metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a model \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), base point \(x_k\), and symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H_k\), variable-metric stabilization forms
\[\Phi_k(y)=m_k(y)+\frac12\lVert y-x_k\rVert_{H_k}^2,\qquad \lVert v\rVert_{H_k}^2=v^{\mathsf T}H_kv,\]
and chooses \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\Phi_k(y)\). Uniform metric control means that constants \(0<\underline h\leq\overline h<\infty\) satisfy \(\underline h I\preceq H_k\preceq\overline h I\) for every \(k\), preventing degeneracy while allowing geometry to change between iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use an iteration-dependent positive-definite quadratic norm, uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean norm, to stabilize each model.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline h I\preceq H_k\preceq\overline h I\) uniformly in \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\Phi_k(y)\) is a well-defined variable-metric model step.

notation.meaning: quadratic norm induced by the metric

source_refs.locator: 3.3.2 Methods of Variable Metric and Methods of Conjugate Directions p. 78

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.2 Methods of Variable Metric and Methods of Conjugate Directions p. 78

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and notation fit variable-metric stabilization, but the cited generic variable-metric section does not yet provide inspectable support for stabilized weakly convex model subproblems or the stated uniform metric bounds.

children.title: Bregman Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Non-Euclidean proximity geometries induced by reference functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient certificate for a convex Bregman-stabilized subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be closed and convex, let \(m_x\) be proper closed convex, and suppose \(h\) is differentiable at \(x\) and \(x^+\). If the convex sum rule applies, then \(x^+\) minimizes \(m_x(y)+t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\) over \(C\) if and only if \[0\in\partial m_x(x^+)+t^{-1}(\nabla h(x^+)-\nabla h(x))+N_C(x^+).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model subgradient, the reference-gradient displacement, and a constraint normal must balance at the Bregman step.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is convex and differentiable at \(x\) and \(x^+\).
The convex subdifferential sum rule applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial m_x(x^+)+t^{-1}(\nabla h(x^+)-\nabla h(x))+N_C(x^+).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Bregman Optimality Inclusion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman stabilization under an explicit differentiability-domain convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\operatorname{dom}h\) be convex, let \(x\in C\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), and let \(h\) be proper, closed, strictly convex, and differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\). For \(y\in C\), define \[D_h(y,x)=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle.\] Given a model \(m_x\) and \(t>0\), a Bregman-stabilized step is any minimizer \[x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\{m_x(y)+t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\},\] whenever the minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a Bregman divergence whose center lies in the reference function's differentiability region to stabilize the model.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, strictly convex, and differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\).
The stabilized objective attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\{m_x(y)+t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\}.

notation.meaning: reference function generating the Bregman geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Center Bregman Model Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on metric reasoning and admissible centers for Bregman stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Bregman divergence need not be symmetric and need not satisfy the triangle inequality. If \(h\) is differentiable only on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), the gradient formula for \(D_h(y,x)\) is unavailable at a boundary center \(x\notin\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\). Thus metric arguments and arbitrary boundary centers require additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman divergence is generally not a distance, and its usual formula may be undefined at boundary centers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_h\text{ is generally nonmetric and requires }\nabla h(x)\text{ to exist}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonmetric and Boundary-Center Limitations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic comparison identity for differentiable Bregman geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever all displayed quantities are finite and \(h\) is differentiable at \(x\) and \(z\), \[D_h(y,x)-D_h(y,z)-D_h(z,x)=\langle\nabla h(z)-\nabla h(x),y-z\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A difference of three Bregman divergences equals a reference-gradient difference paired with a displacement.
assumptions_latex: All displayed divergence values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_h(y,x)-D_h(y,z)-D_h(z,x)=\langle\nabla h(z)-\nabla h(x),y-z\rangle.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Identity
Bregman Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonquadratic stabilization generated by a differentiable strongly convex reference function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strongly convex, and define
\[D_h(y,x)=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle.\]
For a model \(m_x:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and parameter \(t>0\), its Bregman-stabilized step is any
\[x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\left\{m_x(y)+t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\right\}.\]
The divergence is nonnegative and vanishes only at \(y=x\); hence it supplies proximity control adapted to the geometry generated by \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilize the model with a scaled Bregman divergence generated by a differentiable strongly convex reference function.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(C\).
The stabilized objective attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\{m_x(y)+t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Bregman-stabilization leaf, but no source supports the model step or specifies the differentiability/domain convention needed for the displayed divergence on a general convex set.

children.title: Metric-Geometry Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between stabilization geometry and local objective structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise Hessian test for relative weak convexity in a smooth common domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m_x\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable on an open convex set \(U\). Then \(m_x+\rho h\) is convex on \(U\) if and only if \[\nabla^2m_x(y)+\rho\nabla^2h(y)\succeq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in U.\] Thus this Hessian inequality is a checkable compatibility test in the smooth regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For twice-differentiable models and reference functions, compatibility is exactly a positive-semidefinite Hessian comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x+\rho h\text{ is convex on }U\iff\nabla^2m_x+\rho\nabla^2h\succeq0\text{ on }U.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Curvature Compatibility Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent compatibility stated through convexification by the reference function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex and let \(h:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex. A model \(m_x\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex relative to \(h\) on \(C\) when \[m_x+\rho h\quad\text{is convex on }C.\] If \(h\) is differentiable at the center \(x\) and the stabilization coefficient \(\alpha\) satisfies \(\alpha>\rho\), then \[m_x(y)+\alpha D_h(y,x)=(m_x(y)+\rho h(y))+(\alpha-\rho)h(y)-\alpha\langle\nabla h(x),y\rangle+\text{constant}.\] Consequently the stabilized objective is convex, and it is strictly convex when \(h\) is strictly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The geometry is compatible when adding rho times the reference function convexifies the model; any larger Bregman coefficient then dominates the negative curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is convex and differentiable at the center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x(\cdot)+\alpha D_h(\cdot,x)\text{ is convex, and is strictly convex if }h\text{ is strictly convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Weak-Convexity Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic relative-geometry example at and below the compatibility threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(y)=y^2/2\) and \(m(y)=-\rho y^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), with center zero. Then \[m(y)+\alpha D_h(y,0)=\frac12(\alpha-\rho)y^2.\] At \(\alpha=\rho\) strict convexity and uniqueness fail; for \(\alpha<\rho\) the stabilized objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilization coefficient must exceed the relative negative-curvature modulus to ensure strict convexity and well-posedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha\le\rho\text{ does not guarantee a unique minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Failure of Curvature Domination
Metric-Geometry Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility ensuring stabilization dominates model weak convexity in the chosen geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be convex, let \(h\) be differentiable on \(C\), and let \(m_x\) be a model. Metric-geometry compatibility with modulus \(\rho\geq0\) requires
\[m_x(y)\geq m_x(z)+\langle v,y-z\rangle-\rho D_h(y,z)\]
for all \(y,z\in C\) and every \(v\in\partial m_x(z)\). If the stabilized subproblem uses \(t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\), compatibility additionally requires \(t^{-1}>\rho\). Under these conditions, \(y\mapsto m_x(y)+t^{-1}D_h(y,x)\) is strongly convex relative to \(h\), so it has at most one minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The chosen divergence must dominate the model’s negative curvature; a stabilization coefficient strictly above the relative weak-convexity modulus ensures uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: \(D_h\) is generated by a differentiable strictly convex reference function on \(C\).
The displayed relative weak-convexity inequality holds with modulus \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_x(\cdot)+t^{-1}D_h(\cdot,x)\) is strongly convex relative to \(h\) and has at most one minimizer.

notation.meaning: convex or limiting subdifferential used by the model framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the compatibility leaf, but the relative weak-convexity inequality, the choice of subdifferential, and the relative-strong-convexity conclusion depend on conventions that are neither fixed nor sourced.

children.title: Model-Subproblem Solution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy and reuse regimes for stabilized model subproblems.

children.title: Exact Model-Subproblem Solves
children.top_down_role: Reference regime for separating outer-model and inner-solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Model-Subproblem Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference regime in which every stabilized model subproblem is globally minimized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(\Phi_k:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) denote the stabilized model objective on its feasible domain \(Y\). An exact model-subproblem solve returns \(y_k\in Y\) satisfying
\[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}\Phi_k(y),\qquad \Phi_k(y_k)=\inf_{y\in Y}\Phi_k(y).\]
Equivalently, the objective-value error \(\Phi_k(y_k)-\inf_Y\Phi_k\) is zero. When \(\Phi_k\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and strongly convex with an attained minimum, this point is unique and satisfies \(0\in\partial\Phi_k(y_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact inner solve returns a global minimizer of the stabilized model, with zero subproblem objective error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}\Phi_k(y)\) and its objective-value error is zero.

notation.meaning: stabilized model objective at iteration k

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Is Not an Exact-Solve Certificate for Nonconvex Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between global exactness and first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Phi(u)=(u^2-1)^2\), \(0=\Phi'(0)\), but \(\Phi(0)=1>0=\min_u\Phi(u)\). Thus \(0\in\partial\Phi(y)\) does not certify a global exact solve without convexity or another global-optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary point of a nonconvex model need not be its global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial\Phi(0)\not\Rightarrow0\in\operatorname*{argmin}\Phi.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Is Not an Exact-Solve Certificate for Nonconvex Models

children.title: Certified Inexact Model-Subproblem Solves
children.top_down_role: Inner solves controlled by model-quality or residual certificates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent certificates for a strongly convex model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with minimizer \(y^\star\). Either \[L\le\min\Phi,\quad \Phi(y)-L\le\varepsilon,\] or \[r\in\partial\Phi(y),\quad\|r\|\le\sqrt{2\mu\varepsilon}\] certifies \[\Phi(y)-\Phi(y^\star)\le\varepsilon.\] The gap certificate also gives \(\|y-y^\star\|\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon/\mu}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid lower-bound gap or a calibrated subgradient residual certifies objective accuracy; a certified gap also controls solution distance.
assumptions_latex: The stated lower bound or subgradient residual is verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(y)-\min\Phi\le\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: verified lower bound on the optimum

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Gap and Residual Inexactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent convex formulation of objective-gap inexactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex \(\Phi\) with attained minimum, \[\Phi(y)-\min_z\Phi(z)\le\varepsilon\iff0\in\partial_\varepsilon\Phi(y),\] where \[\partial_\varepsilon\Phi(y)=\{v:\Phi(z)\ge\Phi(y)+\langle v,z-y\rangle-\varepsilon\ \forall z\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex epsilon-optimality is exactly zero membership in the epsilon-subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(y)-\min\Phi\le\varepsilon\iff0\in\partial_\varepsilon\Phi(y).
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Subdifferential Characterization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Tolerance Without Curvature Does Not Control the Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual-only objective certification without an error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Phi(u)=\tau|u|\) with \(\tau>0\), every \(y>0\) admits \(r=\tau\in\partial\Phi(y)\), while \[\Phi(y)-\min\Phi=\tau y\to+\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded absolute subgradient residual need not bound objective error without curvature or another error-bound condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r\|=\tau\quad\text{while}\quad\Phi(y)-\min\Phi\to+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Tolerance Without Curvature Does Not Control the Gap
Certified Inexact Model-Subproblem Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable objective-gap or first-order residual control for an approximate inner solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_k\) be a proper closed \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex stabilized model with minimizer \(y_k^\star\). A candidate \(y_k\) is a certified \(\varepsilon_k\)-inexact solve if it is accompanied by either a verified gap bound
\[\Phi_k(y_k)-L_k\leq\varepsilon_k,\qquad L_k\leq\inf_y\Phi_k(y),\]
or a residual \(r_k\in\partial\Phi_k(y_k)\) satisfying \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\sqrt{2\mu_k\varepsilon_k}\). The gap certificate directly implies \(\Phi_k(y_k)-\Phi_k(y_k^\star)\leq\varepsilon_k\); the residual certificate implies the same bound by strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate inner solution is certified by a computable lower-bound gap or a sufficiently small subgradient residual.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a verified lower bound, or \(r_k\in\partial\Phi_k(y_k)\) is computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_k(y_k)-\min_y\Phi_k(y)\leq\varepsilon_k\).

notation.meaning: verified lower bound on the subproblem optimum

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate and the two alternatives are mathematically coherent under strong convexity, but no source supports the residual-to-objective-gap constant or this combined certificate formulation.

children.title: Model-Solve State-Reuse Methods
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solver state across neighboring model subproblems.

children.title: Warm-Started Model Solves
children.top_down_role: Initialization of a model subproblem from a neighboring solve.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal initialization of each model solve from a neighboring solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi_k\) be the current model subproblem and \(y_{k-1}\) the preceding accepted inner solution. Choose a transport \(T_k\) into the current solver domain, initialize \(z_{k,0}=T_k(y_{k-1})\), run the current inner iteration, and output the first iterate satisfying the current exact or inexact subproblem certificate. If the domains coincide, the canonical transport is \(T_k(y)=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm-started solve uses the preceding primal solution as the current initializer, after any required feasibility transport, and then certifies the current solve.
assumptions_latex: \(T_k(y_{k-1})\) is admissible for the current inner solver.
A current-subproblem stopping certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The accepted output satisfies the current subproblem certificate.}

notation.meaning: transport into the current solver domain

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started Model Solves

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Warm Starting Alone Gives No Speedup Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility and performance boundary of primal-only reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The preceding solution may be infeasible for the current domain or arbitrarily far from the current solution after a substantial model change. Without a sensitivity bound and an inner-solver rate, primal warm initialization alone guarantees neither fewer inner iterations nor convergence from that initializer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previous solution is only an initializer; model changes can make it infeasible or no better than a cold start.
assumptions_latex: Consecutive model subproblems may have different domains or solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Warm initialization alone does not imply feasibility, convergence, or an iteration saving.}
knowledge_statements.title: Warm Starting Alone Gives No Speedup Guarantee

children.title: Recycled Model Solves
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solver state, factorizations, or active information across subproblems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of auxiliary solver state beyond a primal warm start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_{k-1}\) contain a terminal primal candidate and auxiliary state such as an active set, factorization, bundle, dual estimate, or preconditioner. Before solving the current model, apply a transfer-and-validation map \(R_k\) to obtain an admissible state \(s_{k,0}=R_k(s_{k-1})\); discard or repair components that fail current-model validity tests. Iterate the current solver and accept its primal output only after the current subproblem certificate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recycled solve transfers validated auxiliary solver state, repairs or discards stale components, and recertifies the current subproblem.
assumptions_latex: Transferred components have current-model admissibility or validity tests.
The inner solver accepts admissible transferred state.
The stopping test certifies the current subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The output is accepted only after satisfying the current-model certificate.}

notation.meaning: initial full state for the current inner solve
state transfer, validation, and repair map

knowledge_statements.title: Recycled Model Solves

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-model recertification boundary for recycled state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Validity or optimality of \(s_{k-1}\) for subproblem \(k-1\) does not imply validity or optimality for subproblem \(k\). In particular, a changed constraint or model piece can invalidate a previously active set or dual multiplier. Therefore state reuse alone supplies neither a current-solve certificate nor a universal iteration saving.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Previously valid auxiliary state can become stale after the model changes, so recycling never replaces current-model validation and certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Previous-state validity}\not\Rightarrow\text{current-state validity or optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Recycling Does Not Transfer Optimality

children.title: Solver-State Transfer Reliability
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting reliable reuse after substantial model changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient invariant-region and contraction conditions for reliable reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k^\star\) be a current solution state. Suppose the transferred state satisfies \(\|R_k(s_{k-1})-s_k^\star\|\le R\), and the current iteration map satisfies \[\|S_k(s)-s_k^\star\|\le q\|s-s_k^\star\|\quad\text{whenever }\|s-s_k^\star\|\le R,\] for some \(q\in[0,1)\). Then the transferred iterations remain in the reliability region and satisfy \[\|s_{k,j}-s_k^\star\|\le q^jR.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer is locally reliable when it lands in an invariant region where the current solver contracts.
assumptions_latex: The transferred state is admissible for the current solver.
The transfer lands within radius \(R\) of a current solution state.
The current iteration is \(q\)-contractive on that region, with \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|s_{k,j}-s_k^\star\|\le q^jR.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Reliability of Solver-State Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of conclusions based on local transfer reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a transferred state is inadmissible, lies outside the current solver's invariant attraction region, or contains components invalid for the changed model, the local contraction estimate gives no conclusion. A current-subproblem certificate must still be checked even when transfer is locally contractive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large model changes or stale auxiliary state can place a transferred solve outside its reliability regime, and contraction never replaces current certification.
assumptions_latex: The available solver guarantee is local.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Failure of admissibility or region membership precludes the local reliability conclusion.}
knowledge_statements.title: Transfer Outside the Validity Region
Solver-State Transfer Reliability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient contraction and admissibility conditions for reliable transferred inner states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_k^\star\) be a solution state for the current subproblem, let \(R_k\) transfer the preceding terminal state, and let \(S_k\) be the current inner iteration. Transfer is reliable on radius \(R>0\) if constants \(q\in[0,1)\) and \(R>0\), independent of \(k\), satisfy
\[\lVert R_k(s_{k-1})-s_k^\star\rVert\leq R,\qquad \lVert S_k(s)-s_k^\star\rVert\leq q\lVert s-s_k^\star\rVert\]
whenever \(\lVert s-s_k^\star\rVert\leq R\). Then transferred iterations remain in the reliability region and obey \(\lVert s_{k,j}-s_k^\star\rVert\leq q^jR\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred state is reliable when it is admissible and lies in a uniform region where the current inner solver contracts.
assumptions_latex: The transferred state lies within radius \(R\) of a current solution state.
The current solver is uniformly \(q\)-contractive on that radius, with \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert s_{k,j}-s_k^\star\rVert\leq q^jR\), so the recycled inner iteration converges geometrically.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the reliability leaf and its contraction conclusion is internally consistent, but no source supports this particular uniform-radius definition for transferred solver states.

children.title: Weakly Convex Descent Certificate

children.title: Model-Decrement Certificates
children.top_down_role: Progress indicators obtained from stabilized model improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Decrement Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable progress certificate from reduction of the stabilized local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a base point \(x\), model \(m_x\), and parameter \(t>0\), define \(\Phi_x^t(y)=m_x(y)+(2t)^{-1}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\). If \(m_x(x)=f(x)\) and a trial point \(y\) satisfies the model-majorization test \(f(y)\leq m_x(y)\), then the stabilized model decrement
\[\Delta_t(x;y)=\Phi_x^t(x)-\Phi_x^t(y)\]
is directly computable. Whenever \(\Delta_t(x;y)>0\), it certifies
\[f(x)-f(y)\geq\Delta_t(x;y)+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert y-x\rVert^2>0.\]
Thus positive stabilized-model improvement verifies actual objective descent under the stated model test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive stabilized-model decrement certifies actual descent when the model matches the objective at the base point and majorizes it at the trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(y)\geq\Delta_t(x;y)+(2t)^{-1}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\).

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

children.title: Proximal-Displacement Certificates
children.top_down_role: Stationarity indicators based on stabilized-model displacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Displacement Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-stationarity certificate obtained from the displacement of an exact stabilized-model minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower-semicontinuous, and let
\[y_t=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{m_x(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\},\qquad G_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-y_t).\]
Exact subproblem optimality gives \(G_t(x)\in\partial m_x(y_t)\). Hence \(\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-small model subgradient at the nearby point \(y_t\), while \(G_t(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(y_t=x\) and implies \(0\in\partial m_x(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled displacement to the stabilized-model minimizer is a model subgradient; its norm therefore gives a computable model-stationarity certificate.
assumptions_latex: The stabilized model has an exact minimizer \(y_t\).
The limiting-subdifferential sum rule applies at \(y_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_t(x)\in\partial m_x(y_t)\), and \(\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) certifies model stationarity within tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

children.title: Model-Optimality Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual indicators supplied by the model subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Optimality Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable subgradient residual certifies accuracy of a strongly convex regularized model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi_x(z)=m_x(z)+(2t)^{-1}\|z-x\|^2\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, with unique minimizer \(z_x\). For a trial point \(y\in\operatorname{dom}\phi_x\), choose \(q\in\partial m_x(y)+t^{-1}(y-x)=\partial\phi_x(y)\). Then \(\|q\|\) is a verifiable model-optimality residual and
\[
\|y-z_x\|\leq \mu^{-1}\|q\|,
\qquad
0\leq \phi_x(y)-\phi_x(z_x)\leq (2\mu)^{-1}\|q\|^2.
\]
Thus \(\|q\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies both \(\varepsilon/\mu\)-solution accuracy and \(\varepsilon^2/(2\mu)\)-subproblem objective accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small subgradient residual of a strongly convex regularized model bounds both distance to the exact model step and model-subproblem objective error.

notation.meaning: exact minimizer of the regularized model

review_flags: Exact strongly-convex residual certificate needs a directly supporting theorem locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically coherent and the content kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for the strongly convex residual-to-distance and residual-to-objective-gap bounds.

children.title: Envelope-Gradient Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measured through the smooth implicit regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Gradient Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity is measured by the gradient of a differentiable Moreau envelope of a weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with the upper bound omitted when \(\rho=0\). Define
\[
f_\lambda(x)=\min_y\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\},
\qquad p_\lambda(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x).
\]
The envelope is continuously differentiable and \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-p_\lambda(x))\). A point \(x\) is envelope-gradient \(\varepsilon\)-stationary when \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Envelope stationarity is the norm of the Moreau-envelope gradient, equivalently the proximal displacement divided by the regularization parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|=\lambda^{-1}\|x-p_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Nearby-Point Stationarity Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer from envelope stationarity to the original objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Point Stationarity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A small envelope gradient produces an equally stationary point of the original objective at controlled distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the weak-convexity and parameter assumptions for the Moreau envelope, set \(p=p_\lambda(x)\) and \(v=\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\). Proximal optimality gives
\[
v\in\partial f(p),
\qquad v=\nabla f_\lambda(x),
\qquad \|x-p\|=\lambda\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|.
\]
Consequently, if \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\), then the nearby point \(p\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p))\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|p-x\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An envelope-stationary point has a nearby proximal point whose original subdifferential stationarity is no worse, with distance proportional to the envelope gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p_\lambda(x)))\leq\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\) and \(\|p_\lambda(x)-x\|=\lambda\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\).

notation.meaning: transferred subgradient at the proximal point

children.title: Envelope Descent Accounting
children.top_down_role: Progress accounting underlying deterministic convergence and complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Descent Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-step envelope decrease inequality telescopes into a global bound on squared stationarity measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an iteration sequence satisfy
\[
f_\lambda(x_{k+1})\leq f_\lambda(x_k)-c\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|^2+e_k
\]
for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), where \(c>0\) and \(e_k\geq0\). If \(f_\lambda^\star=\inf_x f_\lambda(x)>-\infty\), then telescoping yields
\[
c\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|^2
\leq f_\lambda(x_0)-f_\lambda^\star+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k.
\]
Hence the smallest squared envelope-gradient norm among the first \(N\) iterates is at most the right-hand side divided by \(cN\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing per-iteration envelope descent bounds the cumulative squared stationarity and therefore the best stationarity achieved within a finite run.
assumptions_latex: The displayed one-step descent inequality holds for every indexed iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\leq k<N}\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|^2\leq [f_\lambda(x_0)-f_\lambda^\star+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k]/(cN)\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative descent error at iteration k

review_flags: Telescoping statement is standard but no supplied locator states this deterministic envelope-descent accounting result.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping accounting is mathematically correct and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable source locator for this nontrivial convergence statement.

children.title: Model-to-Proximal Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Translation between model residuals and proximal displacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-to-Proximal Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An approximate proximal optimality residual converts a model step into a bound on exact proximal displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be proper, closed, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, let \(0<t<1/\rho\), and put \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{tf}(x)\). Suppose a model step \(y\) supplies a vector
\[
e\in\partial f(y)+t^{-1}(y-x).
\]
Strong monotonicity of \(z\mapsto\partial f(z)+t^{-1}(z-x)\) gives
\[
\|y-p\|\leq\frac{\|e\|}{t^{-1}-\rho},
\qquad
\frac{\|x-p\|}{t}\leq\frac{\|x-y\|}{t}+\frac{\|e\|}{1-\rho t}.
\]
Thus model displacement and consistency residual jointly bound the exact proximal stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model step with small displacement and small original-objective optimality residual guarantees a small exact proximal displacement.
review_flags: Direct support for the displayed residual-to-proximal constants should be checked.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed inequalities concern an approximate optimality residual for the original proximal subproblem, since e belongs to the original-objective inclusion. No model function or hypothesis translating a model residual into that inclusion is given. Calling y a model step does not establish the model-to-proximal translation required by this leaf, and repairing it would require substantive model-accuracy assumptions rather than a local wording change.

children.title: Proximal-to-Subdifferential Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Translation from regularized points to generalized criticality.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-to-Subdifferential Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The proximal displacement is an explicit limiting subgradient at the associated regularized point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), and set \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). Fermat's rule for the proximal subproblem gives
\[
\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\in\partial f(p).
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p))
\leq \lambda^{-1}\|x-p\|.
\]
In particular, vanishing proximal displacement implies generalized criticality at \(p\), while an \(\varepsilon\)-small normalized displacement certifies \(\varepsilon\)-subdifferential stationarity there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized displacement from a point to its proximal point is a subgradient of the original objective at that proximal point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\in\partial f(p)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p))\leq\lambda^{-1}\|x-p\|\).

children.title: Composite Stationarity Translations
children.top_down_role: Stationarity interfaces specialized to composite models.

assumptions_latex: \(t>0\), and \(y\) is an exact minimizer of the displayed prox-linear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(0\in\partial g(y)+
abla c(x)^*\partial h(c(x)+
abla c(x)(y-x))+t^{-1}(y-x)\), so \(t^{-1}(x-y)\in\partial g(y)+
abla c(x)^*\partial h(c(x)+
abla c(x)(y-x))\).

notation.meaning: adjoint Jacobian of c at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite criticality and exact prox-linear model optimality are expressed through compatible subgradient inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be given by \(F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\), where \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and Lipschitz, \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable, and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. Composite stationarity is represented by
\[
0\in \partial g(x)+\nabla c(x)^*\partial h(c(x)).
\]
For \(t>0\), suppose \(y\) exactly minimizes the prox-linear model
\[
z\mapsto h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(z-x))+g(z)+\frac{1}{2t}\|z-x\|^2.
\]
Then exact model optimality gives
\[
0\in\partial g(y)+\nabla c(x)^*\partial h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+t^{-1}(y-x).
\]
Equivalently, \(t^{-1}(x-y)\) belongs to the sum of the linearized composite and regularizer subdifferentials at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite stationarity uses the composite chain-rule inclusion. An exact prox-linear step satisfies the corresponding linearized inclusion, with its normalized displacement represented by the model subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Stationarity Translations

children.title: Deterministic Weakly Convex Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity classifications by model family, target certificate, and geometric growth regime.

children.title: Baseline Stationarity Complexity
children.top_down_role: General complexity for regularized first-order stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Baseline Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform envelope descent yields the baseline deterministic inverse-square iteration complexity for regularized stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a deterministic method generates \(x_0,x_1,\ldots\) satisfying
\[
f_\lambda(x_{k+1})\leq f_\lambda(x_k)-c\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|^2
\]
with \(c>0\), and let \(\Delta=f_\lambda(x_0)-\inf f_\lambda<\infty\). After \(N\geq1\) iterations,
\[
\min_{0\leq k<N}\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|
\leq\sqrt{\frac{\Delta}{cN}}.
\]
Consequently, at most \(\lceil\Delta/(c\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) iterations are sufficient to produce an iterate with envelope-gradient norm at most \(\varepsilon\). This is an \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer-iteration bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform decrease proportional to squared envelope-gradient norm gives an inverse-square deterministic iteration bound for finding a regularized stationary point.
assumptions_latex: The stated descent inequality holds with a uniform \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\geq\Delta/(c\varepsilon^2)\) guarantees \(\min_{0\leq k<N}\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the deterministic weakly convex envelope complexity theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-square bound follows correctly from the assumed uniform envelope descent, and complexity_bound is the correct content kind. No source locator is supplied for the deterministic weakly convex complexity result.

children.title: Prox-Linear Composite Complexity Family
children.top_down_role: Complexity specialized to structured composite models.

children.title: Prox-Linear Complexity
children.top_down_role: Deterministic complexity regimes specialized to prox-linear models.

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact prox-linear steps inherit inverse-square outer complexity from a sufficient-decrease inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=h\circ c+g\), let \(x_{k+1}\) be an exact prox-linear step of parameter \(t>0\), and define \(G_t(x_k)=t^{-1}(x_k-x_{k+1})\). Suppose
\[
F(x_{k+1})\leq F(x_k)-a\|G_t(x_k)\|^2
\]
for a uniform \(a>0\), and let \(\Delta_F=F(x_0)-\inf F<\infty\). Then
\[
\min_{0\leq k<N}\|G_t(x_k)\|
\leq\sqrt{\frac{\Delta_F}{aN}}.
\]
Thus \(N=\lceil\Delta_F/(a\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) exact convex model solves suffice to obtain \(\|G_t(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under uniform sufficient decrease, exact prox-linear iterations require order inverse-square model solves to obtain a small prox-linear gradient mapping.
assumptions_latex: Each outer iteration exactly solves its prox-linear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(\lceil\Delta_F/(a\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) exact prox-linear subproblem solves produce \(\|G_t\|\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: A prox-linear theorem locator is needed to instantiate the decrease coefficient from standard smoothness parameters.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional telescoping complexity bound is correct and belongs in this complexity leaf, but no prox-linear theorem source is supplied to support the sufficient-decrease premise or its standard parameter regime.

children.title: Composite-Model Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes for structured outer-inner model compositions.

assumptions_latex: For every \(k\), \(t_k>0\), and the displayed regularized convex-composite model has an exact minimizer \(y_k\).
The uniform sufficient-decrease inequality holds with \(a>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\leq k<N}\|R_k\|\leq\sqrt{[F(x_0)-F_\star]/(aN)}\); hence \(N\geq[F(x_0)-F_\star]/(a\varepsilon^2)\) guarantees an index \(k<N\) with \(\|R_k\|\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: lower bound on the objective values
convex-composite model used at iteration k

review_flags: A theorem source specifying the composite model class and sufficient-decrease coefficient is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform descent by squared displacement controls the best residual generated by exact regularized convex-composite model solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and for each \(k\geq0\) let \(M_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper, closed, convex composite model centered at \(x_k\). Choose \(t_k>0\), let
\[
y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{M_k(z)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|z-x_k\|^2\right\},
\qquad x_{k+1}=y_k,
\qquad R_k=t_k^{-1}(x_k-y_k).
\]
Assume constants \(a>0\) and \(F_\star>-infty\) satisfy
\[
F(x_{k+1})\leq F(x_k)-a\|R_k\|^2,
\qquad F(x_k)\geq F_\star
\]
for every \(k\geq0\). Then, for every integer \(N\geq1\),
\[
\min_{0\leq k<N}\|R_k\|
\leq\sqrt{\frac{F(x_0)-F_\star}{aN}}.
\]
Consequently, \(N\geq[F(x_0)-F_\star]/(a\varepsilon^2)\) guarantees an index \(k<N\) with \(\|R_k\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact regularized convex-composite model steps, a uniform objective decrease proportional to squared normalized displacement yields inverse-square outer complexity for that displacement residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Model Complexity

children.title: Structure-Dependent Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Information costs shaped by the selected composite representation.

assumptions_latex: The outer method terminates after at most \(N(\varepsilon)\) iterations with residual at most \(\varepsilon\).
Each outer iteration uses at most \(S\) structural-oracle calls.
Iteration \(k\) uses at most \(Q_k(\delta_k)\) additional primitive oracle calls to solve its model to tolerance \(\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total primitive-call count is at most \(S N(\varepsilon)+\sum_{k=0}^{N(\varepsilon)-1}Q_k(\delta_k)\); if \(N(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{-2}\) and \(Q_k(\delta_k)\leq Q(\varepsilon)\), it is at most \(C\varepsilon^{-2}[S+Q(\varepsilon)]\).

notation.meaning: additional primitive cost of the kth model solve
maximum structural-oracle calls per outer iteration

review_flags: A source is required for any concrete structure-dependent inner oracle bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive oracle cost combines outer model complexity with structural evaluations and the structure-specific cost of each model solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an outer model method terminates after at most \(N(\varepsilon)\) iterations with residual at most \(\varepsilon\). Assume each outer iteration uses at most \(S\geq0\) structural-oracle calls, and iteration \(k\) uses at most \(Q_k(\delta_k)\geq0\) additional primitive oracle calls to solve its model to tolerance \(\delta_k\). Then the total number of primitive oracle calls is at most
\[
S N(\varepsilon)+\sum_{k=0}^{N(\varepsilon)-1}Q_k(\delta_k).
\]
If \(N(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{-2}\) and \(Q_k(\delta_k)\leq Q(\varepsilon)\) for all completed iterations, then the total is at most
\[
C\varepsilon^{-2}[S+Q(\varepsilon)].
\]
Thus an outer iteration bound does not by itself determine the structure-dependent primitive oracle complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total primitive oracle complexity is the structural-oracle cost of the outer iterations plus the additional primitive cost of their model solves.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Dependent Oracle Complexity

children.title: Inexact-Model Complexity
children.top_down_role: Outer complexity coupled with model and subproblem accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Model Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable model and subproblem errors enlarge the baseline stationarity bound by their accumulated descent loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose inexact model steps satisfy
\[
f_\lambda(x_{k+1})\leq f_\lambda(x_k)-c\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|^2+e_k,
\qquad e_k\geq0,
\]
where \(e_k\) aggregates model and subproblem inaccuracies. With \(\Delta=f_\lambda(x_0)-\inf f_\lambda<\infty\),
\[
\min_{0\leq k<N}\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|^2
\leq\frac{\Delta+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k}{cN}.
\]
If \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k\leq E\) uniformly, then \(N\geq(\Delta+E)/(c\varepsilon^2)\) suffices for envelope-gradient norm at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulated model and subproblem errors add to the initial envelope gap; bounded total error preserves inverse-square outer stationarity complexity.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inexact descent inequality holds with \(c>0\) and \(e_k\geq0\).
The accumulated error is bounded by \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\geq(\Delta+E)/(c\varepsilon^2)\) guarantees some \(k<N\) with \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: combined model and subproblem descent error

review_flags: A source is needed that derives the inexact descent error from explicit model and subproblem accuracy conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional telescoping inequality is correct and the content kind fits. However, the record does not provide a source or explicit conditions connecting model and subproblem accuracy to the descent-error sequence, which is the substantive inexact-model claim of this leaf.

children.title: Sharpness-Based Local-Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Improved local regimes associated with sharpness and error bounds.

children.title: Growth-Based Local Rates
children.top_down_role: Improved local behavior associated with objective growth near solution sets.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) has finite minimum \(F_*\) and nonempty minimizer set \(X_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=2\) gives a linear objective-gap rate, while \(p>2\) gives \(F(x_k)-F_*=O(k^{-p/(p-2)})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional local rates obtained by combining growth with a model-method gap recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_k:=F(x_k)-F_*\). Suppose that, after entry into a neighborhood of \(X_*\), the model method satisfies \(e_{k+1}\le e_k-ce_k^{2-2/p}\). For quadratic growth, \(p=2\), this becomes \(e_{k+1}\le(1-c)e_k\), provided \(0<c<1\), and hence \(e_k\le(1-c)^{k-k_0}e_{k_0}\). If \(p>2\), then the standard scalar-recursion estimate gives \[e_k=O\!\left(k^{-p/(p-2)}\right).\] The growth inequality additionally yields \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X_*)\le(e_k/\mu)^{1/p}\). For \(1\le p<2\), the displayed recursion cannot persist with positive gaps arbitrarily near zero; it therefore entails finite termination once the recursion is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth inequality converts the method's local gap recursion into linear convergence for quadratic growth and a polynomial rate for higher growth powers.
knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Based Local Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar-recursion calculations are plausible, including the polynomial exponent and the finite-termination implication for 1<=p<2, but no inspectable source supports the model-method recursion or its connection to the stated growth condition. The plain statement also omits the distance-rate and finite-termination conclusions.

children.title: Error-Bound Local Rates
children.top_down_role: Improved local behavior associated with residual-to-solution distance control.

assumptions_latex: Near \(X_*\), the update map \(T\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(T(x),X_*)\le aR(x)\) and \(R(x)\le b\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(ab<1\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_{k+1},X_*)\le ab\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X_*)\) locally.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric error bound combined with a local residual-to-step contraction estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the local error bound \(R(x)\le b\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)\) and the update estimate \(\operatorname{dist}(T(x),X_*)\le aR(x)\) hold throughout a neighborhood \(U\) of \(X_*\). If \(q:=ab<1\) and the iterates \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) remain in \(U\), then \[\operatorname{dist}(x_{k+1},X_*)\le q\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X_*).\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X_*)\le q^{k-k_0}\operatorname{dist}(x_{k_0},X_*)\) after entry at index \(k_0\). If additionally \(R(x)\le b\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)\) remains valid along the sequence, then \(R(x_k)\le bq^{k-k_0}\operatorname{dist}(x_{k_0},X_*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error bound and a sufficiently strong residual-to-update estimate yield local linear convergence in distance and residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Local Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed contraction follows algebraically from the two assumed inequalities, but the inequality called an error bound has the residual-to-distance orientation R(x)<=b dist(x,X_*), whereas standard metric error bounds commonly use the reverse control. A source is required to establish that this is the intended local error-bound regime for the model-method family.

children.title: Sharpness-Driven Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local acceleration regimes arising from sharp objective geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex for some \(\rho\ge0\).
The minimum \(F_*:=\min F\) is finite, the set \(X_*:=\operatorname*{argmin}F\) is nonempty, and \(F(y)-F_*\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(y,X_*)\) for every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)<\lambda\mu\), then \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda F}(x)\in X_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-step proximal capture under a sharp global growth inequality; genuinely local variants must specify a neighborhood containing every possible proximal comparison point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(x^+:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda F}(x)\) be the unique minimizer of \(y\mapsto F(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\). If \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)<\lambda\mu\), then \(x^+\in X_*\). Hence an exact proximal iteration reaches the minimizer set in one further step whenever its current iterate lies in the open tube \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)<\lambda\mu\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under global linear sharpness, an exact proximal step maps every point whose distance to the minimizer set is less than lambda times the sharpness constant directly into that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness-Driven Rate Regimes

children.title: Nonconvex Cutting-Plane Model Families
children.top_down_role: Affine and convexified models adapted to the loss of global supporting-hyperplane validity.

children.title: Localized Affine-Cut Models
children.top_down_role: Affine information accompanied by locality control.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz near a sampling point \(z\).
\(g\in\partial f(z)\) is supplied by a generalized-gradient oracle.
A locality radius \(r>0\) and error allowance \(\varepsilon_z(r)\ge0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut \(a_z\) is certified only on \(B(z,r)\), with error controlled by \(\varepsilon_z(r)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition using a ball-restricted affine approximation and explicit overestimation allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A localized affine-cut model at \(z\) consists of the affine function \[a_z(x):=f(z)+\langle g,x-z\rangle\] together with a radius \(r>0\) and a bound \(\varepsilon_z(r)\ge0\) such that \(a_z(x)\le f(x)+\varepsilon_z(r)\) for every \(x\in B(z,r)\). The triple \((a_z,r,\varepsilon_z(r))\), rather than \(a_z\) alone, is the cut. A bundle model on a common localization set \(D\subseteq\bigcap_{z\in\mathcal B}B(z,r_z)\) is \(m(x):=\max_{z\in\mathcal B}a_z(x)\); its certified error on \(D\) is bounded by \(\max_{z\in\mathcal B}\varepsilon_z(r_z)\). No validity is asserted outside the recorded localization sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localized affine cut carries both an affine oracle approximation and a region on which its overestimation error is controlled.
knowledge_statements.title: Localized Affine-Cut Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed triple is mathematically coherent, but no source establishes this locality-radius and additive-overestimation convention as the intended localized affine-cut model in the immutable nonconvex bundle context.

children.title: Downshifted-Cut Models
children.top_down_role: Adjusted cuts designed to control nonconvex overestimation.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a sample \(z\), and an oracle vector \(g\) are given.
\(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty compact localization set.
The supremum defining the downshift is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The shifted cut satisfies \(a_z^{\downarrow}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).

notation.meaning: smallest nonnegative valid downshift on D

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal downward adjustment making an affine oracle cut valid on a localization set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the raw affine cut by \(a_z(x):=f(z)+\langle g,x-z\rangle\). Its minimal nonnegative downshift over \(D\) is \[\delta_z(D):=\max\left\{0,\sup_{x\in D}\bigl(a_z(x)-f(x)\bigr)\right\}.\] The associated downshifted cut is \(a_z^{\downarrow}(x):=a_z(x)-\delta_z(D)\). It satisfies \(a_z^{\downarrow}(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in D\), and no smaller nonnegative constant shift has this property. A downshifted bundle model is \(m_D(x):=\max_{z\in\mathcal B}a_z^{\downarrow}(x)\) on a set where every constituent cut has been certified. The construction controls nonconvex overestimation at the cost of losing exactness at sampled points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A downshift subtracts the smallest nonnegative constant needed to make an affine cut underestimate the objective on the current localization set.
knowledge_statements.title: Downshifted-Cut Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supremum construction does produce the smallest constant shift giving a minorant on D, but no source shows that this global-on-D construction is the downshifted-cut model intended by the taxonomy. Established bundle downshift conventions may instead be tied to a serious iterate or oracle-specific correction.

children.title: Redistributed Convexified Models
children.top_down_role: Bundle models representing an adaptive local convexification.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A Redistributed Proximal Bundle Method for Nonconvex Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A Redistributed Proximal Bundle Method for Nonconvex Optimization

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex on a convex localization set \(D\).
A center \(\bar x\in D\) and convexification parameter \(\gamma\ge\rho\) are fixed.
Affine minorants of the convexified function are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Subtracting the common quadratic redistributes a convex cutting-plane model back to a model of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation by cutting planes of a local convexification with the quadratic term subsequently removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(h_{\bar x,\gamma}(x):=f(x)+(\gamma/2)\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\) on \(D\). Because \(\gamma\ge\rho\), this function is convex on \(D\). For sample points \(z_i\in D\) and subgradients \(s_i\in\partial h_{\bar x,\gamma}(z_i)\), define \(q_i(x):=h_{\bar x,\gamma}(z_i)+\langle s_i,x-z_i\rangle\). The redistributed convexified model of \(f\) is \[m(x):=\max_i q_i(x)-\frac{\gamma}{2}\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2.\] On \(D\), each \(q_i\le h_{\bar x,\gamma}\), hence \(m
i x\mapsto m(x)\le f(x)\). Updating \(\bar x\), \(\gamma\), or the cuts adapts the local convexification without changing this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cutting planes model a locally convexified objective; removing their shared quadratic term produces a bundle model of the original weakly convex function.
knowledge_statements.title: Redistributed Convexified Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convexification identity is plausible, but the specific redistributed-model terminology and assumptions lack a source. The phrase \(m\ni x\mapsto m(x)\le f(x)\) is malformed and must be repaired once the sourced convention is established.

children.top_down_role: Convex local models assembled from cutting-plane oracles under explicit model-trust rules.

children.title: Standard Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Canonical generalized-gradient models used when their local regularity is adequate.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz on an open set \(U\).
At every \(z\in U\), the oracle returns \(f(z)\) and \(g_z\in\partial f(z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical oracle model is \(M(y;z)=f(z)+\langle g_z,y-z\rangle\), exact at \(y=z\).

notation.meaning: generalized subdifferential used by the oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical affine generalized-gradient model, without a strengthened strict approximation requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard first-order oracle model based at \(z\in U\) is obtained from an oracle response \((f(z),g_z)\), where \(g_z\in\partial f(z)\), by setting \[M(y;z):=f(z)+\langle g_z,y-z\rangle.\] It is exact at its base point because \(M(z;z)=f(z)\), and its directional information is \(M'(z;z;d)=\langle g_z,d\rangle\). For a finite bundle \(\mathcal B\), the associated polyhedral model is \(M_{\mathcal B}(y):=\max_{z\in\mathcal B}M(y;z)\). In the nonconvex setting neither a global lower-model inequality nor a strict two-point approximation property follows from this definition; any such property must be imposed separately or enforced by localization or correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard oracle model is the affine function formed from a sampled value and generalized gradient; nonconvex validity requires additional controls.
knowledge_statements.title: Standard Oracle Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a nonconvex locally Lipschitz function, the meaning of \(\partial f\) must be fixed, and an arbitrary generalized subgradient affine function is not automatically the standard oracle model under every bundle framework. A source is needed for the exact oracle and model convention.

children.title: Strict Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Model families with strengthened sequential approximation behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strictness means the positive modeling error is uniformly \(o(\lVert y-x\rVert)\) as both arguments approach \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential upper-approximation form of strict first-order model consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The oracle model \(M\) is strict at \(\bar x\) if it is exact on the diagonal and, for every pair of sequences \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(y_k\to\bar x\) with \(x_k\ne y_k\), \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{[f(y_k)-M(y_k;x_k)]_+}{\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert}=0.\] Equivalently, along every such pair there exist numbers \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\) such that \(f(y_k)\le M(y_k;x_k)+\varepsilon_k\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert\). This condition strengthens base-point exactness by controlling simultaneous motion of the base and trial points. It is local at \(\bar x\) and makes no global minorization or convexity assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict oracle model upper-approximates the objective with error little-o of displacement even when the base and trial points move together.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Oracle Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assumption \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\neq(-\infty,+\infty]\) is invalid. More importantly, strict-model definitions differ in the orientation of the modeling error and in whether an upper semicontinuous error modulus or a sequential condition is required. An authoritative source is needed before selecting and repairing the definition.

children.title: Structure-Exploiting Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Composite, spectral, and max-structured oracle models.

assumptions_latex: The linearized point lies in the effective domain of \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structure-exploiting oracle model is \(M(y;x)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-composite linearization covering max and spectral models through a structured outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex-composite objective \(F=h\circ c\), the structure-exploiting model at \(x\) is \[M(y;x):=h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x)\bigr).\] It preserves the outer convex structure while linearizing only the smooth inner map, and satisfies \(M(x;x)=F(x)\). If \(h(u)=\max_{1\le i\le r}u_i\), then \(M(y;x)=\max_i\{c_i(x)+\langle\nabla c_i(x),y-x\rangle\}\). Matrix spectral objectives fit the same pattern by taking \(c(x)\) matrix-valued and \(h\) a convex spectral function, with the linearization interpreted in the corresponding matrix space. Bundle cuts may be generated from subgradients of \(h\) at modeled inner values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite oracle models preserve convex max or spectral outer structure while linearizing only the smooth inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Exploiting Oracle Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-composite model is standard in form, but no source supports its placement as the exact oracle-model convention here. The spectral extension also changes the declared codomain of c from \(\mathbb{R}^m\) to a matrix space without introducing that space or the corresponding derivative domains.

children.top_down_role: Canonical subproblem architectures providing well-posedness and step control.

children.title: Proximal Bundle Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Bundle subproblems stabilized by a proximity term.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous bundle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point minimizes \(m_k(y)+(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\) over \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core stabilized trial-point subproblem, independent of a particular serious/null-step acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a stability center \(x_k\in D\), a bundle model \(m_k\), and \(t_k>0\), compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in D}\left\{m_k(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Define the predicted decrease by \(\Delta_k:=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)-(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert^2\). Evaluate \(f(y_k)\) and the chosen oracle at \(y_k\). If a prescribed acceptance test comparing actual and predicted decrease holds, set \(x_{k+1}:=y_k\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}:=x_k\). In either case, add the new oracle information to the bundle, optionally aggregate or delete inactive cuts, and stop when a selected model residual or \(\Delta_k\) is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle step minimizes the current model plus a quadratic centered at the incumbent, then accepts or rejects the trial using model agreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Bundle Subproblems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal minimization is an appropriate core subproblem, but the acceptance test, predicted-decrease formula, bundle update, and stopping rule describe an underspecified family of algorithms. A source is required to determine the intended nonconvex bundle variant and its sufficient model assumptions.

children.title: Trust-Region Tangent Programs
children.top_down_role: Localized tangent programs with explicit displacement control.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a tangent or bundle model finite at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
The trial displacement obeys \(\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert
i\le\Delta_k\) by construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region stabilization of a localized tangent or bundle model.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute a trial point by \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{m_k(y):y\in D,\ \lVert y-x_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\}.\] When \(m_k(x_k)>m_k(y_k)\), form \(r_k:=[f(x_k)-f(y_k)]/[m_k(x_k)-m_k(y_k)]\). Accept the trial by setting \(x_{k+1}:=y_k\) when \(r_k\ge\eta_1\), and otherwise set \(x_{k+1}:=x_k\), where \(0<\eta_1<1\). Shrink \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit enlargement after sufficiently good agreement, subject to fixed positive bounds. Update the tangent information at evaluated trial points. Stop when the predicted reduction or a model-based stationarity measure is at most the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region tangent program minimizes the local model under an explicit displacement bound and updates that bound using actual versus predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Tangent Programs

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited trust-region section is too general to support the stated nonsmooth tangent-or-bundle specialization, its update rules, and its stationarity stopping measure. The conclusion also contains the erroneous relation \(\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert\ni\le\Delta_k\), which must be changed to \(\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\) after a suitable source is supplied.
