children.title: Level Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Bundle subproblems stabilized through target level sets.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a convex bundle model with lower estimate \(L_k\).
An incumbent value \(U_k>L_k\), center \(x_k\), and fraction \(\theta_k\in(0,1)\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next trial is the projection of \(x_k\) onto the model level set \(\{y\in D:m_k(y)\le\ell_k\}\).

notation.meaning: current lower and upper objective estimates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-type level subproblem formed from a convex bundle model and an intermediate target value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose the target level \(\ell_k:=(1-	heta_k)L_k+	heta_kU_k\) and define \(Q_k:=\{y\in D:m_k(y)\le\ell_k\}\). If \(Q_k\ne\varnothing\), compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y
i\in Q_k}\frac12\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2.\] Evaluate the objective and oracle at \(y_k\), update the incumbent upper estimate, and add the resulting cut to \(m_k\). If \(Q_k=\varnothing\), the model certifies that \(\ell_k\) is below its attainable value on \(D\), so update the lower estimate accordingly before selecting another level. Terminate when \(U_k-L_k\) or the chosen stationarity surrogate is within tolerance. In nonconvex applications, localization and model-validity safeguards are additionally required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level subproblem projects the current center onto a model sublevel set at a target strictly between the lower and incumbent values.
knowledge_statements.title: Level Subproblems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-type convex level subproblem is plausible, but the argmin domain contains the malformed expression \(y\ni\in Q_k\). No source supports the lower-bound updates, stopping rule, or additional safeguards needed to place this convex-model construction in the stated nonconvex model-method family.

children.title: Proximal-Level Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Level-set subproblems augmented by proximal geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) is a finite polyhedral bundle model on \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(t>0\), and the level \(\ell\in\mathbb R\) gives a nonempty set \(L_\ell=\{x:m(x)\le \ell\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+\) is the point of \(L_\ell\) nearest to \(c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Euclidean proximal-level subproblem with a polyhedral bundle model.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(m\), \(c\), \(t\), and \(\ell\), compute
\[
x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac{1}{2t}\|x-c\|^2:m(x)\le \ell\right\}.
\]
Initialize \(c\) at the current serious iterate and choose \(\ell\) between an available model lower value and the current objective value. If the constraint is feasible, return its unique minimizer \(x^+\); otherwise return an infeasibility flag for the model level set. Infeasibility is only a model statement unless the cuts are valid global lower bounds for the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the current center onto a polyhedral model level set; infeasibility concerns only that model unless every cut is a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Level Subproblems

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

children.title: Nonconvex Level-Method Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundary between nonconvex bundle usage and primarily convex level-method theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Level-Method Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary caused by treating local nonconvex cuts as global underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(f(x)=-x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\) and form at \(0\) the affine local model \(m(x)=f(0)+0(x-0)=0\). For any \(\ell<0\),
\[
\{x:m(x)\le\ell\}=\varnothing,
\qquad
\{x:f(x)\le\ell\}=\{x:|x|\ge\sqrt{-\ell}\}\ne\varnothing.
\]
Thus infeasibility of a level subproblem built from merely local nonconvex models does not certify that the true objective level set is empty. A valid level-method lower-bound interpretation requires global minorants, a convexified model with an appropriate curvature correction, or an explicit locality restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local affine model can have an empty lower level while the nonconvex objective attains that level, so model infeasibility need not certify objective infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \(f(x)=-x^2\); equivalently, \(f\) is \(2\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb R\).
The level model consists only of the affine first-order model at \(0\), namely \(m(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\ell<0\), \(\{x:m(x)\le\ell\}=\varnothing\) while \(\{x:f(x)\le\ell\}\ne\varnothing\).

children.title: Bundle-Multiplier Representations
children.top_down_role: Dual-weight representations of active bundle information.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bundle weights belong to \(\Delta_I\), and the primal step satisfies \(x^*=c-t\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-Lagrange dual of a polyhedral proximal bundle subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal problem
\[
\min_x\left\{m(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-c\|^2\right\},
\]
introduce an epigraph variable and multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for \(a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le r\). Its dual is
\[
\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_I}\left\{\sum_i\lambda_i(a_i+\langle g_i,c\rangle)-\frac t2\left\|\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\right\|^2\right\},
\quad
\Delta_I=\{\lambda\ge0:\sum_i\lambda_i=1\}.
\]
At any primal-dual solution, \(x^*=c-t\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\), and positive multipliers can occur only on cuts active at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual simplex weights select active bundle cuts, and their weighted subgradient determines the proximal displacement from the center.
knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Multiplier Representations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

children.title: Aggregate-Subgradient Representations
children.top_down_role: Compressed first-order information derived from subproblem duality.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair and an optimal multiplier \(\lambda^*\in\Delta_I\) are as in Bundle-Multiplier Representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar g=\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i=(c-x^*)/t\) and \(\bar a+\langle\bar g,x^*\rangle=m(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation induced by optimal dual weights in the proximal subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\bar g=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i^*g_i,
\qquad
\bar a=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i^*a_i.
\]
Then the aggregate affine function \(x\mapsto\bar a+\langle\bar g,x\rangle\) is a convex combination of bundle cuts and therefore does not exceed \(m(x)\) for any \(x\). Complementarity gives
\[
\bar a+\langle\bar g,x^*\rangle=m(x^*),
\qquad
\bar g=\frac{c-x^*}{t}.
\]
Consequently, the single pair \((\bar a,\bar g)\) preserves both the model value at the proximal solution and the first-order balance of the full active bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal dual weights compress active cuts into one affine aggregate that preserves the model value and proximal stationarity at the trial point.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Subgradient Representations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Convex Quadratic and Nonlinear Programs p. 80

children.title: Primal-Dual Model Certificates
children.top_down_role: Model-quality information combining primal trial points and dual bundle data.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Model Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for a convex polyhedral proximal model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the primal value at \(x^*\) by \(p(x^*)=m(x^*)+\|x^*-c\|^2/(2t)\), and define
\[
d(\lambda^*)=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i^*(a_i+\langle g_i,c\rangle)-\frac t2\left\|\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i^*g_i\right\|^2.
\]
If \(x^*\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda^*\in\Delta_I\), and \(p(x^*)=d(\lambda^*)\), then primal-dual equality certifies exact subproblem optimality. In that case,
\[
\delta=m(c)-p(x^*)=m(c)-m(x^*)-\frac{1}{2t}\|x^*-c\|^2\ge0.
\]
The quantity \(\delta\) certifies predicted decrease in the regularized model; comparison with actual objective decrease requires separate objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible primal and dual points with matching values certify the exact proximal model solution, and the resulting regularized model decrease is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) is a finite polyhedral model on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(p(x^*)=d(\lambda^*)\), then \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) certifies exact primal-dual optimality and \(\delta=m(c)-p(x^*)\ge0\).

children.title: Localized Proximal Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Proximal bundle methods with locality-controlled cuts.

assumptions_latex: Each cut \(q_i\) is certified as a lower local model of \(f\) on a ball \(B(y_i,r_i)\).
A current center \(c_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and proximal parameter \(t_k>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted trial lies where all cuts used to predict its decrease are certified locally valid.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic locality-controlled proximal bundle architecture, not a named implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), retain the eligible cuts
\[
I_k(x)=\{i:x\in B(y_i,r_i)\},
\qquad
m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k(x)}q_i(x),
\]
and compute a trial point by minimizing \(m_k(x)+\|x-c_k\|^2/(2t_k)\) subject to \(\|x-c_k\|\le\Delta_k\) and membership in the validity regions of all cuts used at the solution. Evaluate \(f\) at the trial point. Accept it as the next center when actual decrease is a prescribed positive fraction of predicted decrease; otherwise retain \(c_k\), add a local cut, and reduce \(\Delta_k\) or the eligible bundle. Stop under a stated model-stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method solves proximal bundle subproblems using only cuts valid near the trial point, then accepts or localizes according to actual versus predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Localized Proximal Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the method leaf, but the cited weak-convexity section does not establish this locality-controlled algorithm. The state-dependent index set can make the model discontinuous, and the requirement that all cuts used at the solution be locally valid is circular without a precise subproblem construction.

children.title: Redistributed Proximal Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Proximal methods based on adaptively redistributed convexified models.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex and \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Redistributing the common negative curvature into the proximal term produces a strongly convex trial subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-curvature redistribution for finite-dimensional weakly convex bundle models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form valid weak-convexity cuts
\[
q_i(x)=f(y_i)+\langle g_i,x-y_i\rangle-\frac\rho2\|x-y_i\|^2,
\qquad
m_k(x)=\max_i q_i(x).
\]
Compute
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-c_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
Expanding the common quadratic term redistributes curvature: the objective equals a maximum of affine functions plus a quadratic having Hessian \((t_k^{-1}-\rho)I\), up to constants and linear terms. Hence it is strongly convex when \(t_k<1/\rho\). Use actual-versus-predicted decrease to accept the trial or update the bundle and \(t_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak-convexity curvature is moved from quadratic bundle cuts into the proximal regularizer, yielding a strongly convex subproblem when the step parameter is small enough.
knowledge_statements.title: Redistributed Proximal Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The curvature algebra and strong-convexity threshold are correct, and algorithm is the appropriate kind. However, the supplied weak-convexity locator does not support the asserted redistributed proximal bundle method, including its bundle and acceptance updates.

children.title: Inexact Proximal Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Proximal bundle methods with controlled oracle or subproblem errors.

assumptions_latex: Oracle data satisfy \(|\tilde f_i-f(y_i)|\le\varepsilon_i^f\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(\tilde g_i,\partial f(y_i))\le\varepsilon_i^g\).
The computed trial point has subproblem objective at most \(\eta_k\) above the exact infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method may declare termination only when its stationarity residual and the accumulated error allowance are both below prescribed tolerances.
review_flags: no supplied locator supports the stated inexactness model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deterministic absolute-error oracle and inexact-subproblem variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Construct each bundle cut from \((\tilde f_i,\tilde g_i)\) with an explicit downward correction large enough to cover \(\varepsilon_i^f\), \(\varepsilon_i^g\), and the region on which the cut is used. Given the corrected model \(\tilde m_k\), compute \(x_{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
\tilde m_k(x_{k+1})+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x_{k+1}-c_k\|^2
\le
\inf_x\left\{\tilde m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-c_k\|^2\right\}+\eta_k.
\]
Accept or reject using decrease tests enlarged by the certified error bounds. Stop only if a computable stationarity residual and the total oracle-plus-solve allowance are below their respective tolerances; otherwise refine the oracle, solve more accurately, or continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified oracle and subproblem errors are included in cuts, acceptance tests, and stopping rules; termination requires both stationarity and error allowances to be small.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but no citation is supplied. A pointwise subgradient-distance error does not by itself determine the stated regional downward correction or the accumulated stopping allowance; these require a precise error model and method-specific source.

children.title: Constrained Proximal Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Proximal bundle methods retaining tractable constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Proximal Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-convex constrained proximal bundle subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(c_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), construct the finite convex bundle model \(m_k\) and compute
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-c_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
The trial point exists and is unique, and its optimality condition is
\[
0\in\partial m_k(x_{k+1})+\frac{1}{t_k}(x_{k+1}-c_k)+N_C(x_{k+1}).
\]
Evaluate \(f\) at \(x_{k+1}\); accept it as a serious iterate when actual decrease adequately matches predicted decrease, and otherwise retain \(c_k\) while adding bundle information. Every center and trial point remains in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the finite convex bundle model plus the proximal term over the closed convex feasible set; the unique trial point satisfies an optimality condition containing the feasible-set normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and optimization over \(C\) is tractable.
\(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is a finite convex bundle model, \(c_k\in C\), and \(t_k>0\).
\(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is the objective evaluated by the serious-step test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique trial point satisfies \(0\in\partial m_k(x_{k+1})+t_k^{-1}(x_{k+1}-c_k)+N_C(x_{k+1})\).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone to the feasible set

children.title: Polyhedral Bundle Trust-Region Methods
children.top_down_role: Trust-region methods using piecewise-affine bundle models.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) is a finite piecewise-affine model.
A center \(c_k\), norm \(\|\cdot\|_k\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point minimizes the polyhedral model over the trust region and is accepted according to actual versus predicted reduction.
review_flags: bundle specialization of trust-region locator is provisional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral bundle model with a norm trust region.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Compute
\[
x_k^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|x-c_k\|_k\le\Delta_k}m_k(x),
\qquad
\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(c_k)-m_k(x_k^+).
\]
If \(\operatorname{pred}_k\) is below the stopping tolerance, return \(c_k\) with the corresponding model certificate. Otherwise evaluate \(f(x_k^+)\) and form
\[
r_k=\frac{f(c_k)-f(x_k^+)}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.
\]
Accept \(x_k^+\) as the new center when \(r_k\) exceeds a prescribed threshold; otherwise keep \(c_k\) and add a cut at the trial point. Enlarge, retain, or contract \(\Delta_k\) according to fixed thresholds on \(r_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a piecewise-affine bundle model inside a trust region, then update the center, bundle, and radius using the ratio of actual to predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Bundle Trust-Region Methods

A center \(c_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and a specified global or certified subproblem solver are available.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form the curvature-enriched model \(m_k(c_k+s)=\max_{i\in I_k}q_i(s)\) and compute
\[
s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|s\|_k\le\Delta_k}\max_{i\in I_k}q_i(s).
\]
If all \(B_i\succeq0\), this is a convex epigraph-constrained quadratic problem; otherwise the algorithm must use a global solver or return an explicit subproblem accuracy certificate. Define predicted reduction by \(m_k(c_k)-m_k(c_k+s_k)\), evaluate the objective at \(c_k+s_k\), and accept or reject through the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio. Update the radius and retain curvature pieces whose locality and accuracy conditions remain valid.

children.title: Second-Order Bundle Trust-Region Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle trust-region methods using richer curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Bundle Trust-Region Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic second-order local bundle trust-region architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At center \(c_k\), define eligible second-order pieces
\[
q_i(x)=f_i+\langle g_i,x-y_i\rangle+\frac12\langle x-y_i,H_i(x-y_i)\rangle,
\qquad
M_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}q_i(x).
\]
Compute a globally optimal or certified approximate solution of
\[
\min_{\|x-c_k\|_k\le\Delta_k}M_k(x).
\]
Evaluate \(f\) at the trial point and compare actual reduction with \(M_k(c_k)-M_k(x)\). Accept when the ratio and declared second-order modeling-error bounds meet prescribed thresholds; otherwise retain the center, add information, regularize unreliable \(H_i\), or contract \(\Delta_k\). Stop only with a stated stationarity and subproblem-accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local quadratic pieces from second-order data form a bundle trust-region model; acceptance requires both observed reduction and certified curvature-model reliability.
assumptions_latex: For each sampled point \(y_i\), first-order data \((f_i,g_i)\) and a symmetric second-order model \(H_i\) are available.
Each second-order piece has a declared locality region and modeling-error bound.
The objective \(f\), center \(c_k\), trust-region norm \(\|\cdot\|_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and eligible finite index set \(I_k\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A trial step is accepted only when its second-order bundle prediction is reliable relative to observed objective reduction and the declared modeling-error bounds.

children.title: Curvature-Model Reliability
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits for curvature-enriched bundle trust-region models.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite near the current center \(x_k\).
The bundle model \(m_k\) satisfies \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), and \(d_k\) approximately minimizes its curvature-enriched trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\geq\eta\) certifies reliability for accepting the trial point; \(\rho_k<\eta\) declares the local curvature model unreliable at the current radius.

notation.meaning: Acceptance threshold in the open unit interval.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio-based reliability test for a curvature-enriched bundle model within a trust region.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio by \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+d_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+d_k)}.\] For a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the curvature model is reliable for this trial when \(\rho_k\geq\eta\). In that case the trial point may replace the center. When \(\rho_k<\eta\), the trial is rejected as a serious step, and the algorithm must instead refine the bundle, modify the curvature term, reduce \(\delta_k\), or combine these actions before relying on the model for center movement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature model is reliable when its predicted decrease agrees sufficiently with the observed decrease, as measured by a trust-region reduction ratio.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Model Reliability

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

children.title: Structure-Exploiting Bundle Trust-Region Methods
children.top_down_role: Composite, spectral, and difference-of-convex trust-region variants.

assumptions_latex: \(f=h\circ F+g-q\) on a closed set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), with locally available structure-specific models.
Each component model is finite at the center \(x_k\) and exact there.
The trust-region subproblem has a computed feasible approximate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update exploits the declared composite, spectral, or difference-of-convex structure while retaining bundle-model stabilization and ratio-based acceptance.

notation.meaning: Structure-preserving local model of the objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite-dimensional template covering composite, spectral, and difference-of-convex bundle trust-region variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), construct a structure-preserving bundle model \(M_k\) by linearizing only those constituent mappings for which first-order information is available, retaining exactly evaluable convex or spectral constituents, and majorizing or explicitly separating the concave term \(-q\). Compute \[d_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d}\{M_k(x_k+d):x_k+d\in C,\ \|d\|\leq\delta_k\}.\] Evaluate \(f(x_k+d_k)\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) when the prescribed actual-to-predicted reduction test holds; otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), append trial information to the bundle, and update the model or radius. Stop when the model decrease or a stationarity residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method preserves known composite, spectral, or difference-of-convex structure inside a bundle trust-region subproblem and accepts steps by model agreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Exploiting Bundle Trust-Region Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This record blends composite, spectral, and difference-of-convex variants into one algorithm without defining the properties of h, F, g, and q that justify the proposed model operations. An authoritative source is needed to determine whether this is a valid common algorithm or must be represented as separate variants.

children.title: Level Bundle Variants
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods stabilized through model level sets.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a finite convex bundle model on \(C\), exact at the center \(x_k\).
Bounds \(L_k\leq f_*\leq U_k=f(x_k)\) are available, with \(L_k<U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next trial is a projection onto a model level set lying strictly between the current lower and upper objective bounds.

notation.meaning: Reference point used in the projection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection form of a convex-model level bundle iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\theta_k\in(0,1)\) and set \(\ell_k=(1-\theta_k)L_k+\theta_kU_k\). Form the model level set \[S_k=\{x\in C:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}.\] If \(S_k\neq\varnothing\), compute \(y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S_k}\tfrac12\|x-z_k\|^2\), evaluate \(f(y_k)\), add the resulting function and subgradient information to the bundle, and update \(U_k\) whenever \(f(y_k)<U_k\). If \(S_k=\varnothing\), raise the lower bound consistently with the model certificate. Stop when \(U_k-L_k\) or a prescribed model-based stationarity measure is at most the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level bundle method projects a reference point onto a bundle-model level set and updates objective bounds using feasibility and trial evaluations.
knowledge_statements.title: Level Bundle Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-level template is recognizable, and algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the assumptions describe a convex level-bundle variant while the immutable path is a weakly convex-nonconvex method family. A source is needed to support this placement and to specify the lower-bound certificate and update rules.

children.title: Proximal-Level Bundle Variants
children.top_down_role: Level methods combining projection and proximity control.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex bundle model, exact at \(x_k\).
The chosen model level set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point simultaneously satisfies the model level constraint and minimizes a proximal distance to the current center or reference point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set projection with an explicit proximal stabilization term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_k=\{x\in C:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\) and compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S_k}\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\|x-z_k\|^2.\] Evaluate \(f(y_k)\) and obtain first-order information there. If the prescribed descent or level-improvement test holds, move the stability center to \(y_k\); otherwise retain the center and enrich the bundle with the new information. Update \(\ell_k\), \(z_k\), and possibly \(\tau_k\) while maintaining a level strictly below the current upper bound. Return the best evaluated point when the objective gap or the model-based stationarity residual is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-level variant projects onto a bundle-model level set while a proximal term controls displacement from a selected reference point.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Level Bundle Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The level-set projection is mathematically well posed under the stated assumptions, but the center, level, reference, and proximal-parameter updates are left method dependent. A proximal-level bundle source is required to verify the complete algorithm and its use in the stated nonconvex family.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refined Inner Iteration for a Nonconvex Bundle Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner iteration combining approximate-stationarity, serious-step, null-step, line-search, and stabilization-parameter refinement decisions; the referenced model and SS/NS tests are defined outside this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a locally Lipschitz function \(\mathcal F\), an iteration point \(z^k\), and trial points \(\{y^i\}_{i=1}^k\), initialize \(t^1=t_{k-1}\), \(t^*=0\), \(\bar t=T\), and \(j=1\). Solve model (6.9), replacing \(\alpha_{jk}\) by \(\beta_{jk}\), to obtain \((u^j,d^j)\). If \(\|d^j\|/t^j\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|d^j\|^2/t^j+u^j\geq-\varepsilon\), stop and declare \(z^k\) almost stationary. Otherwise set \(w^j=z^k+d^j\) and compute \(v(w^j)\in\partial\mathcal F(w^j)\). Under SS(i), take the serious step \(z^{k+1}=y^{k+1}=w^j\). Under NS(i)--NS(iii), take the null step \(z^{k+1}=z^k\), \(y^{k+1}=w^j\). If NS(i) and NS(ii) hold but NS(iii) fails, perform the prescribed line search along \(z^k+s d^j\), \(s\geq0\), when the second condition of NS(ii) holds; otherwise bisect the stabilization parameter and repeat the refinement loop. If NS(i) holds but NS(ii) fails, set \(\bar t=t^j\), \(t^{j+1}=\tfrac12(\bar t+t^*)\), increment \(j\), and resolve the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the refined bundle model and test for approximate stationarity. Otherwise evaluate a subgradient at the trial point and apply the referenced serious-step and null-step tests to accept a new center, retain the current center while adding a trial point, conduct a line search, or refine the stabilization parameter.
assumptions_latex: \text{Model (6.9), the coefficients }\beta_{jk},\text{ and tests SS(i), NS(i)--NS(iii) are defined}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The inner iteration returns an almost-stationarity declaration, a serious step, a null step, or a refined model.}

children.title: Descent Bundle Line Searches
children.top_down_role: Line searches targeting accepted movement of the stability center.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz near the center \(x_k\).
A bundle model \(m_k\), search direction \(d_k\), and positive predicted decrease \(\Delta_k\) are available.
The line search examines trial points \(x_k+t d_k\) with \(t\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted serious step moves the stability center and realizes a fixed fraction of the bundle model's predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serious-step line search driven by a bundle model's predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting with \(t=1\), evaluate \(f(x_k+t d_k)\) and first-order information, reducing \(t\) according to the selected backtracking rule until \[f(x_k+t d_k)\leq f(x_k)-\sigma t\Delta_k.\] On satisfaction, declare a serious step, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t d_k\), and update the bundle at the new center. Every rejected trial may be inserted into the bundle before continuing the search. Terminate unsuccessfully only under the method's prescribed minimum-step or stationarity test; otherwise output the accepted center and the enriched bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The line search moves the stability center only when an evaluated trial realizes a prescribed fraction of the model-predicted descent.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent Bundle Line Searches

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The serious-step line-search pattern fits the leaf and algorithm is the correct role, but the use of t Delta_k depends on how the full-step predicted decrease is defined. The admissible backtracking, rejected-trial handling, and termination conditions require a bundle line-search source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conceptual nonsmooth bundle iteration combining a quadratically stabilized cutting-plane subproblem with line-search-based serious/null-step selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $t_k>0$, compute $d_k\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f_{\mathrm{CP}}(x_k;d)+\frac{1}{2t_k}d^Td\right\}$ and perform a line search for $f$ along $x_k+\lambda d_k$, $\lambda\geq0$. If sufficient decrease is obtained, take a serious step $x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_kd_k$, with $\lambda_k\in\arg\min_{\lambda>0}f(x_k+\lambda d_k)$, and compute $g_{k+1}\in\partial f(x_{k+1})$. If only insufficient decrease is obtained, take a null step $x_{k+1}=x_k$ and compute $g_{k+1}\in\partial f(x_k+\lambda d_k)$ for a suitable small $\lambda>0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the quadratically stabilized cutting-plane model and line-search along the resulting direction. Sufficient decrease yields a serious step and a subgradient at the accepted point; insufficient decrease leaves the iterate fixed and gathers a subgradient at a nearby trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The iteration produces either }x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_kd_k\text{ in the serious-step branch or }x_{k+1}=x_k\text{ in the null-step branch, and computes the specified subgradient.}

children.title: Null-Step-Compatible Line Searches
children.top_down_role: Searches permitting model enrichment without reference-point movement.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near the current center \(x_k\).
A bundle model and direction \(d_k\) provide positive predicted decrease \(\Delta_k\).
A trial point supplies a function value and admissible first-order information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the serious-step test need not terminate the search: the center remains fixed while the rejected trial strengthens the model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line search allowing null steps that enrich the bundle without moving the center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate \(y_k=x_k+t_kd_k\). If \[f(y_k)\leq f(x_k)-\sigma t_k\Delta_k,\] declare a serious step and set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\). Otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), add the value and first-order information from \(y_k\) to the bundle, and declare a null step whenever that information yields the prescribed improvement of the local model. After a null step, recompute the model direction or modify \(t_k\); do not require movement of the center. Stop when the enriched model certifies the selected stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejected trial can become a null step: it enriches the bundle while the stability center remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step-Compatible Line Searches

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record captures the defining center-preserving behavior of a null step, but the required model-improvement test is only referenced as prescribed and is not stated. A specific bundle line-search source is needed to establish when a rejected trial qualifies as a null step and how the search continues.

children.title: Nonmonotone-Fractional Acceptance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes beyond the classical binary serious/null decision.

children.title: Nonmonotone Acceptance
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes permitting controlled departures from monotone objective decrease.

assumptions_latex: A sequence of accepted-center values \(f(x_j)\) is available.
The trial has positive model-predicted decrease \(\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule may accept an objective increase relative to \(f(x_k)\), but only within the controlled reference envelope \(R_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope-based nonmonotone serious-step test for a bundle line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a finite-memory or averaged reference value \(R_k\) satisfying \(R_k\geq f(x_k)\). A trial displacement \(s_k\) with predicted decrease \(\Delta_k>0\) is accepted whenever \[f(x_k+s_k)\leq R_k-\sigma\Delta_k.\] After acceptance, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and update \(R_{k+1}\) by the prescribed finite-memory maximum or convex averaging rule. The reference update must keep \(R_{k+1}\) bounded by recent accepted values or their convex combinations, so unrestricted objective growth is excluded even though monotonicity of \(f(x_k)\) is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonmonotone acceptance compares a trial with a controlled history-dependent reference, allowing limited increases while still requiring model-based reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Acceptance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the local meaning of nonmonotone acceptance, but finite-memory maxima and convexly averaged references have different update invariants. A source is required to support the claimed common envelope properties in a bundle line-search setting.

children.title: Fractional Acceptance
children.top_down_role: Intermediate trial outcomes between full serious-step acceptance and null rejection.

assumptions_latex: The trial has actual reduction \(A_k\) and strictly positive predicted reduction \(P_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial is accepted exactly when the actual reduction realizes at least the fraction \(\eta_k\) of the predicted reduction.

notation.meaning: Actual reduction relative to the selected reference value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-versus-predicted fractional acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\) be the acceptance reference, let \(y_k\) be the trial point, and define \[A_k=R_k-f(y_k),\qquad P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0.\] The trial is accepted as a serious step precisely when \[A_k\geq\eta_kP_k,\] equivalently when \(A_k/P_k\geq\eta_k\). Otherwise the center is unchanged and the trial may be used for bundle enrichment. The reference may be monotone, with \(R_k=f(x_k)\), or nonmonotone, provided its update obeys the compatibility requirements of the chosen convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional acceptance requires the observed reduction to be at least a prescribed fraction of the bundle model's predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Acceptance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The actual-versus-predicted fractional test is precise and condition is the appropriate content kind. However, no citation supports its bundle-method specialization, its definition of predicted reduction, or the stated serious-step consequence.

children.title: Acceptance-Regime Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction of nonmonotone reference values with fractional center movement.

assumptions_latex: The predicted reductions satisfy \(P_k>0\) at every nonstationary trial.
Reference values obey \(f(x_k)\leq R_k\) and have controlled excess \(R_k-f(x_k)\).
Accepted trials satisfy \(R_k-f(x_{k+1})\geq\eta P_k\) for fixed \(\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonmonotone reference and fractional test are compatible when accumulated accepted predicted decrease remains controlled by genuine objective progress and vanishing reference excess.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient compatibility condition for combining nonmonotone references with fractional model acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The regimes are compatible if the reference update ensures \(e_k=R_k-f(x_k)\geq0\), \(e_k\to0\) along accepted centers, and either \(\sum_k e_k<\infty\) or an equivalent telescoping reference inequality. Together with \[R_k-f(x_{k+1})\geq\eta P_k,\] these requirements prevent the nonmonotone allowance from indefinitely paying for trials having inadequate actual progress. Consequently, whenever the accepted objective values are bounded below, the convergence argument can force \(P_k\to0\) along an infinite accepted subsequence, subject to the bundle method's separate model-consistency assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonmonotone and fractional rules are compatible when reference excess vanishes sufficiently fast, so accepted predicted decrease cannot be financed indefinitely by past values.
knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Regime Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The summable-excess version can support a telescoping argument, but the alternative described only as an equivalent telescoping reference inequality is not a mathematical condition. The conclusion P_k to 0 is theorem-like and depends on indexing, lower boundedness, reference updates, and model consistency that must be verified from a method-specific convergence source.

children.top_down_role: Bundle methods using second-order surrogates, changing metrics, or smooth-subspace structure.

children.title: Bundle Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods incorporating second-order local information.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz and a bundle provides affine first-order pieces near \(x_k\).
A symmetric curvature matrix \(H_k\) makes the stabilized subproblem bounded below.
The computed trial supplies new function and first-order information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration combines bundle cutting planes with a Newton-type quadratic term and accepts or rejects the resulting trial by a model-agreement test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Newton-type bundle subproblem with quadratic curvature stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At center \(x_k\), construct the quadratic bundle model \[M_k(d)=\widehat m_k(x_k+d)+\tfrac12\langle d,H_kd\rangle+\tfrac{1}{2\tau_k}\|d\|^2,\qquad \tau_k>0.\] Compute an approximate minimizer \(d_k\), possibly subject to a trust region, and evaluate \(f(x_k+d_k)\). Accept the trial and update the center when its actual reduction is a prescribed fraction of the predicted reduction; otherwise retain \(x_k\) and add the trial information to the bundle. Update \(H_k\) from available second-order or secant information. Stop when the model displacement and a compatible stationarity residual satisfy tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bundle Newton methods add a Newton-type quadratic term to a cutting-plane model, stabilize the subproblem, and use model agreement to accept trials.
knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Newton Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited proximal Newton section does not, by its locator, support a cutting-plane bundle Newton algorithm with serious and null steps. A specialized bundle Newton source is required for the quadratic model, curvature update, acceptance rule, and stopping test.

children.title: Variable-Metric Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods using changing stabilization metrics.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz and has a finite bundle model \(m_k\) at \(x_k\).
Each metric matrix \(B_k\) is symmetric positive definite.
Uniform constants satisfy \(0<\underline b I\preceq B_k\preceq\overline b I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The changing metric defines a uniformly equivalent proximal geometry, so every stabilized bundle subproblem is strongly convex whenever \(m_k\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly positive-definite variable-metric proximal bundle iteration.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.2 Methods of Variable Metric and Methods of Conjugate Directions p. 78

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\left\{m_k(y)+\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\langle y-x_k,B_k(y-x_k)\rangle\right\}.\] Evaluate \(f(y_k)\) and first-order information. Move the center to \(y_k\) if the serious-step test holds; otherwise retain \(x_k\) and enrich the bundle. Update \(B_k\) by the prescribed secant, quasi-Newton, or scaling rule, safeguarding the spectral bounds \(\underline b I\preceq B_k\preceq\overline b I\). Return the current center when the variable-metric model residual or predicted decrease is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-metric bundle method replaces Euclidean proximal stabilization by a changing uniformly positive-definite metric while preserving serious and null steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Bundle Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.2 Methods of Variable Metric and Methods of Conjugate Directions p. 78

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general variable-metric section may support safeguarded positive-definite metrics, but it does not support the stated proximal bundle algorithm or its serious/null-step logic. A variable-metric bundle source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: VU Smooth-Subspace Bundle Method Pair
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods separating smooth and nonsmooth local directions.

children.title: VU Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods organized around local VU decompositions.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is prox-regular near a reference point \(\bar x\) for a selected subgradient \(\bar g\).
A bundle near \(x_k\) approximates the active subgradients defining the nonsmooth subspace.
The resulting subspace decomposition is numerically well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration uses bundle information for the nonsmooth \(\mathcal V\)-component and a smooth Newton-type correction on the complementary \(\mathcal U\)-component.

notation.meaning: Subspace spanned by active subgradient differences.
Orthogonal projections onto the two subspaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local VU decomposition coupling nonsmooth bundle control with smooth-subspace Newton correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(\mathcal V_k\) from differences of active or nearly active bundle subgradients and set \(\mathcal U_k=\mathcal V_k^\perp\). Compute a stabilized bundle displacement \(v_k\in\mathcal V_k\) from the nonsmooth model. Conditional on that displacement, compute \(u_k\in\mathcal U_k\) by solving a smooth reduced Newton or quasi-Newton model on \(\mathcal U_k\). Form \[y_k=x_k+u_k+v_k.\] Accept \(y_k\) when the prescribed actual-to-predicted reduction test holds; otherwise retain \(x_k\), enrich the bundle, and recompute the subspaces. Stop when both projected stationarity residuals \(P_{\mathcal U_k}r_k\) and \(P_{\mathcal V_k}r_k\) meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A VU bundle method models nonsmooth behavior in the active V-subspace and applies a Newton-type correction in the complementary smooth U-subspace.
knowledge_statements.title: VU Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Prox-regularity and a numerically defined subspace decomposition alone do not ensure an identifiable smooth U-subspace or justify a reduced Newton step. A specialized VU or partial-smoothness source is required to determine the active-subgradient construction, identification hypotheses, projected residuals, and acceptance mechanism.

children.title: Smooth-Subspace Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods exploiting locally smooth directional subspaces.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz near a stability center \(x_k\).
An orthogonal decomposition \(\mathbb{R}^n=U_k\oplus V_k\) is available, with nonsmooth variation represented in \(V_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+U_ku_k+V_kv_k\), with \(u_k\) obtained from a smooth local model and \(v_k\) controlled by bundle information.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis matrices for the estimated smooth and nonsmooth subspaces
steps in the smooth and nonsmooth coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deterministic VU-type scheme; globalization and subspace construction remain method-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), form an orthogonal decomposition \(\mathbb{R}^n=U_k\oplus V_k\). Construct a smooth local model \(q_k:U_k\to\mathbb{R}\) for variation along \(U_k\), and a bundle model \(m_k:V_k\to\mathbb{R}\) for variation along \(V_k\). Compute \(u_k\) by approximately minimizing \(q_k(u)\) subject to the current globalization restriction, compute \(v_k\) from the bundle subproblem, and set \(y_k=x_k+U_ku_k+V_kv_k\). Accept \(y_k\) as the next center only when its actual reduction satisfies the prescribed comparison with predicted reduction; otherwise retain \(x_k\), enrich the bundle, and recompute the decomposition if required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth-subspace bundle method combines a smooth step on an estimated smooth subspace with a bundle-controlled step on its nonsmooth complement.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Subspace Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this bundle-specific algorithm. Moreover, U_k and V_k are described as basis matrices but used as subspaces in the direct-sum decomposition and as model domains; the accepted-center update also depends on an unspecified globalization rule.

children.title: Subspace Identification Reliability
children.top_down_role: Limits on stable separation of smooth and nonsmooth local directions.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is partly smooth at \(x_\star\) relative to a smooth manifold \(\mathcal M\).
The iterates satisfy \(x_k\to x_\star\), and bundle subgradients approximate the active subdifferential geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gap}(U_k,T_{\mathcal M}(x_\star))\to0\), and finite identification means \(x_k\in\mathcal M\) for every sufficiently large \(k\).

notation.meaning: active smooth manifold and its tangent space
distance between two subspaces induced by their orthogonal projectors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability criterion for an estimated VU smooth subspace near a partly smooth solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The estimated smooth subspaces \((U_k)\) are asymptotically reliable at \(x_\star\) when \(\operatorname{gap}(U_k,T_{\mathcal M}(x_\star))\to0\), where \(\operatorname{gap}(U,V)=\|P_U-P_V\|\). Identification is finite when there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in\mathcal M\) and \(\dim U_k=\dim T_{\mathcal M}(x_\star)\) for every \(k\ge K\). Thus reliability requires both angular consistency of the estimated subspace and eventual dimensional consistency; convergence of iterates alone does not establish identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subspace identification is reliable when estimated smooth subspaces converge in projector distance to the active tangent space, with matching eventual dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Identification Reliability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Partly smoothness and iterate convergence alone do not establish finite manifold or subspace identification; method-specific nondegeneracy and algorithmic hypotheses are required. The plain statement also omits the finite manifold-membership condition stated in LaTeX.

children.title: Large-Scale Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle architectures controlling memory, dimension, and structured information storage.

children.title: Limited-Memory Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods retaining a bounded information set.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), affine information consists of cuts \(\ell_i(x)=a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\).
A fixed memory bound \(M\in\mathbb{N}\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|B_k|\le M\) for every \(k\), while the trial point is computed from the model \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in B_k}\ell_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: indices of cuts retained at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory-bounded bundle architecture independent of a particular cut-retention rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a bundle \(B_0\) with \(|B_0|\le M\). At iteration \(k\), compute a trial point from the stabilized model \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in B_k}\ell_i(x)\). After evaluating the oracle at the trial point, insert its new cut. If the resulting bundle has more than \(M\) elements, retain at most \(M\) cuts according to a prescribed policy, which may protect the newest cut, active cuts, and an aggregate cut. Set the reduced collection to \(B_{k+1}\), so \(|B_k|\le M\) holds uniformly, and stop when the chosen stationarity or model-gap test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limited-memory bundle method uniformly bounds stored cuts, discarding or aggregating information after each oracle evaluation according to a specified retention rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the limited-memory container, but no source supports the proposed retention architecture or establishes which protected cuts and aggregation rules yield a valid bundle method.

children.title: Aggregate Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle methods compressing discarded information into aggregate elements.

assumptions_latex: The current cutting-plane model is \(m(x)=\max_{i\in B}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\).
At a bundle subproblem solution, multipliers satisfy \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(x)=a_{\mathrm{agg}}+\langle g_{\mathrm{agg}},x\rangle=\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i\ell_i(x)\le m(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex aggregation of affine cuts in a max-type bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(a_{\mathrm{agg}}=\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i a_i\) and \(g_{\mathrm{agg}}=\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i g_i\). The aggregate affine function is then \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(x)=a_{\mathrm{agg}}+\langle g_{\mathrm{agg}},x\rangle=\sum_{i\in B}\lambda_i\ell_i(x)\). Since a convex combination cannot exceed the largest component, \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(x)\le\max_{i\in B}\ell_i(x)=m(x)\) for every \(x\). An aggregate bundle method may therefore replace selected cuts by \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}\), preserving their multiplier-weighted first-order information while reducing storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate cut is the multiplier-weighted convex combination of stored affine cuts and lies below their pointwise maximum model.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-combination identity is correct and the representation fits the container, but no cited source supports its use as an aggregate bundle element or the claim about preserving the relevant first-order information.

children.title: Partially Separable Bundle Methods
children.top_down_role: Bundle architectures exploiting componentwise or chained structure.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

assumptions_latex: Each component oracle supplies local affine model information for \(f_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q m_{j,k}(P_jx)\), and component subgradients assemble as \(g_k=\sum_{j=1}^qP_j^{\mathsf T}g_{j,k}\).

notation.meaning: linear extraction map for component j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively partially separable objectives with componentwise bundle models.

source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an additively partially separable objective \(f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q f_j(P_jx)\), maintain a separate bundle model \(m_{j,k}\) for every component. The assembled model is \(m_k(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q m_{j,k}(P_jx)\). If \(g_{j,k}\) is selected from the component model at \(P_jx\), then the corresponding full-space first-order vector is \(g_k=\sum_{j=1}^qP_j^{\mathsf T}g_{j,k}\). After a trial evaluation, only bundles for evaluated or affected components need be updated; the output is the accepted center together with the component bundles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an additively partially separable objective, component bundle models sum to a full model, and component subgradients assemble through adjoint extraction maps.
knowledge_statements.title: Partially Separable Bundle Methods

source_witnesses.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

children.title: Nonconvex Bundle Model Management
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms governing model validity, trial acceptance, information retention, and stabilization parameters.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Essentials of Numerical Nonsmooth Optimization
