children.title: Local Convexification Management
children.top_down_role: Selection and adaptation of curvature corrections for nonconvex bundle models.

children.title: Fixed Convexification
children.top_down_role: Predetermined curvature correction.

assumptions_latex: A fixed parameter \(\gamma\ge\rho\) is chosen before the iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto f(x)+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|x\|^2\) is convex, and the center-relative model receives the correction \(\frac{\gamma}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global fixed quadratic correction for a weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex when \(x\mapsto f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x\|^2\) is convex. Hence any predetermined \(\gamma\ge\rho\) supplies a valid fixed convexification: \(x\mapsto f(x)+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|x\|^2\) is convex. In a bundle model centered at \(x_k\), the equivalent center-relative curvature correction is \(\frac{\gamma}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2\), up to an affine function of \(x\). The same \(\gamma\) is used at every iteration, independently of observed agreement between predicted and actual reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed parameter at least as large as the weak-convexity modulus gives a globally convex quadratic correction used unchanged at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Convexification

children.title: Adaptive Convexification
children.top_down_role: Curvature correction updated from observed model behavior.

assumptions_latex: A nonnegative convexification parameter \(\gamma_k\) and model \(m_k\) are available at iteration \(k\).
The trial point \(y_k\) has predicted reduction \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_{k+1}\) is increased after inadequate agreement and may be decreased after reliable agreement, subject to prescribed bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic ratio-controlled quadratic convexification update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(y_k\) from the current convexified model and define \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}=f(x_k)-f(y_k)\), \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)\), and \(r_k=\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}/\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\). Choose thresholds \(0\le\eta_1<\eta_2\le1\), factors \(\tau_+>1\) and \(0<\tau_-\le1\), and bounds \(0\le\underline\gamma\le\overline\gamma\). If \(r_k<\eta_1\), set \(\gamma_{k+1}=\min\{\tau_+\gamma_k,\overline\gamma\}\); if \(r_k>\eta_2\), set \(\gamma_{k+1}=\max\{\tau_-\gamma_k,\underline\gamma\}\); otherwise set \(\gamma_{k+1}=\gamma_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive convexification increases curvature after poor model agreement, decreases it after strong agreement, and otherwise leaves it unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Convexification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio-controlled update fits adaptive convexification, but its thresholds, parameter bounds, and increase/decrease rule are an uncited generic construction whose validity for a nonconvex bundle method is method-dependent.

children.title: Redistributed Convexification
children.top_down_role: Curvature correction encoded through adjusted bundle information.

assumptions_latex: At center \(x_k\), cut \(i\) has affine form \(\ell_i(x)=f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\).
A common curvature correction \(\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i(x)+\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2=\widetilde a_{i,k}+\langle\widetilde g_{i,k},x\rangle+\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|x\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic redistribution of a common quadratic correction into adjusted cut data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Expanding the center-relative correction gives \(\ell_i(x)+\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2=\widetilde a_{i,k}+\langle\widetilde g_{i,k},x\rangle+\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|x\|^2\), where \(\widetilde g_{i,k}=g_i-\gamma_kx_k\) and \(\widetilde a_{i,k}=f(x_i)-\langle g_i,x_i\rangle+\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|x_k\|^2\). Thus the center dependence of convexification can be encoded in adjusted bundle slopes and intercepts, leaving a common quadratic term. Redistributed convexification updates these adjusted data whenever \(x_k\) or \(\gamma_k\) changes, without changing the represented corrected cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A center-relative quadratic correction can be rewritten as a common quadratic plus adjusted cut slopes and intercepts.
knowledge_statements.title: Redistributed Convexification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic redistribution formula is correct and the representation fits the container, but no source establishes that this data transformation is the intended bundle-method notion of redistributed convexification.

children.title: Bundle Model-Validity Domain Calculus
children.top_down_role: Management of where and how collected first-order information remains trustworthy.

children.title: Locality-Measure Management
children.top_down_role: Spatial relevance metadata for bundle elements.

assumptions_latex: Each bundle element \(i\) was generated at \(x_i\) and is used at the current center \(x_k\).
A nonnegative locality measure \(s_{i,k}\) is assigned to every retained element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{i,k}=0\) for local information and larger \(s_{i,k}\) weakens, corrects, or removes increasingly remote information according to a fixed policy.

notation.meaning: locality measure of bundle element i at iteration k
generation point and current stability center

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract admissibility conditions for spatial relevance metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A locality-measure policy assigns \(s_{i,k}\in[0,+\infty]\) to each bundle element so that \(s_{i,k}=0\) when \(x_i=x_k\), and \(s_{i,k}\) does not decrease when the prescribed distance from \(x_i\) to \(x_k\) increases while other metadata are fixed. A model-management rule then uses \(s_{i,k}\) to downweight, downshift, or delete element \(i\), with \(s_{i,k}=+\infty\) denoting exclusion. A common admissible choice is \(s_{i,k}=\|x_i-x_k\|\), but scaled distances or combined spatial and model-error measures may be used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locality measure records how remote a cut is from the current center and controls its correction, weighting, or deletion.
knowledge_statements.title: Locality-Measure Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the asserted monotonicity condition, the infinity-as-exclusion convention, or the listed management actions. Locality measures in nonconvex bundle methods are method-specific and need a cited definition or policy.

children.title: Cut-Correction Management
children.top_down_role: Downshifting and related corrections for unreliable affine information.

assumptions_latex: The cut will be used on a trusted set \(D_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\ell_{i,k}(x)=\ell_i(x)-c_{i,k}\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D_k\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative downward correction applied to cut i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Downshift sufficient to make an affine cut valid on a trusted domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a computable correction satisfying \(c_{i,k}\ge\sup_{x\in D_k}(\ell_i(x)-f(x))_+\), where \((t)_+=\max\{t,0\}\). Define the corrected cut \(\widehat\ell_{i,k}(x)=\ell_i(x)-c_{i,k}\). Then \(\widehat\ell_{i,k}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D_k\). In implementations the supremum may be replaced by a certified upper bound obtained from weak convexity, locality data, or past oracle errors. Insert \(\widehat\ell_{i,k}\) into the bundle, and recompute or enlarge \(c_{i,k}\) whenever the trusted domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Downshift an unreliable affine cut by a certified error bound so that it underestimates the objective throughout the trusted domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Correction Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supremum bound tautologically yields a valid downshift, but no source supplies a computable certified bound or connects this construction to the intended nonconvex bundle cut-correction procedure.

children.title: Trusted Model-Domain Management
children.top_down_role: Restriction of model use to reliable neighborhoods.

assumptions_latex: A center \(x_k\), model \(m_k\), and trust radius \(\Delta_k>0\) are given.
A trial point is computed only within \(D_k=\{x:\|x-x_k\|\le\Delta_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\in D_k\), and \(\Delta_k\) is contracted after poor agreement and may be expanded after good boundary agreement.

notation.meaning: trusted model domain at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ball-shaped trusted domains governed by actual-to-predicted reduction agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(D_k=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|x-x_k\|\le\Delta_k\}\) and minimize the stabilized bundle model over \(D_k\) to obtain \(y_k\). For positive predicted reduction, compute \(r_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/(f(x_k)-m_k(y_k))\). If \(r_k\) is below a prescribed lower threshold, reject the center update and contract \(\Delta_k\). If \(r_k\) exceeds an upper threshold and \(y_k\) lies near the boundary of \(D_k\), the radius may be expanded; otherwise retain it. Model cuts are used only where their validity conditions hold inside the current trusted domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trial points are restricted to a trusted neighborhood whose radius contracts after poor model agreement and may expand after successful boundary steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Trusted Model-Domain Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement gives a generic trust-region update rather than a sourced bundle-specific model-validity-domain rule. Thresholds, contraction and expansion conditions, and cut-validity handling remain unspecified and method-dependent.

children.title: Bundle Step-Outcome Management Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Trial-outcome regimes distinguished by movement of the stability center and enrichment of the model.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Essentials of Numerical Nonsmooth Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Essentials of Numerical Nonsmooth Optimization

children.title: Serious-Step Management
children.top_down_role: Accepted updates of the stability center.

assumptions_latex: The current center is \(x_k\), the trial point is \(y_k\), and the predicted decrease \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) exactly when \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\ge\eta\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\); otherwise \(x_{k+1}=x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard actual-versus-predicted decrease test for updating a bundle stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute a trial point \(y_k\) and its predicted decrease \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\). Declare a serious step when \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\ge\eta\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\). On a serious step set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\), rebuild or translate center-dependent model data, and retain any cuts allowed by the memory policy. If the inequality fails, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\); this is not a serious step, although the trial-point oracle information may still be added to the bundle. Stop instead when the prescribed stationarity or vanishing-predicted-decrease test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A serious step moves the stability center to a trial point whose actual decrease reaches a fixed fraction of predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The serious-step test fits the container and is internally coherent, but no citation supports this exact predicted-decrease definition and acceptance rule for the intended deterministic nonconvex bundle family.

children.title: Null-Step Management
children.top_down_role: Model refinement without stability-center movement.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-step update for a stabilized finite-dimensional bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\) be the stability center, \(m_k\) a bundle model, and \(y_k\) a trial point with predicted decrease \(\Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\). Define \(\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/\Delta_k\). Given \(\eta_0\in(0,1)\), if \(\rho_k<\eta_0\), declare a null step and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Query \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)\), construct a localized or downshifted affine element \(\ell_k\) valid for the chosen nonconvex model, and update \(m_{k+1}=\max\{m_k,\ell_k\}\), possibly followed by aggregation or deletion. The stability center remains fixed while model information is refined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejected trial leaves the stability center unchanged but adds localized first-order information to improve the bundle model.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) admits the subgradient oracle used by the model.
The new affine element satisfies the model’s prescribed locality or downshift rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(m_{k+1}\) contains information generated at \(y_k\).
review_flags: Exact nonconvex cut-validity convention is method-dependent.
Bundle-method source with a null-step update theorem or algorithm is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Null-Step Management, but the decrease ratio, nonconvex affine-element validity, and model update are method-dependent. No citation supports the stated convention.

children.title: Fractional-Nonmonotone Step Management
children.top_down_role: Intermediate and nonmonotone acceptance regimes.

children.title: Fractional-Step Management
children.top_down_role: Management of intermediate stability-center movement after trial assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional-Step Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance of a proper fraction of a rejected or unsafe full trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_k=y_k-x_k\) and \(\Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\). Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\alpha_{\min}\in(0,1)\). Starting with \(\alpha=1\), replace \(\alpha\) by \(\beta\alpha\) until either \(f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\le f(x_k)-\eta\alpha\Delta_k\) or \(\alpha<\alpha_{\min}\). In the first case set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha d_k\); when \(0<\alpha<1\), classify the update as a fractional step. In the second case reject center movement and process the evaluated points as null-step model information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking accepts a proper fraction of the trial direction when it achieves a prescribed fraction of predicted decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite at every evaluated point.
The segment \(\{x_k+\alpha d_k:0\le\alpha\le1\}\) lies in the trial domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\eta\alpha\Delta_k\) for some \(\alpha\in[\alpha_{\min},1]\), or no center movement occurs.
review_flags: Fractional-step tests vary across nonconvex bundle methods.
A source fixing the intended scaling of predicted decrease is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Fractional-Step Management, but scaling the full-step predicted decrease by alpha is not a universal bundle-method rule. A method-specific source is required.

children.title: Nonmonotone-Step Management
children.top_down_role: Management of accepted trials relative to nonmonotone reference values.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone-Step Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory nonmonotone acceptance relative to a reference objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a memory length \(q\ge1\) and define \(R_k=\max\{f(x_j):\max(0,k-q+1)\le j\le k\}\). For a trial point \(y_k\) with predicted decrease \(\Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\), fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and accept a nonmonotone serious step when \(f(y_k)\le R_k-\eta\Delta_k\), setting \(x_{k+1}=y_k\). Otherwise retain \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and perform a null-step model update. The test may accept \(f(x_{k+1})>f(x_k)\), but every accepted value remains below the current reference by the required model-based margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial may increase the current objective, provided it decreases a finite-memory reference value by a model-based margin.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x_j)\) is finite for every stored center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies \(f(x_{k+1})\le R_k-\eta\Delta_k<R_k\).

notation.meaning: Predicted decrease at the trial point.

review_flags: Multiple inequivalent nonmonotone reference sequences exist.
A source identifying the intended bundle acceptance test is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but this particular finite-memory maximum and acceptance margin are only one possible nonmonotone scheme and lack source support.

children.title: Intermediate-Acceptance Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Controls preventing unreliable progress under intermediate acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate-Acceptance Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions preventing unsafe acceptance of fractional or nonmonotone trial points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k=x_k+\alpha_k(y_k-x_k)\), where \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), and let \(R_k\ge f(x_k)\) be the current acceptance reference. For constants \(\alpha_{\min}>0\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and localization radius \(r_k>0\), intermediate acceptance is safeguarded by the simultaneous conditions \[\alpha_k\ge\alpha_{\min},\qquad f(z_k)\le R_k-\eta\alpha_k\Delta_k,\qquad \|z_k-x_k\|\le r_k,\] where \(\Delta_k>0\) is the full-trial predicted decrease. If any condition fails, \(z_k\) cannot become the next stability center; its oracle information may still refine the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intermediate point is accepted only with sufficient step size, reference decrease, and localization; otherwise it supplies model information only.
assumptions_latex: All points in the tested segment belong to the oracle domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of any safeguard forces \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) for this acceptance attempt.
review_flags: The displayed safeguards form a coherent generic specification, not a uniquely standard rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is appropriate for this leaf, but the simultaneous step-size, decrease, and localization requirements are a constructed generic specification rather than a sourced safeguard for the target method family.

children.title: Bundle Information Management
children.top_down_role: Selection, aggregation, deletion, and rebuilding of accumulated model information.

children.title: Bundle-Element Selection
children.top_down_role: Retention based on activity, locality, or model relevance.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Element Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite bundle retention preserving active, recent, and aggregate model information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the model as \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(x)\). Given a capacity \(B\ge3\), form a retained index set \(J_k\subseteq I_k\) containing one index active at the center, the newest oracle element, and any mandatory aggregate element. Fill remaining positions, up to \(|J_k|\le B\), by decreasing relevance score \[s_i=w_a\mathbf{1}_{\{\ell_i(x_k)=m_k(x_k)\}}-w_d\|y_i-x_k\|-w_e a_i,\] where \(y_i\) is the sampling point and \(a_i\ge0\) its locality error. Replace the bundle model by \(m_k^{\mathrm{sel}}(x)=\max_{i\in J_k}\ell_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep mandatory active, newest, and aggregate elements, then use activity and locality scores to fill a bounded bundle.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is at least the number of mandatory retained elements.
Every element has recorded sampling and locality data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|J_k|\le B\), and every mandatory model element remains represented.

notation.meaning: Current and retained bundle index sets.

review_flags: Selection scores and mandatory elements are implementation-dependent.
A bundle-management source is required for the intended retention invariant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Bundle-Element Selection, but the mandatory set and relevance score are method-dependent. The weights w_a, w_d, and w_e are also introduced without sign or domain conditions.

children.title: Bundle Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Compression of accumulated primal-dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-weighted compression preserving first-order information at a model subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\), with \(\ell_i(x)=a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\), and let \(y\) solve a stabilized model subproblem. Suppose its optimality system supplies multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1\) and \(\lambda_i>0\) only when \(\ell_i(y)=m(y)\). Define \[\bar g=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i,\qquad \bar a=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i a_i,\qquad \bar\ell(x)=\bar a+\langle\bar g,x\rangle.\] Then \(\bar\ell(y)=m(y)\), and \(\bar g\in\partial m(y)\). Thus one aggregate element preserves the active model value and dual-weighted slope at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex combination of active cutting planes forms one aggregate plane preserving the model value and subgradient at the subproblem solution.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and every \(\ell_i\) is affine.
The multipliers are nonnegative and sum to one.
Positive multipliers are supported only on planes active at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\ell(y)=m(y)\) and \(\bar g\in\partial m(y)\).
review_flags: Standard finite-max aggregation identity, but no supplied locator supports bundle aggregation.
A direct authoritative source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Bundle Aggregation and the finite-max aggregation statement is mathematically standard, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Bundle Deletion-Restart Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Removal of stale information and reconstruction of unreliable models.

children.title: Bundle Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal of stale, redundant, or unreliable bundle elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-limited deletion that preserves mandatory model information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_k\) index the current bundle and let \(M_k\subseteq I_k\) contain the newest oracle element, every protected aggregate element, and at least one element active at the stability center \(x_k\). Given capacity \(B\ge|M_k|\), delete indices only from \(I_k\setminus M_k\), in nondecreasing order of a prescribed relevance score, until the retained set \(J_k\) satisfies \(|J_k|\le B\). Set \(m_k^{+}(x)=\max_{i\in J_k}\ell_i(x)\). Deletion is permitted only when the model’s locality and validity invariants continue to hold for all retained elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete the least relevant unprotected elements until capacity is met, while preserving active, newest, aggregate, and validity information.
assumptions_latex: The relevance ordering is deterministic after tie breaking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k\subseteq J_k\subseteq I_k\), \(|J_k|\le B\), and protected model information is retained.
review_flags: Protected-set requirements depend on the convergence analysis.
No direct deletion rule is supported by the supplied locators.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Bundle Deletion, but the protected elements and retained-model validity requirements depend on a particular convergence analysis and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Bundle Restart
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction of the working bundle after model reliability deteriorates.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Restart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reinitialization of stale or inconsistent bundle information at the current center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a restart iteration \(k\), keep the stability center \(x_k\), query or retain \(f(x_k)\) and \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), and discard all bundle elements not certified for the new local model. Construct a fresh center element \(\ell_k\) satisfying \(\ell_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), set \(I_{k+1}=\{k\}\) and \(m_{k+1}=\ell_k\), and reset the stabilization parameter to a prescribed admissible value. Optionally retain one aggregate element only if its validity at \(x_k\) is independently certified. The restart changes model memory but not the current stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart discards stale bundle memory, rebuilds the model at the current center, and resets stabilization without moving the center.
assumptions_latex: A valid oracle element can be constructed at \(x_k\).
The reset stabilization parameter lies in its admissible range.
Any retained aggregate element is certified for the restarted model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and the restarted bundle contains only newly valid or explicitly certified information.
review_flags: Restart contents and parameter resets are method-specific.
A convergence-compatible restart source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Bundle Restart, but restart contents and parameter resetting require method-specific support. Setting the restarted index set to a singleton also conflicts with the subsequent option to retain an aggregate unless that alternative is stated separately.

children.title: Deletion-to-Restart Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguishing selective pruning from full reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion-to-Restart Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between safe selective deletion and full model reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\) denote the mandatory bundle indices required to preserve center activity, the newest oracle information, aggregation, and local model validity. Selective deletion is admissible only if there exists \(J_k\) such that \[P_k\subseteq J_k\subseteq I_k,\qquad |J_k|\le B,\qquad \mathcal V(J_k,x_k)=1,\] where \(\mathcal V\) is the method’s model-validity predicate. If no such \(J_k\) exists, or if retained elements have incompatible locality data after a center or parameter change, deletion cannot guarantee the required invariant and a restart is triggered. Thus infeasibility of the retention predicate is the deletion-to-restart boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion is safe only when a capacity-feasible retained bundle preserves all invariants; otherwise the model must be restarted.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V\) is a verifiable validity predicate for the chosen model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists J_k\) satisfying the retention predicate implies restart rather than further deletion.

notation.meaning: Mandatory indices for convergence and validity.

review_flags: The validity predicate must be instantiated for a specific nonconvex bundle method.
No supplied source identifies a canonical deletion-to-restart boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure-boundary is the correct content kind, but the abstract predicate makes the claim largely procedural, and no source establishes infeasibility of this retention predicate as the intended restart trigger.

children.title: Stabilization-Parameter Management
children.top_down_role: Adaptive control of proximity strength, localization size, model levels, and tolerances.

children.title: Proximal-Weight Management
children.top_down_role: Adjustment of proximity control using model performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Weight Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio-based adjustment of the quadratic proximal stabilization weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given center \(x_k\), model \(m_k\), and weight \(t_k>0\), compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{t_k}{2}\|x-x_k\|^2\right\}.\] Let \(\Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\) and \(\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/\Delta_k\). Choose \(0<\eta_0<\eta_1<1\) and factors \(\gamma_+>1\), \(\gamma_-\in(0,1)\). Set \(t_{k+1}=\gamma_+t_k\) when \(\rho_k<\eta_0\), set \(t_{k+1}=\gamma_-t_k\) when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), and otherwise set \(t_{k+1}=t_k\), with projection onto prescribed positive bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poor model agreement increases proximal regularization, strong agreement decreases it, and intermediate agreement leaves it unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The stabilized model subproblem has a minimizer.
The admissible weight interval is contained in \((0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_{k+1}\) remains positive and responds monotonically to the agreement class.
review_flags: Some bundle conventions use the reciprocal proximal parameter, reversing updates.
A source fixing the chapter’s parameter convention is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Proximal-Weight Management, but reciprocal parameter conventions reverse the updates, and stabilized bundle methods may include the quadratic term in predicted reduction. A source fixing both conventions is required.

children.title: Trust-Region Radius Management
children.top_down_role: Adjustment of explicit localization size.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Radius Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement-ratio update of an explicit bundle-model localization radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given radius \(r_k>0\), compute a trial point \(y_k\) by minimizing the bundle model over \(\|x-x_k\|\le r_k\). For predicted decrease \(\Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\), set \(\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/\Delta_k\). Choose \(0<\eta_0<\eta_1<1\), \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\), and bounds \(0<r_{\min}\le r_{\max}\). If \(\rho_k<\eta_0\), shrink the radius; if \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\) and \(\|y_k-x_k\|=r_k\), enlarge it; otherwise retain it. Project every update onto \([r_{\min},r_{\max}]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrink the trust region after poor agreement and enlarge it after strong agreement at an active boundary.
assumptions_latex: The trust-region model subproblem has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{k+1}\in[r_{\min},r_{\max}]\), with contraction after poor agreement and conditional expansion after strong agreement.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

review_flags: The locator supports general trust-region management; compatibility with a nonconvex bundle model remains to be checked.

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited locator concerns general trust-region methods, but it does not yet support this exact nonsmooth nonconvex bundle-model ratio and radius update. Full-text, bundle-compatible evidence is required.

children.title: Level-Tolerance Management Coupling
children.top_down_role: Adjustment of model levels and admissible approximation errors.

children.title: Level Management
children.top_down_role: Adjustment of target levels used by stabilized bundle models.

knowledge_statements.title: Level Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-based update of a model level between lower and upper objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a lower estimate \(L_k\) and an incumbent upper value \(U_k\) with \(L_k<U_k\). For fixed \(\theta\in(0,1)\), define the target level \(\ell_k=L_k+\theta(U_k-L_k)\) and compute a localized point satisfying \(m_k(y_k)\le\ell_k\), typically by minimizing distance to the stability center over this level set. If evaluation yields a better incumbent, set \(U_{k+1}=\min\{U_k,f(y_k)\}\). If the model level set is certified empty, raise the lower estimate without exceeding \(\ell_k\). Otherwise retain the bounds and refine the model. Recompute the level after every bound change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a model level inside the current bound gap, lowering the upper bound after success or raising the lower bound after certified infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k<U_k\) are valid lower and upper estimates for the managed subproblem.
Level-set infeasibility is certified by the model subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le L_{k+1}\le U_{k+1}\le U_k\), and each new level lies strictly inside every positive updated gap.

notation.meaning: Current lower and upper objective estimates.

review_flags: Global lower bounds may be unavailable in weakly convex nonconvex variants.
A source specifying the intended local or global level interpretation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Level Management, but valid global lower bounds and certified empty model level sets are not generally available in weakly convex nonconvex variants. The intended local or global level scheme needs a source.

children.title: Tolerance Management
children.top_down_role: Adjustment of admissible model, oracle, or subproblem inaccuracies.

assumptions_latex: The tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_k>0\), and fixed constants obey \(0<\theta_-<1<\theta_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow 0\) along unsuccessful refinements, while tolerances are not tightened after a step meeting the prescribed model test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deterministic tolerance policy; exact acceptance tests depend on the bundle variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), \(L_k\), and \(\varepsilon_k\), compute a trial point whose model residual satisfies \(r_k\leq\varepsilon_k\). If the trial point fails the prescribed level or model-adequacy test because the subproblem was solved too coarsely, set \(\varepsilon_{k+1}=\theta_-\varepsilon_k\) and resolve without changing the stability center. If the test succeeds, accept the algorithm's serious or null-step decision and choose \(\varepsilon_{k+1}\leq\theta_+\varepsilon_k\). Require \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) on every infinite subsequence of unresolved or null refinements. Stop when \(r_k\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\), where \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}>0\) is the requested stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighten the model-solution tolerance after inadequate trials, permit controlled relaxation after successful tests, and force tolerances to vanish along infinite refinement sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the tolerance-management leaf, but no source identifies a bundle variant supporting these update, refinement, relaxation, and stopping rules. The stationarity tolerance is also used without being included in the notation, and the asserted behavior on null refinements is variant-dependent.

children.title: Level-Tolerance Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination between target levels and acceptable approximation quality.

assumptions_latex: The model subproblem is solved with objective or residual error at most \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_k\leq\eta\Delta_k\) makes subproblem error a fixed fraction of the current level gap.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative accuracy condition coupling level reduction and inner model-solution error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A level and tolerance pair is coupled with fraction \(\eta\in(0,1)\) when \[0<\varepsilon_k\leq\eta\Delta_k,\qquad \Delta_k:=f(x_k)-L_k.\] Consequently, whenever \(\Delta_k\to0\), the associated tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_k\to0\). If a computed trial has residual \(r_k>\eta\Delta_k\), it is classified as insufficiently accurate and the tolerance must be reduced before the trial is used to update the stability center or level. This condition separates genuine failure of the current level from failure caused solely by an inaccurate model-subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound each subproblem tolerance by a fixed fraction of the current level gap, so shrinking levels automatically force increasingly accurate model solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Level-Tolerance Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the coupling leaf, but no cited source supports the specific fraction rule or the claim that a residual exceeding the fraction must trigger resolution before any update. The residual is also not defined in this record, and objective-error and residual-error interpretations are blended.

children.title: Nonconvex Bundle Stationarity Targets
children.top_down_role: Criticality notions selected according to objective regularity, model family, and oracle access.

children.title: Clarke Criticality Targets
children.top_down_role: Criticality for locally Lipschitz black-box models.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The target is \(0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)\), or approximately \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_C f(x))\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Clarke subdifferential of the locally Lipschitz objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained finite-dimensional Clarke stationarity for locally Lipschitz objectives.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109
source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Clarke subdifferential at \(x\) is \[\partial_C f(x):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle v,d\rangle\leq f^{\circ}(x;d)\ \text{for every }d\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.\] A point \(\bar x\) is Clarke critical when \(0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)\), equivalently \(f^{\circ}(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(\varepsilon>0\), an \(\varepsilon\)-Clarke-critical target is any \(x\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_C f(x))\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz objective is Clarke critical when its Clarke subdifferential contains zero; approximate criticality bounds the distance from zero to that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Criticality Targets

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Relationship Between Quasidifferential and Clarke Subdifferential p. 109
source_witnesses.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

children.title: Limiting-Subdifferential Criticality Targets
children.top_down_role: Criticality for variationally regular nonconvex objectives.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The target is \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\), with sequential approximate form \(x_i\to\bar x\), \(f(x_i)\to f(\bar x)\), and \(v_i\in\widehat\partial f(x_i)\), \(v_i\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting stationarity for proper lower-semicontinuous objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The limiting subdifferential is \[\partial f(\bar x):=\left\{v:\begin{array}{l}\text{there exist }x_i\to\bar x,\ f(x_i)\to f(\bar x),\ v_i\to v,\\ v_i\in\widehat\partial f(x_i)\end{array}\right\}.\] The point \(\bar x\) is limiting-subdifferential critical when \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Equivalently, there are sequences \(x_i\to\bar x\) and \(v_i\in\widehat\partial f(x_i)\) such that \(f(x_i)\to f(\bar x)\) and \(v_i\to0\). An approximate target requires such nearby pairs with both \(\|x_i-ar x\|\) and \(\|v_i\|\) below prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting criticality means that zero is a limiting subgradient, witnessed by nearby Fréchet subgradients converging to zero with matching function values.
knowledge_statements.title: Limiting-Subdifferential Criticality Targets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact limiting-subdifferential definition is standard, but no authoritative locator is supplied. The approximate target is not formulated with explicit finite tolerances or quantifiers, and its displayed norm contains the malformed expression \(x_i-ar x\). Source support is needed before selecting a precise corrected formulation.

children.title: Proximal-Model Criticality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Criticality expressed through proximal points, model residuals, or decrements.

children.title: Proximal Criticality Targets
children.top_down_role: Criticality targets expressed through proximal points or proximal residuals.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal criticality target is \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\), and exact criticality is equivalent to \(x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau-envelope stationarity for finite-dimensional weakly convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[P_\lambda(x):=\mathop{\arg\min}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\},\qquad G_\lambda(x):=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x)).\] Weak convexity and \(\lambda<1/\rho\) make \(P_\lambda(x)\) single-valued, and the Moreau envelope satisfies \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=G_\lambda(x)\). The point \(x\) meets the \(\varepsilon\)-proximal criticality target when \(\|G_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\). Exact proximal criticality means \(G_\lambda(x)=0\), equivalently \(x=P_\lambda(x)\), and then \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal criticality is measured by the Moreau-envelope gradient, equivalently the scaled displacement from a point to its proximal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Criticality Targets

children.title: Model Criticality Targets
children.top_down_role: Criticality targets expressed through local model residuals or decrements.

assumptions_latex: For a center \(x\), the model \(m_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The stabilization parameter satisfies \(t>0\), and the proximal model subproblem has a minimizer \(y_t(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model criticality is measured by \(R_t^m(x):=t^{-1}(x-y_t(x))\), with target \(\|R_t^m(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: bundle model based at the stability center

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal residual target for a convex bundle model at a fixed stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), define \[y_t(x)\in\mathop{\arg\min}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_x(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\|y-x\|^2\right\},\qquad R_t^m(x):=t^{-1}(x-y_t(x)).\] The point \(x\) satisfies the \(\varepsilon\)-model-criticality target when \(\|R_t^m(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\). The proximal optimality condition gives \(R_t^m(x)\in\partial m_x(y_t(x))\). Thus \(R_t^m(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(y_t(x)=x\), and, when the model is base-point exact, it identifies stationarity of the model at its stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model criticality uses the scaled displacement between the stability center and the proximal minimizer of its convex bundle model.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Criticality Targets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role is suitable, and the convex proximal-model residual and its optimality inclusion are mathematically plausible. However, no source supports this as the intended bundle-model criticality convention. Moreover, zero residual already characterizes stationarity of the convex model at the center; base-point exactness is not what establishes that model-stationarity equivalence.

children.title: Proximal-to-Model Criticality Translation
children.top_down_role: Connections between proximal evidence and model-based criticality evidence.

assumptions_latex: The model is base-point exact and satisfies \(f(y)\leq m_x(y)+(\kappa/2)\|y-x\|^2\) for every relevant \(y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate residual translation under a global quadratic upper-model error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_t(x):=\operatorname{prox}_{tf}(x)\) and let \(y_t(x)\) minimize the stabilized model. Under the stated quadratic model-error bound and \(t\kappa<1\), the candidate residual comparison is \[\|G_t(x)\|\leq\frac{1}{1-t\kappa}\|R_t^m(x)\|.\] Hence an \(\varepsilon\)-model-critical center is a \(\varepsilon/(1-t\kappa)\)-proximal-critical point. In particular, if \(R_t^m(x_k)\to0\) along centers for which the same \(t\) and \(\kappa\) apply, then \(G_t(x_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform quadratic model-error bound translates a small model proximal residual into a controlled true proximal residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-to-Model Criticality Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf calls for a proximal-to-model translation, but the stated one-sided model-error bound does not transparently yield the claimed residual inequality or its constant. No source is provided for the orientation of the bound, the required locality or globality, or additional model assumptions. The result may ultimately be a theorem rather than a generic property, depending on the sourced formulation.

children.title: Bundle Model Adequacy Principle
children.top_down_role: Model-quality families connecting bundle information with local objective behavior.

children.title: Base-Point Model Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Model agreement at the current stability center.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is finite at the stability center \(x\).
The bundle model \(m_x:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is defined at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Base-point adequacy is the interpolation condition \(m_x(x)=f(x)\).

notation.meaning: bundle model based at the center

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zeroth-order agreement of a bundle model with the objective at its stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model \(m_x\) is base-point adequate for \(f\) at \(x\) when \[m_x(x)=f(x).\] If the model is assembled as a maximum of cutting functions \(a_i\), so that \(m_x(y)=\max_{i\in I}a_i(y)\), base-point adequacy additionally requires at least one active exactness element \(i_x\in I\) satisfying \(a_{i_x}(x)=f(x)\), while every element obeys \(a_i(x)\leq f(x)\). The equality is a model invariant at the current stability center and does not by itself impose first-order or neighborhood accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bundle model is base-point adequate when it reproduces the objective value exactly at the current stability center.
knowledge_statements.title: Base-Point Model Adequacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and interpolation equality fit base-point model adequacy. However, the additional assertion that every cutting element underestimates the objective at the center does not follow merely from representing the model as a maximum; it requires a particular cutting-plane convention. A source is needed to establish that convention and the exact scope.

children.title: First-Order Model Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Consistency with admissible generalized first-order information.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and model \(m_x\) are proper and lower semicontinuous near \(x\).
Both functions are finite at \(x\), and \(m_x(x)=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order adequacy is \(\partial m_x(x)\subseteq\partial f(x)\), with equality when complete first-order agreement is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient consistency of the bundle model with admissible objective information at the center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A base-point-exact model is first-order adequate at \(x\) if every model subgradient active at the center is admissible objective information: \[\partial m_x(x)\subseteq\partial f(x).\] Equivalently, each \(g\in\partial m_x(x)\) must be a limiting subgradient of \(f\) at \(x\). Complete first-order agreement strengthens the inclusion to \(\partial m_x(x)=\partial f(x)\). For a locally Lipschitz objective and a convex model, a Clarke variant replaces the right-hand side by \(\partial_C f(x)\). The chosen subdifferential must remain fixed throughout a convergence statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order adequacy requires every model subgradient active at the center to be legitimate generalized first-order information for the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Model Adequacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but the limiting-subdifferential inclusion is not a convention-free definition of first-order model adequacy. For nonconvex objectives, convex-model subgradients are often compared with Clarke or other model-specific generalized subdifferentials, and the limiting subdifferential need not be convex. The limiting and Clarke variants therefore require separate sourced hypotheses rather than being combined here.

children.title: Localized-Strict Model Adequacy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood and sequential model-quality regimes used in global convergence.

children.title: Localized Model Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Model quality restricted to trusted neighborhoods of relevant base points.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite near a fixed center \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Localized adequacy is \(f(y)\leq m_x(y)+\omega_x(\|y-x\|)\) locally, where \(\omega_x(t)/t\to0\).

notation.meaning: model based at the fixed center

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided first-order model accuracy near a fixed stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model is locally adequate at the fixed center \(x\) if there exist \(r_x>0\) and a function \(\omega_x:[0,r_x]\to[0,+\infty)\) such that \[f(y)\leq m_x(y)+\omega_x(\|y-x\|)\quad\text{whenever }\|y-x\|\leq r_x,\qquad \lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\omega_x(t)}{t}=0.\] Equivalently, \(f(y)-m_x(y)=o(\|y-x\|)\) from above as \(y\to x\), with the center held fixed. The radius and modulus may depend on \(x\); no uniformity over moving centers is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed center, the model upper-approximates the objective up to an error that is little-o of the distance to that center.
knowledge_statements.title: Localized Model Adequacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role matches localized model adequacy, and the fixed-center one-sided little-o statement is internally coherent. No source is supplied, however, to confirm that this upper-model orientation and modulus formulation are the intended adequacy convention for the surrounding nonconvex bundle framework.

children.title: Strict Model Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Stronger sequential model-quality behavior used in global convergence analysis.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite near \(\bar x\).
A model \(m_x\) is available for every center \(x\) near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict adequacy requires \(f(y_k)-m_{x_k}(y_k)\leq o(\|y_k-x_k\|)\) uniformly for all \(x_k,y_k\to\bar x\).

notation.meaning: model based at a moving center

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform one-sided first-order accuracy for trial points and stability centers approaching the same reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model family is strictly adequate at \(\bar x\) if there exist \(r>0\) and \(\omega:[0,r]\to[0,+\infty)\) with \(\omega(t)/t\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that \[f(y)\leq m_x(y)+\omega(\|y-x\|)\] whenever \(x,y\in B_r(\bar x)\). Equivalently, for every pair of sequences \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(y_k\to\bar x\), with \(x_k\neq y_k\), \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{f(y_k)-m_{x_k}(y_k)}{\|y_k-x_k\|}\leq0.\] Unlike localized adequacy, the estimate is uniform over moving centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict adequacy makes the little-o upper-model error uniform when both stability centers and trial points approach the reference point.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Model Adequacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits strict adequacy, but the two formulations are not equivalent as written. A single modulus depending only on \(\|y-x\|\) for every pair in one fixed ball controls arbitrarily close pairs away from the reference point, whereas the sequential condition only concerns centers and trials jointly approaching the reference point. A source is needed to determine the intended uniform formulation and hypotheses.

children.title: Localization-to-Strictness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating local validity from stronger sequential adequacy.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every fixed-center model is locally adequate, but the model family is not strictly adequate at \(0\).

notation.meaning: affine first-order model at the center

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiability gives pointwise adequacy but does not supply uniform strict adequacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is differentiable at every \(x\), so for each fixed center \(x\), \[f(y)-m_x(y)=o(|y-x|)\quad\text{as }y\to x.\] Thus the affine model is locally adequate at every fixed center. However, let \(x_k=((2k+1)\pi)^{-1/2}\) and \(y_k=0\). Then \(x_k,y_k\to0\), \(f(x_k)=0\), \(f'(x_k)=2/x_k\), and \(m_{x_k}(0)=-2\). Consequently, \[\frac{f(y_k)-m_{x_k}(y_k)}{|y_k-x_k|}=\frac{2}{x_k}\to+\infty.\] Hence strict adequacy at \(0\) fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise differentiability ensures localized affine-model accuracy, yet oscillating derivatives can destroy the uniform moving-center estimate required for strict adequacy.
knowledge_statements.title: Localization-to-Strictness Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role exactly fits the boundary leaf, and the derivative calculation and chosen sequences support the claimed failure of moving-center strict adequacy while preserving fixed-center differentiability. Nevertheless, this nontrivial counterexample has no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale, so it cannot be accepted under the evidence contract.

children.title: Global Convergence to Nonsmooth Criticality
children.top_down_role: Convergence families distinguished by accepted-step behavior, model refinement, and objective geometry.

children.title: Serious-Step Subsequence Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence conclusions organized around accepted stability-center updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Subsequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence of accepted centers for a weakly convex proximal bundle scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, bounded below on the initial level set, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex. At serious iteration \(k\), let \(y_k\) minimize \(m_k(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x_k\|^2\), where \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), and define \(\Delta_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)-(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y_k-x_k\|^2\). If acceptance ensures \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\geq\eta\Delta_k\) with \(\eta>0\), and infinitely many serious steps occur, then along their indices \(S\), \(\sum_{k\in S}\Delta_k<\infty\), \(\Delta_k\to0\), and \(\|y_k-x_k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted centers have summable predicted reductions; consequently, predicted reductions and accepted displacements vanish along the serious-step subsequence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, weakly convex, and bounded below on the relevant level set.
\(0<\lambda<1/\rho\) and every trial subproblem has a minimizer.
Serious steps satisfy the stated fixed-fraction decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k\in S}\Delta_k<\infty\), \(\Delta_k\to0\), and \(\|y_k-x_k\|\to0\) along \(S\).

notation.meaning: bundle model at the current center

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this bundle-specific theorem. The telescoping argument additionally requires the serious-step update relation, such as x_{k+1}=y_k, while vanishing displacement requires a stated curvature condition relating Delta_k to ||y_k-x_k||^2; interpolation alone does not provide it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing of BT Quantities Under Infinitely Many Serious Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific subsequence convergence for the convex BT algorithm. Conditions (3.39) and the serious-step rule (3.36) are retained symbolically because their definitions lie outside the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If condition \((3.39)\) holds and infinitely many Serious Steps are made in \((3.36)\), then there exists a subsequence \(\{k(i)\}\) such that \(\lim_{i\to\infty}z_{k(i)}=0\) and \(\lim_{i\to\infty}\sigma_{k(i)}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under condition (3.39), if the update rule (3.36) makes infinitely many Serious Steps, then z and sigma both converge to zero along a suitable subsequence.
assumptions_latex: \text{Infinitely many Serious Steps are made in }(3.36).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\{k(i)\}:\quad \lim_{i\to\infty}z_{k(i)}=0\quad\text{and}\quad\lim_{i\to\infty}\sigma_{k(i)}=0.

children.title: Null-Step Model-Refinement Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence driven by repeated improvement of a fixed-center model.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Model-Refinement Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-center convergence under monotone, asymptotically exact bundle refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a center \(x\) and \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). Let \(m_j\leq f\), \(m_j(x)=f(x)\), and \(m_{j+1}\geq m_j\), and set \(J_j=\inf_y\{m_j(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\}\). Suppose every null step adds an exact oracle cut at a minimizer \(y_j\), the stabilized objectives are uniformly strongly convex, and the refinement is asymptotically exact in the sense that \(f(y_j)-m_j(y_j)\to0\). Then \(J_j\uparrow f_\lambda(x)\), where \(f_\lambda(x)=\inf_y\{f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\}\), and every cluster point of \((y_j)\) is a proximal point of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed center, monotone exact refinement makes stabilized model values converge to the true proximal value and trial points approach proximal minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The stabilized model objectives are uniformly strongly convex.
The oracle discrepancy \(f(y_j)-m_j(y_j)\) tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_j\uparrow f_\lambda(x)\), and every cluster point of \((y_j)\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\}\).

notation.meaning: optimal stabilized-model value after refinement j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The result fits the fixed-center refinement container, but no source identifies a nonconvex bundle model class for which the monotonicity, exact-cut, uniform-strong-convexity, and asymptotic-exactness hypotheses hold together.

children.title: Cluster-Point Criticality
children.top_down_role: Criticality conclusions for accumulation points.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Point Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting criticality from vanishing proximal-model residuals and outer semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\) be bounded and let \(y_k-x_k\to0\). Suppose vectors \(g_k\) and residuals \(r_k\) satisfy \(g_k+(y_k-x_k)/\lambda=r_k\), \(r_k\to0\), and \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)+e_k\mathbb{B}\) with \(e_k\to0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and \(\partial f\) is the limiting subdifferential. If \(f(y_k)\to f(\bar x)\) whenever \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\), then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\) satisfies \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing steps, subproblem residuals, and model-to-function subgradient errors imply that every value-consistent accumulation point is limiting-critical.
assumptions_latex: The residual and subgradient-transfer errors satisfy \(r_k\to0\) and \(e_k\to0\).
Function values are consistent along convergent subsequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\) for every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The limiting-subdifferential argument is plausible, but no source is cited. The domain of lambda must be stated, and value consistency should explicitly read f(y_{k_j})→f(bar x) along every subsequence x_{k_j}→bar x.

children.title: Full-Sequence Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Additional geometric regimes supporting convergence of the entire sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Sequence Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL-based upgrade from subsequential criticality to convergence of all accepted centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let the bounded serious-center sequence \((x_k)\) satisfy \(f(x_{k+1})+a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\leq f(x_k)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\leq b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\) for constants \(a,b>0\). If \(f\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property on the cluster set and function values are continuous along that set, then \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty\). Consequently, the entire serious-center sequence converges to one point \(x_\star\) satisfying \(0\in\partial f(x_\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under sufficient decrease, a relative-error bound, boundedness, and KL geometry, all serious centers converge to one critical point with finite total length.
assumptions_latex: The serious-center sequence is bounded and satisfies sufficient decrease.
\(f\) has the KL property on the cluster set with value continuity there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty\), \(x_k\to x_\star\), and \(0\in\partial f(x_\star)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a full-sequence KL convergence theorem of the correct kind, but its precise uniformization, continuity, relative-error, finite-length, and criticality hypotheses require an inspectable KL convergence source.

children.title: Bundle Termination-Quality Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Computable indicators of model quality, trial-point quality, and approximate criticality.

children.title: Predicted-Reduction Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates obtained from stabilized-model improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Predicted-Reduction Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable certificate from the optimal value of a stabilized bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a model satisfying \(m(x)=f(x)\), and let \(y\) minimize \(m(z)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|z-x\|^2\) for \(\lambda>0\). Define \(\Delta=f(x)-m(y)-(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\). Comparison with the feasible point \(z=x\) gives \(\Delta\geq0\). If the stabilized model is \(\mu\)-strongly convex, then \(\Delta\geq(\mu/2)\|y-x\|^2\). Thus the displayed optimal value certifies both model improvement and, when \(\Delta\leq\varepsilon\), the step bound \(\|y-x\|\leq\sqrt{2\varepsilon/\mu}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilized subproblem value yields a nonnegative predicted reduction and converts a small reduction into a verifiable small-step certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(m(x)=f(x)\) and the stabilized subproblem attains its minimum.
The stabilized model is \(\mu\)-strongly convex for the displacement bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta\geq(\mu/2)\|y-x\|^2\geq0\); hence \(\Delta\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(\|y-x\|\leq\sqrt{2\varepsilon/\mu}\).

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of the stabilized model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and its strong-convexity estimate are mathematically standard and fit the terminal container, but the nontrivial certificate claim has no cited source or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Aggregate-Subgradient Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates obtained from compressed dual bundle information.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Subgradient Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual compression certificate for a finite max-of-cuts bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(z)=\max_{1\leq i\leq p}\{a_i+\langle g_i,z\rangle\}\), and suppose \(y\) minimizes \(m(z)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|z-x\|^2\). There exist multipliers \(\alpha_i\geq0\), supported on cuts active at \(y\), with \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), such that the aggregate vector \(\bar g=\sum_i\alpha_i g_i\) satisfies \(\bar g+(y-x)/\lambda=0\). More generally, computed multipliers certify residual \(r=\bar g+(y-x)/\lambda\). The tuple \((\alpha,\bar g,r)\) is directly checkable from stored cuts, and \(\|r\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-accurate subproblem stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex multipliers on active cuts compress the bundle into one aggregate subgradient whose proximal optimality residual is directly verifiable.
assumptions_latex: The model is a finite maximum of affine cuts.
The stabilized model subproblem attains its minimum.
Aggregate multipliers are nonnegative, sum to one, and use active cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar g=\sum_i\alpha_i g_i\) and \(\bar g+(y-x)/\lambda=r\), with \(r=0\) at exact optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-cut multiplier certificate is correct for a finite convex max-of-affine model, but no source supports this model specialization or its role in the stated weakly convex-nonconvex bundle family.

children.title: Proximal-Point Quality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates interpreting trial points as approximate proximal points.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Quality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate proximal-point guarantee obtained from uniform model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex for \(\rho\geq0\). Let \(\lambda>0\) satisfy \(\lambda\rho<1\), and let \(\delta,\epsilon\geq0\). Suppose \(m:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfies \(m(z)\leq f(z)\leq m(z)+\delta\) for every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(y\) satisfies \(m(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\leq\inf_z\{m(z)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|z-x\|^2\}+\epsilon\), then \(f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\leq f_\lambda(x)+\delta+\epsilon\). The true proximal objective is \((1/\lambda-\rho)\)-strongly convex, so its unique minimizer \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) satisfies \(\|y-p\|\leq\sqrt{2(\delta+\epsilon)/(1/\lambda-\rho)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous weakly convex function, a global uniform model-error bound and approximate model-subproblem optimality bound the true proximal objective gap and the distance to the unique exact proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex with \(\rho\geq0\).
\(y\) solves the stabilized model objective to objective accuracy \(\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2-f_\lambda(x)\leq\delta+\epsilon\) and \(\|y-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\|\leq\sqrt{2(\delta+\epsilon)/(1/\lambda-\rho)}\).

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of f with parameter lambda
unique exact proximal point of f at x

children.title: Model-Agreement Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates comparing predicted and realized local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Agreement Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance certificate comparing realized decrease with stabilized-model prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a center \(x\), trial point \(y\), and positive predicted reduction \(\Delta=f(x)-m(y)-(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\), define the agreement ratio \(r=(f(x)-f(y))/\Delta\). The quantities in \(r\) require only the stored model, subproblem solution, and function values. For fixed \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), \(r\geq\eta_1\) certifies a serious step, \(r<\eta_1\) certifies a null step requiring model refinement, and \(r\geq\eta_2\) certifies strong agreement. Equivalently, the discrepancy \(d=\Delta-[f(x)-f(y)]\) satisfies \(d/\Delta=1-r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The realized-to-predicted reduction ratio gives a directly checkable serious-step, null-step, or strong-agreement classification.
assumptions_latex: Both \(f(x)\) and \(f(y)\) are available from the deterministic oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\geq\eta_1\) certifies acceptance, while \(r<\eta_1\) certifies rejection and model refinement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio is a suitable model-agreement certificate, but classifying its threshold outcomes as serious, null, or strong-agreement steps is an algorithm-dependent convention requiring a method-specific source.

children.title: Bundle Complexity-Work Accounting
children.top_down_role: Separation of accepted steps, model-refinement steps, oracle evaluations, and subproblem effort.

children.title: Serious-Step Complexity
children.top_down_role: Work counted by accepted stability-center movements.

knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-step bound derived from objective decrease per certified prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(f(x_0)-f_{\inf}\leq D<\infty\), where \(f_{\inf}\) is a lower bound on all serious centers. If every serious step with certificate \(\Delta_k>\varepsilon\) satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\eta\Delta_k\) for some \(\eta\in(0,1]\), then each such step decreases the objective by more than \(\eta\varepsilon\). Hence the number \(N_S(\varepsilon)\) of serious steps occurring before a certificate \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon\) is obtained satisfies \(N_S(\varepsilon)\leq\lfloor D/(\eta\varepsilon)\rfloor+1\). The resource counted is accepted stability-center movements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-fraction acceptance test bounds serious steps by the available objective gap divided by the required per-step predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\) on serious centers.
Every serious step realizes at least an \(\eta\)-fraction of its prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_S(\varepsilon)\leq\lfloor D/(\eta\varepsilon)\rfloor+1\).

notation.meaning: number of serious steps before tolerance epsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decrease accounting gives a valid loose bound, but no source supports the complexity statement, and the definition of N_S must clarify whether the certificate-producing terminal trial is included.

children.title: Null-Step Complexity
children.top_down_role: Work required for model refinement between accepted movements.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional refinement bound under geometric contraction of fixed-center model error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed center, let \(G_j=J_\star-J_j\geq0\) denote the stabilized-model value error after \(j\) null steps. Suppose each oracle cut and bundle update guarantees \(G_{j+1}\leq qG_j\) for a constant \(q\in(0,1)\). Then \(G_j\leq q^jG_0\), so the number of null steps sufficient for \(G_j\leq\varepsilon\) is at most \(N_N(\varepsilon)=\max\{0,\lceil\log(G_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q)\rceil\}\). Without a quantitative refinement condition such as this contraction, convergence of fixed-center model values alone gives no finite uniform null-step complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric contraction yields logarithmic null-step complexity; qualitative model convergence alone does not provide a uniform finite bound.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-center model error \(G_j\) is nonnegative.
Each null-step update contracts that error by a uniform factor \(q\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_N(\varepsilon)\leq\max\{0,\lceil\log(G_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q)\rceil\}\).

notation.meaning: stabilized-model value error after j refinements
null steps required for error tolerance epsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic estimate follows from the assumed contraction, but no source establishes that contraction for an applicable bundle-refinement method. The qualitative warning also requires support.

children.title: Oracle-Subproblem Complexity Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Accounting that separates information acquisition from model solution.

children.title: Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Accounting for objective, first-order, or subordinate oracle evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic oracle-call accounting across serious and null trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Count one deterministic first-order oracle call returning \((f(y),g)\) with \(g\in\partial f(y)\) at every distinct trial point, and one initialization call at \(x_0\). If the method reaches its stopping certificate after \(N_S\) serious trials and \(N_N\) null trials, without reevaluating cached points, then its oracle complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}=1+N_S+N_N\). Consequently, any bounds \(N_S\leq B_S(\varepsilon)\) and \(N_N\leq B_N(\varepsilon)\) imply \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}\leq1+B_S(\varepsilon)+B_N(\varepsilon)\). Extra line-search or rejected trial evaluations must be added explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one cached oracle evaluation per trial, total oracle calls equal initialization plus serious and null trials.
assumptions_latex: Each distinct trial uses exactly one deterministic value-subgradient oracle call.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}=1+N_S+N_N\leq1+B_S(\varepsilon)+B_N(\varepsilon)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identity is valid under the stated one-call-per-trial convention and fits Oracle Complexity, but that convention and the absence of additional evaluations require an inspectable algorithm or cost-model source.

children.title: Subproblem Complexity
children.top_down_role: Accounting for stabilized model-subproblem solution effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting for stabilized bundle-subproblem solves and their inner computational work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every serious or null trial requires one stabilized bundle-subproblem solve, and the solve at trial \(k\) uses \(T_k(\tau_k)\) elementary inner iterations to achieve residual tolerance \(\tau_k\). After \(N_S\) serious and \(N_N\) null trials, the number of subproblem solves is \(N_{\mathrm{sub}}=N_S+N_N\), while total inner work is \(W_{\mathrm{sub}}=\sum_{k=1}^{N_S+N_N}T_k(\tau_k)\). If \(T_k(\tau_k)\leq T(\tau)\) uniformly, then \(W_{\mathrm{sub}}\leq(N_S+N_N)T(\tau)\). This count separates expensive model optimization from oracle evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There is one stabilized subproblem per trial; total inner work is the sum of solve costs, bounded by trial count times uniform solve cost.
assumptions_latex: Every serious or null trial solves exactly one stabilized model subproblem.
The inner solver terminates at prescribed residual tolerance \(\tau_k\).
A uniform bound \(T_k(\tau_k)\leq T(\tau)\) is available for the final estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{sub}}=N_S+N_N\) and \(W_{\mathrm{sub}}\leq(N_S+N_N)T(\tau)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The accounting identities fit Subproblem Complexity and are conditionally correct, but no source supports the one-solve-per-trial model or the asserted uniform inner-solver work bound.

children.title: Oracle-to-Subproblem Work Balance
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between information acquisition and local model solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-to-Subproblem Work Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic work accounting for a bundle method with oracle calls and optimization subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a deterministic bundle method makes \(N_{o}\) oracle calls and solves \(N_{s}\) subproblems before producing an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary point. If one oracle call costs at most \(c_{o}\) work units and one subproblem costs at most \(c_{s}\), its total work satisfies
\[
W(\varepsilon)\le c_{o}N_{o}(\varepsilon)+c_{s}N_{s}(\varepsilon).
\]
The two resources are asymptotically balanced when \(c_{o}N_{o}(\varepsilon)=\Theta(c_{s}N_{s}(\varepsilon))\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Otherwise the larger term determines the asymptotic work bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total work is the sum of oracle and subproblem costs; balance means that neither weighted contribution asymptotically dominates the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(\varepsilon)=O(c_{o}N_{o}(\varepsilon)+c_{s}N_{s}(\varepsilon))\)

notation.meaning: Numbers of oracle calls and solved subproblems.
Total work required for the stated accuracy.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this two-resource accounting model or its accuracy convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source or locator supports the stated two-resource cost model, the epsilon-stationarity convention, or the asymptotic accounting claim. Moreover, the record supplies a generic accounting identity rather than a derived complexity bound, so complexity_bound is not justified without method-specific bounds on the two counts.
