children.title: Identifiable Geometric Structures
children.top_down_role: Local structures whose discovery reduces nonsmooth behavior to smooth or combinatorial structure.

children.title: Active Manifolds
children.top_down_role: Smooth local manifolds carrying active nonsmooth structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential identifiability of a smooth manifold for a limiting subgradient pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), let \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), and let \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a smooth manifold containing \(\bar x\). The manifold \(M\) is active, or identifiable, for \(f\) at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) if every sequence satisfying \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\), \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), and \(v_k\to\bar v\) has \(x_k\in M\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Thus nearby graph points of the subdifferential converging to \((\bar x,\bar v)\) eventually lie over \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active manifold contains every sufficiently near point whose function value and subgradient converge to the designated reference pair.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth manifold near \(\bar x\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,f(x_k),v_k)\to(\bar x,f(\bar x),\bar v)\Longrightarrow x_k\in M\text{ eventually}\)
review_flags: The supplied smooth-manifold locator does not establish the specialized sequential-identifiability definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential condition is a plausible definition of identifiability for a subgradient pair, but no cited source establishes that this condition alone, together with smoothness of M, is the intended definition of an active manifold in this container.

children.title: Face-Constraint Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral faces and active constraint systems.

children.title: Active Faces
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral face structures stabilized by local iterates or models.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F_C(x)\), and for any representation \(C=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ay\le b\}\), one has \(F_C(x)=\{y\in C:a_i^{\mathsf T}y=b_i\text{ for all }i\in I(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Unique minimal face of the polyhedron containing the point.
Indices of represented inequalities active at the point.
Transpose of the ith row of the represented constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-face activity for a point in a convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty convex polyhedron and let \(x\in C\). The active face at \(x\) is the unique minimal face
\[
F_C(x):=\bigcap\{F:F\text{ is a face of }C\text{ and }x\in F\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F_C(x)\). If, for some \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), the polyhedron is represented as \(C=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ay\le b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\) is the ith row of \(A\), define \(I(x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}\). Then
\[
F_C(x)=\{y\in C:a_i^{\mathsf T}y=b_i\text{ for every }i\in I(x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active face is the unique smallest face containing the point, equivalently the face whose relative interior contains the point. For a fixed finite inequality representation, it is cut out by all inequalities active at that point.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Faces

children.title: Active Constraint Sets
children.top_down_role: Constraint activity patterns stabilized near candidate solutions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(x)=\{i\in\{1,ldots,m\}:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Transpose of the ith row of the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity set for a fixed inequality representation of a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and represent the polyhedron as \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\). Denote the ith row of \(A\) by \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\). At any feasible point \(x\in C\), the active constraint set is
\[
I(x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}.
\]
Its complement relative to \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is the inactive set
\[
I(x)^c=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\}.
\]
The set \(I(x)\) depends on the chosen inequality representation and may include redundant constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed finite inequality representation, the active constraint set contains exactly the inequality indices holding with equality at the feasible point. Its complement contains the strict inequalities, and the active set can change when the representation changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Constraint Sets

children.title: Face-to-Constraint Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Geometric correspondence between active faces and active constraint descriptions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(x)=C\cap\bigcap_{i\in I(x)}\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}y=b_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Active constraints at the point for the fixed representation.
Minimal face of the polyhedron containing the point.
Transpose of the ith row of the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence for a fixed inequality representation of a convex polyhedron.

source_refs.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(C=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ay\le b\}\) be nonempty. Denote the ith row of \(A\) by \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\). For \(x\in C\), define \(I(x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}\). Then the minimal face containing \(x\) is
\[
F_C(x)=C\cap\bigcap_{i\in I(x)}\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}y=b_i\}.
\]
Conversely, if \(F\) is a nonempty face of \(C\) and \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\), then \(F=F_C(x)\). For the fixed representation, all points in \(\operatorname{ri}F\) have the same active index set, including any redundant inequalities that are active on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed finite inequality representation, the equalities active at a point cut out its minimal face. Conversely, every relative-interior point of a nonempty face recovers that face and has the same represented active index set as the other relative-interior points.
knowledge_statements.title: Face-to-Constraint Correspondence

children.title: Discrete Activity Structure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Discrete activity induced by sparsity, low rank, and piecewise representations.

children.title: Support Structures
children.top_down_role: Sparsity-related activity patterns that may stabilize locally.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-support strata used as discrete identifiable structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define its support by
\[
\operatorname{supp}(x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x_i\ne0\}.
\]
For each index set \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the exact-support stratum is
\[
M_S:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\operatorname{supp}(x)=S\}.
\]
Its linear support space is \(L_S:=\{x:x_i=0\text{ for }i\notin S\}\), and \(M_S\) is the relatively open subset of \(L_S\) on which every coordinate indexed by \(S\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support structure records which coordinates are nonzero and partitions the space into exact-support strata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_S=\{x:\operatorname{supp}(x)=S\}\subset L_S\)

notation.meaning: Coordinate subspace supported on the index set.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports support stratification as an identifiable activity structure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support and exact-support fiber definitions are precise, but no source supports their use as the intended identifiable structure in this taxonomy. The distinction between the nonclosed exact-support stratum and its coordinate subspace is consequential for identification and requires sourced context.

children.title: Rank Structures
children.top_down_role: Low-rank strata that may be identified by local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-rank strata for matrix-valued optimization variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the rank structure of a matrix \(X\) is the integer \(r=\operatorname{rank}X\). For each \(0\le r\le\min\{m,n\}\), the exact-rank stratum is
\[
M_r:=\{Y\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}Y=r\}.
\]
For \(r>0\), \(M_r\) is a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \(r(m+n-r)\); \(M_0=\{0\}\). Rank identification means that an algorithm's iterates eventually remain in the stratum \(M_{\operatorname{rank}\bar X}\) associated with the limiting matrix \(\bar X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank structures partition matrix space into smooth fixed-rank strata; identification means eventual agreement with the limit's rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim M_r=r(m+n-r)\)

notation.meaning: Set of matrices having rank exactly r.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not specifically support fixed-rank manifold geometry or rank identification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-rank set and dimension formula are standard, but the record combines a definition, a smooth-manifold theorem, and an algorithmic identification condition without any source. A source is needed to verify both the manifold statement and the intended identification convention.

children.title: Pattern Structures
children.top_down_role: Discrete activity induced by piecewise or combinatorial representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued activity patterns and their induced strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional space and let \(\pi:X\to P\) be a prescribed finite-valued activity map. The pattern structure induced by \(\pi\) is the partition into nonempty fibers
\[
M_p:=\{x\in X:\pi(x)=p\},\qquad p\in P.
\]
A sequence \((x_k)\) identifies the pattern of \(\bar x\) if there exists \(K\) such that \(\pi(x_k)=\pi(\bar x)\) for every \(k\ge K\). Examples of admissible activity maps include coordinate sign patterns, block-support labels, and fixed combinatorial partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite activity map partitions the variable space into pattern fibers; identification is eventual constancy at the limit's pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\text{ identifies }\pi(\bar x)\iff\pi(x_k)=\pi(\bar x)\text{ eventually}\)

notation.meaning: Fiber associated with pattern label p.

review_flags: Pattern structure is context-dependent, and no supplied source fixes the intended activity map or stratification framework.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-fiber construction is internally coherent but is an abstract stipulated definition rather than a demonstrably established notion of pattern structure for nonsmooth identification. No source fixes the intended activity map, regularity of its fibers, or identification framework.

children.title: VU-Primal-Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Local decompositions separating smooth and nonsmooth directions and their dual activity.

children.title: VU Structures
children.top_down_role: Local decompositions separating smooth from nonsmooth directional behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: VU Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal decomposition induced by the active convex subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and choose \(\bar g\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\). The VU structure at \(\bar x\) is the orthogonal decomposition
\[
\mathbb{R}^n=U\oplus V,
\qquad
V:=\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x)),

yad
U:=V^{\perp}.
\]
Here \(V\) contains directions generated by differences of active subgradients, while \(U\) is their orthogonal complement. The decomposition is independent of the selected relative-interior subgradient \(\bar g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The V-space parallels the affine hull of active subgradients, while the U-space is its orthogonal complement.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{R}^n=U\oplus V\), where \(V=\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))\) and \(U=V^\perp\)

notation.meaning: Subspace parallel to the affine hull of a convex set.
Smooth and nonsmooth subspaces of the VU decomposition.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the VU decomposition and its conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the selected VU convention. The statement also contains the malformed token 'yad' where a mathematical separator appears intended, and the selected relative-interior subgradient is unused because V is defined directly from the entire subdifferential. Source verification is needed before choosing and repairing the precise convention.

children.title: Primal-Dual Structures
children.top_down_role: Coupled primal activity and dual multiplier patterns near candidate solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-normal structure associated with a partly smooth active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a smooth active manifold for \(f\) at \(\bar x\), and suppose the sharpness relation
\[
\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))=N_M(\bar x)
\]
holds. The corresponding primal structure is the tangent space \(T_M(\bar x)\), and the dual structure is the normal space \(N_M(\bar x)\), equivalently the subspace parallel to the active subdifferential. They form the orthogonal decomposition
\[
\mathbb{R}^n=T_M(\bar x)\oplus N_M(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active manifold supplies the primal tangent space, while subgradient variation supplies its dual normal space.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth active manifold near \(\bar x\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{R}^n=T_M(\bar x)\oplus\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))\)

notation.meaning: Tangent space of the active manifold.
Normal space of the active manifold.
Subspace parallel to the active subdifferential.

review_flags: The supplied manifold and normal-cone locators do not establish the stated partial-smoothness sharpness correspondence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthogonal tangent-normal decomposition follows from the displayed sharpness identity for a smooth manifold, but no source establishes that this is the intended primal-dual structure or that the active-manifold assumptions used here suffice in the surrounding partial-smoothness setting.

children.title: VU-to-Primal-Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between directional decompositions and primal-dual activity.

knowledge_statements.title: VU-to-Primal-Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of VU subspaces with active-manifold tangent and normal spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a smooth manifold \(M\), with
\[
\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))=N_M(\bar x).
\]
For the VU decomposition defined by \(V=\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))\) and \(U=V^\perp\), one has
\[
V=N_M(\bar x),
\qquad
U=T_M(\bar x).
\]
Thus the VU splitting is exactly the dual-normal and primal-tangent splitting induced by the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under partial-smoothness sharpness, the V-space is the active normal space and the U-space is the active tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U=T_M(\bar x)\) and \(V=N_M(\bar x)\)

notation.meaning: Tangent and normal spaces of the active manifold.

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports the VU and active-manifold correspondence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed correspondence is algebraically consistent with the stated definitions and sharpness identity, and duality fits the leaf. However, neither the VU convention nor the precise partial-smoothness sharpness convention has a cited source, so the claimed identification cannot yet be reviewed reliably.

children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes making active structures stable under proximal and model-based perturbations.

children.title: Partial-Smoothness Regime
children.top_down_role: Smooth behavior along an active manifold with controlled transverse nonsmoothness.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Smoothness Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional partial smoothness relative to a smooth active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\) relative to a smooth manifold \(M\) when: \(f|_M\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\); \(f\) is prox-regular at \((\bar x,\bar v)\); the restriction of \(\partial f\) to \(M\) is continuous at \(\bar x\); and the sharpness identity
\[
\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))=N_M(\bar x)
\]
holds. These conditions isolate smooth tangential behavior and stable transverse nonsmoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial smoothness combines smooth restriction, prox-regularity, subdifferential continuity along a manifold, and equality between subgradient variation and the normal space.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth manifold containing \(\bar x\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f|_M\in C^2\) and \(\operatorname{par}(\partial f(\bar x))=N_M(\bar x)\), with prox-regularity and subdifferential continuity

notation.meaning: Restriction of the function to the manifold.
Subspace parallel to the active subdifferential.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not identify a source for this precise partial-smoothness definition and its chosen regularity convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Partial smoothness has several convention-dependent formulations. No source supports this exact combination of pairwise prox-regularity, C2 restriction, sharpness, and 'restriction of the subdifferential to M is continuous,' the last of which does not specify the relevant set-valued continuity notion. The exact definition therefore requires an authoritative locator.

children.title: Prox-Regular Identification Regime
children.top_down_role: Stable proximal geometry near the active structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Regular Identification Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local prox-regularity combined with an identifiable active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), and \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contain \(\bar x\). The prox-regular identification regime holds at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) relative to \(M\) if there exist \(r,\varepsilon>0\) such that \[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle v,y-x\rangle-\frac r2\|y-x\|^2\] whenever \(x,y\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\), \(v\in\partial f(x)\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar v)\), and \(|f(x)-f(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\); moreover, every sequence \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\) with \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\) satisfies \(x_k\in M\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function has a uniform local quadratic lower support, and every convergent nearby subgradient sequence eventually lies on the active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is finitely identified by graph-convergent subgradient sequences near \((\bar x,\bar v)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the identification-geometry leaf and is internally coherent, but the combined prox-regularity and identifiable-set formulation has no cited evidence.

children.title: Nondegenerate Activity Regime
children.top_down_role: Stable separation of active structure and associated dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate Activity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior separation of the limiting dual vector from activity boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a manifold \(M\), and let \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). The activity is nondegenerate at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) when \[\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x).\] Equivalently for identification purposes, the limiting dual vector lies away from the relative boundary of the active subdifferential face. Under subdifferential continuity, any sequence \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\) with \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\) then enters \(M\) after finitely many indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limiting subgradient in the relative interior of the active subdifferential face prevents ambiguity between neighboring activity patterns and yields finite identification.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
\(f\) is subdifferentially continuous at \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\) implies eventual membership \(x_k\in M\) for graph-convergent subgradient sequences.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-interior condition fits the leaf, but the asserted finite-identification implication may require additional prox-regularity or a particular definition of partial smoothness. A source is needed to fix the exact hypotheses.

children.title: Sharp-Growth Identification Regime
children.top_down_role: Growth geometry supporting structural stabilization and local acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp-Growth Identification Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear growth transverse to an active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed embedded manifold containing \(\bar x\), and let \(P_M\) be single-valued near \(\bar x\). A proper function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) has sharp transverse growth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\) if there exist \(\alpha,\varepsilon>0\) such that \[f(x)\ge f(P_Mx)+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,M)\] for every \(x\in B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\). Thus leaving \(M\) incurs a first-order objective penalty uniformly exceeding errors that are \(o(\operatorname{dist}(x,M))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the reference point, displacement away from the active manifold incurs an objective increase at least proportional to the displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a closed embedded manifold near \(\bar x\).
\(f\) is proper and finite on \(M\) near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(P_Mx)\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,M)\) locally for some \(\alpha>0\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to M

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the sharp-growth leaf, but this particular projection-based transverse-growth definition is uncited and is not uniquely standard across the literature.

children.top_down_role: Finite-entry results organized by the model or method producing approximate critical points.

children.title: Proximal-Method Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification through proximal point and proximal-gradient mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Method Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-manifold identification by exact proximal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be prox-regular and partly smooth at a stationary point \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\), with \(0\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\). Fix a sufficiently small \(\lambda>0\), and generate \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.\] If \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\to0\), then \(v_{k+1}:=(x_k-x_{k+1})/\lambda\in\partial f(x_{k+1})\) converges to \(0\), and there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent exact proximal iterations identify the active manifold finitely when prox-regularity, partial smoothness, and relative-interior nondegeneracy hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is prox-regular and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x_k\in M\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits proximal-method identification, but convergence of the iterates and steps alone does not explicitly provide the function-value convergence normally needed by the stated identification principle. The exact proximal parameter and continuity hypotheses require a source.

children.title: Composite Identification Family
children.top_down_role: Identification through structured composite models.

children.title: Prox-Linear Identification
children.top_down_role: Structural identification arising from prox-linear local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification by active arguments of prox-linear subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\), where \(c\) is continuously differentiable, and define \(d_k\) by minimizing \[h(c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)d)+g(x_k+d)+\frac{1}{2t}\|d\|^2.\] Put \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) and \(z_k=c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)d_k\). Suppose \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(d_k\to0\), \(h\) is partly smooth at \(c(\bar x)\) relative to \(N\), and the subproblem multipliers converge to a vector in \(\operatorname{ri}\partial h(c(\bar x))\). Under the corresponding transversality condition, there exists \(K\) such that \(z_k\in N\) for all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nondegenerate convergent prox-linear subproblems finitely identify the outer function's active manifold through their linearized composite arguments.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable and \(h,g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous functions.
\(h\) is partly smooth relative to \(N\), with the standard composite transversality condition.
\(x_k\to\bar x\), \(d_k\to0\), and subproblem multipliers converge nondegenerately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)d_k\in N\).

notation.meaning: active manifold of the outer function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the leaf, but the subproblem multipliers and the required transversality condition are not formally defined. A source is necessary to determine the valid theorem statement.

children.title: Composite-Model Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification behavior induced by structured outer-inner compositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Model Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability criterion for first-order composite models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=h\circ c+g\), define the model at \(x\) by \[m_x(y)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+g(y).\] Let \(N\) be an active set for \(h\) at \(c(\bar x)\), and let \(S=\{x:c(x)\in N\}\). The composite model is identifying at \(\bar x\) when, for every \(x_k,y_k\to\bar x\) satisfying \(m_{x_k}(y_k)\to F(\bar x)\) and admitting model subgradients converging to a nondegenerate stationary multiplier pair, one has \(c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)(y_k-x_k)\in N\) and \(y_k\in S\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite model is identifying when near-stationary model solutions eventually recover both the outer active set and its primal preimage.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(g\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(N\) is an active set of \(h\) at \(c(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near-stationary model solutions eventually satisfy both linearized outer activity and \(y_k\in c^{-1}(N)\).

notation.meaning: first-order composite model based at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits composite-model identification, but “model subgradients” and a “nondegenerate stationary multiplier pair” are undefined, so the quantified criterion is not presently verifiable.

children.title: Composite Activity Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of active structure between component models and the composite objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Activity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of an outer active manifold through a smooth inner map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(N\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be a smooth manifold containing \(c( ar x)\), and assume transversality \[\operatorname{range}
abla c( ar x)+T_N(c( ar x))=\mathbb{R}^m.\] Then \(S=c^{-1}(N)\) is a smooth manifold near \( ar x\), with \[T_S( ar x)=\{d:
abla c( ar x)d\in T_N(c( ar x))\},\qquad N_S( ar x)=
abla c( ar x)^*N_N(c( ar x)).\] Hence identification of \(c(x_k)\in N\) is exactly identification of \(x_k\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under transversality, an outer active manifold pulls back to a smooth primal manifold with explicit tangent and normal spaces.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a smooth embedded manifold near \(c(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=c^{-1}(N)\) is locally smooth and has the displayed tangent and normal formulas.

notation.meaning: tangent space of N at z
normal space of N at z

children.title: Bundle-Based Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification from bundle primal-dual information and proximal approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Based Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification by convergent bundle contact pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), let \(M\) be identifiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) for \(\partial f\), and suppose a bundle method produces contact pairs \((y_k,g_k)\) with \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)\). If \[y_k\to\bar x,\qquad f(y_k)\to f(\bar x),\qquad g_k\to\bar v,\] then there exists \(K\) such that \(y_k\in M\) for all \(k\ge K\). Consequently, once the bundle retains such contact pairs, its local cutting-plane model contains subgradient information from the identified structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bundle contact points identify an active set finitely when their function values and subgradients converge to an identifiable primal-dual pair.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is identifiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) for \(\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ y_k\in M\).

notation.meaning: subgradient stored at the contact point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Eventual membership follows from the assumed identifiability definition, but no source supports either its bundle-method specialization or the claim about retained cutting-plane information.

children.title: Constraint-Activity Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite recovery of active constraints and faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Activity Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly positive limiting multipliers certify finite recovery of active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous and suppose feasible primal-dual pairs \((x_k,\lambda^k)\) satisfy \[c_i(x_k)\le0,\qquad \lambda_i^k\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i^k c_i(x_k)=0.\] If \((x_k,\lambda^k)\to(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) and strict complementarity holds, meaning \(c_i(\bar x)=0\) implies \(\bar\lambda_i>0\), then for every active index \(i\) one has \(\lambda_i^k>0\), hence \(c_i(x_k)=0\), for all sufficiently large \(k\). Every inactive index remains inactive by continuity, so the active set is eventually exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementary primal-dual iterates finitely recover all active inequalities when every limiting active constraint has a strictly positive multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i\) is continuous for every constraint index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{i:c_i(x_k)=0\}=\{i:c_i(\bar x)=0\}\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).

notation.meaning: active constraint index set at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf and the finite-identification argument is plausible for finitely many constraints, but the constraint index set is not introduced and the damped-Newton LCP locator does not clearly support the stated general nonlinear-constraint result.

children.title: Post-Identification Behavior
children.top_down_role: Reduced models and local acceleration regimes available after structural stabilization.

children.title: Smooth Reduced-Problem Regime
children.top_down_role: Restriction of objectives and models to identified smooth structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Reduced-Problem Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth optimization after finite active-manifold identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\), and suppose an algorithm identifies \(M\): \(x_k\in M\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Then the local reduced objective \(f|_M\) is \(C^2\), and subsequent first- and second-order models may be formed intrinsically on \(M\). In particular, stationarity of the reduced problem is \[\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)=0,\] where \(\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)\in T_M(x)\), and feasible local steps belong to \(T_M(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identification, the nonsmooth problem restricts to a smooth manifold problem with intrinsic gradients, Hessians, and tangent steps.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eventually the local iteration can be analyzed as smooth optimization of \(f|_M\).

notation.meaning: tangent space of M at x

source_refs.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

source_witnesses.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the post-identification leaf, but the cited smooth-manifold appendix does not specifically support the partial-smoothness restriction claim or the asserted reduced optimization regime.

children.title: Manifold Newton Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Second-order local acceleration along an identified manifold.

knowledge_statements.title: Manifold Newton Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic Newton iteration on the identified active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After identification of a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\), choose \(x_0\in M\). At iteration \(k\), solve \[\operatorname{Hess}_M f(x_k)[d_k]=-\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k),\qquad d_k\in T_M(x_k),\] and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(d_k)\), where \(R\) is a second-order retraction. Stop when \(\|\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\), returning \(x_k\). If \(f|_M\) has locally Lipschitz Hessian, \(\operatorname{grad}_M f(\bar x)=0\), and \(\operatorname{Hess}_M f(\bar x)\) is nonsingular, then sufficiently close iterates are well-defined and converge quadratically to \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the intrinsic Newton equation on the identified manifold and retract the step; a nonsingular Lipschitz Hessian gives local quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(f|_M\) is twice continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz Riemannian Hessian.
\(R\) is a second-order retraction and \(x_0\) is sufficiently near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_M(x_{k+1},\bar x)=O(\operatorname{dist}_M(x_k,\bar x)^2)\).

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian of the reduced objective
retraction from the tangent space at x onto M

source_refs.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

source_witnesses.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits manifold Newton acceleration, but the supplied Euclidean Newton and general manifold locators do not directly support the stated retraction-based Riemannian quadratic-convergence theorem.

children.title: Curvature-Metric Acceleration Family
children.top_down_role: Curvature-informed acceleration following identification.

children.title: Quasi-Newton Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Post-identification acceleration using approximate curvature updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superlinear variable-curvature iteration after active-manifold identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After identifying a smooth manifold \(M\), initialize \(x_0\in M\) and an invertible tangent operator \(B_0:T_M(x_0)\to T_M(x_0)\). Compute \[B_kd_k=-\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(d_k),\] transport secant data between tangent spaces, and update \(B_k\) by a safeguarded quasi-Newton rule. Stop when \(\|\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\). If \(x_k\to\bar x\), the reduced Hessian \(H_*\) is nonsingular and locally Lipschitz, unit steps are eventually accepted, and the Dennis--Moré condition \(\|(B_k-H_*)d_k\|/\|d_k\|\to0\) holds, then convergence is superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded tangent-space quasi-Newton method becomes superlinearly convergent when its curvature operators satisfy the Dennis–Moré approximation condition.
assumptions_latex: The identified reduced objective has a nonsingular locally Lipschitz Hessian at \(\bar x\).
The safeguarded iteration converges to \(\bar x\) and eventually accepts unit steps.
The transported operators satisfy the Dennis--Moré condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_M(x_{k+1},\bar x)/\operatorname{dist}_M(x_k,\bar x)\to0\).

notation.meaning: quasi-Newton approximation to the reduced Hessian
reduced Hessian at the limit point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the Dennis–Moré expression subtracts operators or vectors associated with different tangent spaces without specifying transport. The Euclidean quasi-Newton citation does not determine the required manifold formulation.

children.title: Variable-Metric Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Post-identification acceleration using adaptable local metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-space variable-metric iteration after finite identification of a smooth active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F|_{\mathcal M}\) be continuously differentiable on an identified manifold \(\mathcal M\), and let \(g_k=\operatorname{grad}_{\mathcal M}F(x_k)\). Choose a self-adjoint positive-definite tangent-space metric \(H_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to T_{x_k}\mathcal M\), solve \(H_kd_k=-g_k\), and select \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by a sufficient-decrease test. Update \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_kd_k)\), where \(R\) is a retraction. Stop when \(\|g_k\|\leq\varepsilon\). Metrics satisfying \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) yield uniformly gradient-related reduced directions; curvature-informed updates may accelerate the identified smooth iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identification, solve a positive-definite variable-metric system in the active tangent space, retract an accepted step, and stop when the reduced gradient is small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(-\alpha_kH_k^{-1}\operatorname{grad}_{\mathcal M}F(x_k))\).

source_refs.locator: 3.3.2 Methods of Variable Metric and Methods of Conjugate Directions p. 78

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.2 Methods of Variable Metric and Methods of Conjugate Directions p. 78

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but the cited Euclidean variable-metric section does not establish the post-identification manifold specialization, tangent-space operators, retraction, or stated gradient-related conclusion.

children.title: Post-Identification Metric Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Controls on curvature-informed metrics after structural stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Identification Metric Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance conditions preventing unstable curvature metrics after an active manifold has been identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an identified iterate \(x_k\in\mathcal M\), accept a proposed tangent metric \(\widetilde H_{k+1}\) only if its safeguarded form \(H_{k+1}\) satisfies \(mI\preceq H_{k+1}\preceq MI\), the computed direction obeys \(\langle g_k,d_k\rangle\leq-c\|g_k\|\|d_k\|\), and the trial point remains in the identification neighborhood. A secant update additionally requires \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle\geq\eta\|s_k\|^2\). If any test fails, reject or regularize the update and use a reference metric \(H_{\mathrm{ref}}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a post-identification metric only when it is uniformly positive definite, produces descent, has adequate secant curvature, and stays inside the identification neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(s_k\) and \(y_k\) are compared in a common tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{k+1}\) is accepted only when all spectral, descent, curvature, and neighborhood tests hold.

notation.meaning: reduced gradient at the identified iterate

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral clipping, descent tests, and curvature tests are standard variable-metric safeguards

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the safeguard leaf, but the combined spectral, descent, secant-curvature, transport, and identification-neighborhood requirements have no cited source and are not presented as one established acceptance rule.

children.title: Bundle Reduction after Identification
children.top_down_role: Bundle compression and smooth-subspace modeling after activity stabilizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Reduction after Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of cutting planes once all retained information corresponds to one identified smooth manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B_k=\{(a_i,g_i)\}_{i\in I_k}\) define the tangent model \(m_k(d)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{a_i+\langle g_i,d\rangle\}\) on \(T_{x_k}\mathcal M\). After identification, discard planes inconsistent with \(\mathcal M\), retain every plane active at the accepted trial step, and replace the remaining inactive planes by an aggregate plane \((\bar a_k,\bar g_k)=\sum_i\lambda_i(a_i,g_i)\), where \(\lambda_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Choose the multipliers from the preceding model subproblem so that the aggregate preserves its predicted value and aggregate tangent subgradient. The reduced bundle is the retained active planes together with the aggregate plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identification, remove incompatible cuts and aggregate inactive cuts while preserving the previous model value and tangent subgradient.
assumptions_latex: \(x_k\in\mathcal M\) and every retained \(g_i\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\).
The previous model subproblem supplies convex multipliers \(\lambda_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_{k+1}\) preserves the preceding aggregate model value and tangent subgradient with fewer planes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex aggregation of inactive cutting planes is standard in bundle compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the bundle-reduction leaf, but no source supports the identified-manifold deletion rule or the claim that multipliers over the stated inactive planes preserve both the preceding model value and aggregate tangent subgradient.

children.title: Identification Reliability Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Observable evidence of structural stabilization and boundaries of reliable finite identification.

children.title: Active-Pattern Stability Certificates
children.top_down_role: Persistence of combinatorial activity across nearby iterates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable margin certificate for persistence of a finite inequality activity pattern.
