children.title: Manifold-Primal-Dual Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Joint evidence from manifold membership and dual activity.

children.title: Manifold Identification Certificates
children.top_down_role: Observable evidence that iterates or models have stabilized on an active manifold.

knowledge_statements.title: Manifold Identification Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact partial-smoothness certificate for a candidate active manifold in composite optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F=h+g\), where \(h\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is partly smooth at \(x\) relative to a manifold \(\mathcal M\). The pair \((x,v)\) is a manifold-identification certificate when \(x\in\mathcal M\), \(v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(x)\), and \(\nabla h(x)+v=0\). The relative-interior condition supplies strict normal nondegeneracy, while membership in \(\mathcal M\) verifies the proposed stratum. Under the local identifiability theorem for partly smooth functions, every sufficiently close graph point \((x',v')\in\operatorname{gph}\partial g\) near \((x,v)\) has \(x'\in\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Manifold membership, stationarity, and a relative-interior subgradient provide an exact certificate for the locally identifiable active manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is partly smooth at \(x\) relative to \(\mathcal M\).
The applicable partial-smoothness identifiability theorem holds locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,v)\) locally identifies \(\mathcal M\) through nearby points of \(\operatorname{gph}\partial g\).

notation.meaning: limiting or convex subdifferential appropriate to g

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: partial smoothness plus relative-interior nondegeneracy is the standard identification mechanism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, but the notation deliberately leaves the subdifferential as either limiting or convex, while the required partial-smoothness, prox-regularity, subdifferential-continuity, and identifiability hypotheses depend on that choice. An exact theorem citation is required.

children.title: Primal-Dual Identification Certificates
children.top_down_role: Observable evidence from stabilized primal activity and dual behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Identification Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-identification certificate for an ℓ1-regularized smooth problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=h(x)+\lambda\|x\|_1\) with \(\lambda>0\), let \(S=\{i:x_i
eq0\}\). A primal-dual certificate is a vector \(z\) satisfying \(
abla h(x)+\lambda z=0\), \(z_i=\operatorname{sign}(x_i)\) for \(i\in S\), and \(|z_i|<1\) for \(i
otin S\). The strict dual margin \(\gamma=1-\|z_{S^c}\|_\infty>0\) verifies strict complementarity on zero coordinates. Consequently, any sufficiently close stationary primal-dual pair with the same sign margin has zero coordinates on \(S^c\) and signs \(\operatorname{sign}(x_i)\) on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity plus strict dual feasibility on zero coordinates certifies the support and signs of an ℓ1-regularized solution.
assumptions_latex: The nonzero coordinates of \(x\) have fixed signs locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,z,\gamma)\) certifies the signed support pattern \(S\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed subgradient and strict-complementarity conditions are standard for ℓ1 regularization

children.title: Cross-Certificate Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks linking manifold evidence with primal-dual evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Certificate Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility test between manifold and primal-dual identification certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A manifold certificate \((x,\mathcal M,v)\) and a primal-dual certificate \((x,z)\) are cross-consistent when they use the same primal point, the dual representation induces the same subgradient \(v\), and the certified tangent-normal decomposition agrees with the active pattern: \(T_{\mathcal M}(x)=T_{I(z)}(x)\) and \(v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(x)\). For \(g(x)=\lambda\|x\|_1\), consistency means \(v=\lambda z\), \(T_{\mathcal M}(x)=\{d:d_{S^c}=0\}\), \(z_S=\operatorname{sign}(x_S)\), and \(\|z_{S^c}\|_\infty<1\). Conflicting tangent spaces or boundary dual values invalidate joint identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two certificates agree only when their primal point, subgradient, tangent space, active pattern, and strict dual margins describe the same stratum.
assumptions_latex: Both certificates concern the same composite objective \(h+g\).
Their dual variables admit a common subgradient representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathcal M}(x)=T_{I(z)}(x)\) and the two certificates identify one common active stratum.

notation.meaning: tangent space of the certified manifold
activity pattern induced by the dual certificate
support of x in the ℓ1 specialization

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compatible certificates must induce the same subgradient and tangent-normal geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, and the ℓ1 specialization is plausible, but the general object I(z) is not defined. Moreover, a boundary dual value destroys robust identification but does not automatically make two otherwise matching certificates geometrically inconsistent.

children.title: Inexact Identification Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Regimes lacking exact or finitely stable activity.

children.title: Degenerate Identification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Identification behavior under nonunique, unstable, or weakly separated activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Identification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification regime lacking a positive relative-interior or activity-separation margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stationary composite point \(\bar x\) of \(F=h+g\), with \(\bar v=-\nabla h(\bar x)\in\partial g(\bar x)\), the identification regime is degenerate when \(\bar v\notin\operatorname{ri}\partial g(\bar x)\), or when the residual margins separating the proposed active pattern from competing patterns vanish. Equivalently, the available manifold or primal-dual certificate has zero strictness margin. In this regime, arbitrarily small perturbations of the primal-dual pair may be compatible with a different stratum, so stationarity and proximity alone do not certify a unique identified pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identification is degenerate when the dual point lies on a subdifferential boundary or the activity-separation margin is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar v\notin\operatorname{ri}\partial g(\bar x)\) or a zero separation margin defines a degenerate identification regime.

notation.meaning: stationary subgradient paired with the smooth gradient
relative interior of the subdifferential value

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: loss of relative-interior nondegeneracy is the standard boundary of stable identification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but failure of relative-interior nondegeneracy and vanishing residual separation are not established as equivalent in the stated generality. The assertion about arbitrarily small perturbations also requires an explicit identification theorem or counterexample framework.

children.title: Approximate Identification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Near-identification behavior when exact active structure is not finitely stabilized.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Identification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative relaxation of exact manifold membership and strict primal-dual identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=h+g\), let \(\mathcal M\) be a candidate active manifold, and fix tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\delta\geq0\). A pair \((x,v)\) is in an approximate identification regime when \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal M)\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\|\nabla h(x)+v\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), and \(v\in\operatorname{ri}_{\delta}\partial g(x)\), where \(\operatorname{ri}_{\delta}C=\{u\in C:\operatorname{dist}(u,\operatorname{rbd}C)\geq\delta\}\). Exact identification is recovered when \(\varepsilon_p=\varepsilon_d=0\) and \(\delta>0\); positive residual tolerances describe inexact manifold and stationarity information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate identification permits bounded manifold and stationarity errors while retaining a quantified distance from the subdifferential boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(h\in C^1\) and \(\partial g(x)\) is nonempty and convex.
The candidate manifold \(\mathcal M\) is locally closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,v)\) is \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\delta)\)-approximately identified relative to \(\mathcal M\).

notation.meaning: δ-interior relative to the boundary of C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distance-to-manifold, stationarity residual, and boundary margin are natural quantitative relaxations

children.title: Identification Accuracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits separating reliable approximate activity from structurally misleading activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Identification Accuracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dual-error threshold for certifying zero coordinates in ℓ1 identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=h(x)+\lambda\|x\|_1\), suppose an approximate normalized dual vector \(\widehat z\) satisfies \(\|z-\widehat z\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon_z\) for some exact \(z\in\partial\|x\|_1\). A coordinate can be certified as strictly inactive only if \(|\widehat z_i|+\varepsilon_z<1\). Indeed, this inequality forces \(|z_i|<1\), hence \(x_i=0\). At the boundary \(|\widehat z_i|+\varepsilon_z\geq1\), the uncertainty set contains a value with \(|z_i|=1\), which is compatible with either a zero coordinate or an active signed coordinate; the approximate dual data alone cannot identify that coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ℓ1 zero coordinate is certifiable only when its approximate dual magnitude plus its error bound is strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widehat z_i|+\varepsilon_z<1\) certifies \(x_i=0\); failure of strict inequality leaves identification unresolved.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the boundary follows directly from the ℓ1 subdifferential and an infinity-norm error enclosure

children.title: Certificate Reliability Under Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Scope of identification certificates when degeneracy weakens structural conclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reliability Under Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example showing loss of robust activity certification at a boundary dual point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F(x)=|x|-x\) on \(\mathbb R\). At \(\bar x=0\), stationarity holds with \(\bar z=1\in\partial|\bar x|=[-1,1]\), but \(\bar z\notin\operatorname{ri}\partial|\bar x|\). Every \(x>0\) is also stationary and has the singleton subgradient \(\partial|x|=\{1\}\). Hence stationary pairs \((x_k,1)\) with \(x_k\downarrow0\) approach \((0,1)\) while their primal pattern is nonzero, whereas the limit pattern is zero. Thus a boundary-valued primal-dual certificate has no neighborhood in which the zero pattern is forced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For |x|−x, positive stationary points converge to the zero stationary point while retaining a different activity pattern, defeating boundary-valued certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,1)\) does not reliably certify the zero pattern because \((x_k,1)\to(0,1)\) with \(x_k>0\).

notation.meaning: normalized absolute-value subgradient at the limit point
positive stationary sequence converging to zero

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the scalar counterexample is directly checkable from the absolute-value subdifferential

children.title: Identification-Acceleration Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Unstable activity and unsafe transition to reduced smooth methods.

children.title: Manifold Switching
children.top_down_role: Repeated changes in the locally selected manifold or active structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Manifold Switching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite identification when iterates repeatedly enter distinct active strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a stratification \(\{\mathcal M_j\}_{j\in J}\), manifold switching occurs when the assigned indices \(j_k\), defined by \(x_k\in\mathcal M_{j_k}\), change infinitely often. For \(g(x)=|x|\), the sequence \(x_k=(-1)^k/k\) converges to \(0\) but alternates between the strata \(\mathcal M_+=(0,\infty)\) and \(\mathcal M_-=(-\infty,0)\); it never identifies the limiting stratum \(\mathcal M_0=\{0\}\). Therefore convergence and vanishing distance to the limiting point do not alone justify reduced-manifold acceleration; a positive stability margin or repeated certificate is required before switching can be excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent sequence may alternate forever between active manifolds, so proximity alone cannot justify permanent reduced-manifold acceleration.
assumptions_latex: The nonsmooth geometry admits a locally finite stratification.
Acceleration assumes eventual persistence of one stratum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=(-1)^k/k\to0\) exhibits infinite switching and no finite identification of \(\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: stratum index occupied by the kth iterate

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the absolute-value sequence is a direct counterexample to identification from convergence alone

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternating sequence correctly demonstrates manifold switching and failure of finite identification, but the final claim that specifically a positive margin or repeated certificate is required to exclude switching is broader than the example establishes and lacks a source.

children.title: Premature Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Early use of reduced smooth behavior before identification is sufficiently stable.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for switching from a safeguarded full-space method to a locally accelerated reduced model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be weakly convex, let \(x_k\) be the current iterate, and let \(M_k\) be a candidate active manifold. Acceleration is premature whenever the method selects a reduced step \(d_k\in T_{M_k}(x_k)\) before validating both identification and model agreement; concretely, when either \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,M_k)>\varepsilon_k\), the active-set residual exceeds \(\varepsilon_k\), or \(f(x_k+d_k)>f(x_k)-\eta\,\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\), where \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\) is predicted decrease and \(\eta\in(0,1)\). In this regime the reduced step has no certified descent or identification guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration is premature if a reduced-space step is taken before manifold identification and predicted-versus-realized decrease have both been validated.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is weakly convex and finite near \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k\) has no certified descent or active-manifold validity guarantee.

notation.meaning: candidate active manifold at iteration k
decrease predicted by the reduced model
tangent space of the candidate manifold

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited for this specific acceleration boundary. Moreover, \(T_{M_k}(x_k)\) normally requires \(x_k\in M_k\), whereas the proposed failure test allows \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,M_k)>\varepsilon_k\). The active-set residual is also undefined, so the mathematical boundary cannot be reliably validated.

children.title: Acceleration Trigger Failures
children.top_down_role: Unreliable criteria for transitioning from model-based iterations to accelerated local phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration Trigger Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes of finite-accuracy tests used to authorize local reduced-space acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_k\in\{0,1\}\) be an acceleration trigger computed from observable residuals, and let \(I_k\in\{0,1\}\) denote the ideal condition that the active manifold is correctly identified and the reduced model is locally valid. A false-positive trigger occurs when \(C_k=1\) and \(I_k=0\); a false-negative trigger occurs when \(C_k=0\) and \(I_k=1\). If trigger tolerances do not vanish with the stationarity and localization scales, then neither error is excluded asymptotically. Consequently, acceleration based solely on \(C_k\) requires an independent acceptance test and a return mechanism to the safeguarded model method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acceleration trigger fails by activating an invalid reduced model or suppressing a valid one; fixed-scale tests cannot generally exclude either error asymptotically.
assumptions_latex: \(C_k\) is computed from finite-accuracy observable tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_k\neq I_k\) is possible unless trigger accuracy is coupled to the algorithmic scales and independently safeguarded.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The false-positive and false-negative terminology is coherent, but the claim that nonvanishing tolerances exclude neither error asymptotically is method-dependent and unsupported. The ideal validity condition \(I_k\) also lacks a mathematical definition sufficient to establish the conclusion.

children.title: Reduced-Model Reentry Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Protective mechanisms for suspending or restarting reduced-manifold acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Model Reentry Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance-and-reentry rule for safely alternating between reduced acceleration and the full safeguarded model method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), a reduced trial step \(d_k\), predicted decrease \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\), and constants \(0<\eta_-<\eta_+<1\), compute \(y_k=x_k+d_k\) and \(r_k=(f(x_k)-f(y_k))/\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\). Accept the reduced step only if \(r_k\ge\eta_+\) and the identification residual at \(y_k\) does not exceed its prescribed tolerance. If \(r_k<\eta_-\), the residual test fails, or the candidate manifold changes, reject or truncate \(d_k\), restore the full-space model, enlarge stabilization, and resume safeguarded iterations. Output the first accepted trial or a full-model trial after reentry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept reduced acceleration only after sufficient realized decrease and identification consistency; otherwise restore the stabilized full-space model and resume safeguarded iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method retains reduced acceleration only after passing decrease and identification tests; otherwise it reenters the safeguarded full model.

notation.meaning: ratio of realized to predicted decrease

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the safeguard container, but the particular two-threshold acceptance, truncation, stabilization, and reentry protocol has no citation. The identification residual, its tolerance, the meaning of manifold change, and the direction of the stabilization update must be specified by an authoritative method source.

children.title: Failure-Safeguard Duality
children.top_down_role: Geometric, analytical, and computational boundaries of model descent and bundle convergence.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Essentials of Numerical Nonsmooth Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Instability of cutting planes and nonconvex bundle extensions
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Essentials of Numerical Nonsmooth Optimization

children.title: Model-Validity Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by uncontrolled approximation error or unreliable nonconvex cuts.

children.title: Uncontrolled Model Error
children.top_down_role: Model error incompatible with the localization scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Model Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model error that does not shrink at the scale required by localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k(\cdot;x_k)\) model \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) on the localization ball \(B(x_k,\delta_k)\), and define \(E_k=\sup_{\|d\|\le\delta_k}|f(x_k+d)-m_k(x_k+d;x_k)|\). For a first-order localized model, controlled error requires \(E_k=o(\delta_k)\); for a quadratically accurate model it requires \(E_k=O(\delta_k^2)\). Uncontrolled model error occurs when the applicable normalized quantity, respectively \(E_k/\delta_k\) or \(E_k/\delta_k^2\), is unbounded or fails to approach its required limit. Predicted decrease at that scale then need not approximate realized decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model error is uncontrolled when it fails to decay at the localization scale, so predicted decrease need not reflect objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta_k>0\) and the displayed supremum is finite.
The required accuracy order is specified by the model class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model-based decrease predictions on \(B(x_k,\delta_k)\) are not certified at the required order.

notation.meaning: worst model-objective error on the localization ball

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the asserted \(o(\delta_k)\) and \(O(\delta_k^2)\) requirements depend on the precise model class and convergence framework. The record blends first-order consistency and quadratic accuracy without defining those classes or citing their accuracy conditions.

children.title: Invalid Globalized Nonconvex Cuts
children.top_down_role: Local affine information incorrectly treated as global support.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Globalized Nonconvex Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of treating local nonconvex first-order information as a global affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) given by \(f(x)=-x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\), the local affine linearization is \(\ell(x)=f(0)+f'(0)x=0\). Although \(\ell\) matches both value and derivative at \(0\), it is not a global supporting cut: for every \(x\neq0\), \(\ell(x)=0> -x^2=f(x)\). Thus the convex subgradient inequality cannot be imposed on a general nonconvex objective. For a \(\rho\)-weakly convex objective, the valid global lower model is instead quadratic: \(f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle-(\rho/2)\|y-x\|^2\) for an appropriate weak subgradient \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent to a nonconvex function need not globally underestimate it; even the tangent to minus x squared at zero lies above the function elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The affine cut is constructed from the value and derivative at \(\bar x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\) fails for every \(x\neq0\), so \(\ell\) is not a valid global minorant.

notation.meaning: affine linearization at the base point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample itself is correct and the content kind fits the leaf, but no evidence is cited. The additional weak-convexity inequality requires a specified subdifferential and assumptions under which the chosen \(g\) yields the global quadratic lower estimate; these cannot be validated from the record.

children.title: Persistent Model–Objective Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Repeated disagreement between predicted and realized behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Model–Objective Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated failure of predicted decrease to agree with realized objective behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For accepted or tested trial points \(y_k\), define predicted decrease \(p_k=m_k(x_k;x_k)-m_k(y_k;x_k)>0\), realized decrease \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(y_k)\), and agreement ratio \(r_k=a_k/p_k\). Given an acceptance threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), persistent model-objective mismatch holds on an infinite index set \(K\) when \(r_k<\eta\) for every \(k\in K\), or more strongly when \(|a_k-p_k|/p_k\not\to0\) along \(K\), despite localization or model refinement. The model therefore fails to supply asymptotically reliable decrease predictions on that subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mismatch is persistent when realized and predicted decrease repeatedly disagree, even as the method localizes or refines its model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is not asymptotically predictive along \(K\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The agreement-ratio construction is standard in form, but the proposed persistent-mismatch criterion is uncited and method-dependent. Also, calling \(|a_k-p_k|/p_k\not\to0\) the stronger condition is inaccurate: requiring \(r_k<\eta<1\) for every index in the subsequence already forces the relative discrepancy to remain bounded away from zero.

children.title: Stabilization Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by inadequate or unstable proximity and localization control.

children.title: Under-Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Trial points leave the region of model reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Under-Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Insufficient proximal stabilization relative to weak curvature and model reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\rho\)-weakly convex and consider the stabilized model subproblem \(\min_d\{m_k(x_k+d;x_k)+(\lambda_k/2)\|d\|^2\}\). Under-stabilization occurs when \(\lambda_k\) does not dominate the model's negative-curvature modulus, or when the resulting step satisfies \(\|d_k\|>\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k\) is the radius on which model accuracy is certified. In the first case the subproblem need not be strongly convex or well localized; in the second, its trial point lies outside the certified model region. Hence neither uniqueness nor reliable predicted decrease follows from the localized model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilization is insufficient when it fails to offset negative curvature or permits a trial step beyond the model-validity radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the local model have finite weak-curvature moduli near \(x_k\).
Model accuracy is certified only for \(\|d\|\le\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized subproblem lacks a certified localization or strong-convexity guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the container, but the model's negative-curvature modulus and the meaning of one parameter dominating it are not defined. A source is needed to determine the correct threshold, parameter convention, and guarantees for the stated stabilized subproblem.

children.title: Over-Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Excessive localization suppresses useful progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Over-Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Excessive proximal regularization that forces vanishing steps without comparable stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the stabilized subproblem \(d_k\in\arg\min_d\{m_k(x_k+d;x_k)+(\lambda_k/2)\|d\|^2\}\), over-stabilization occurs along an infinite index set \(K\) when \(\lambda_k\to\infty\), \(\|d_k\|\to0\), but a stationarity residual \(s_k\) satisfies \(\liminf_{k\in K}s_k>0\). The vanishing step is then caused by the penalty rather than proximity to stationarity. If model subgradients remain bounded, the optimality relation typically gives \(\|d_k\|=O(1/\lambda_k)\); thus unbounded stabilization can suppress objective progress while leaving the underlying stationarity defect unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over-stabilization forces tiny steps through an excessive proximal penalty even though the stationarity residual remains bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: The stabilized subproblem has a computed minimizer \(d_k\).
A consistent stationarity residual \(s_k\ge0\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|d_k\|\to0\) does not certify stationarity when \(\liminf_{k\in K}s_k>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative failure phenomenon fits the leaf, but the stationarity residual is unspecified and the claimed \(O(1/\lambda_k)\) step rate requires a precise subproblem optimality relation and bounded model subgradients at the relevant points. No source supports this boundary or rate.

children.title: Stabilization-Parameter Oscillation
children.top_down_role: Unstable adaptation prevents consistent model use.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Parameter Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsettling stabilization updates that alternate between incompatible localization regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda_k>0\) be the proximal stabilization parameter. Stabilization-parameter oscillation occurs when there exist constants \(0<\lambda_-<\lambda_+\) and two infinite index sets \(K_-,K_+\) such that \(\lambda_k\le\lambda_-\) for \(k\in K_-\) and \(\lambda_k\ge\lambda_+\) for \(k\in K_+\). If the lower regime permits steps outside the model-validity radius while the upper regime suppresses accepted progress, then no tail of the iteration sequence uses a consistent reliable scale. Convergence arguments requiring eventual bounds \(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_k\le\overline\lambda<\infty\) or eventual model agreement are therefore inapplicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilization parameter oscillates when it repeatedly enters both under-stabilized and over-stabilized regimes, preventing eventual use of a consistent reliable scale.
assumptions_latex: The low and high regimes have the stated model-validity effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No eventual stabilization regime satisfying the required reliability bounds is established.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-subsequence condition can describe nonsettling behavior, but it does not by itself invalidate convergence arguments requiring eventual positive lower and finite upper bounds: a bounded sequence may oscillate forever while satisfying both bounds. A cited method-specific criterion is needed to connect the low and high regimes to failure of model agreement or convergence assumptions.

children.title: Bundle Numerical Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by model stagnation, excessive storage, compression loss, or ill-conditioning.

children.title: Null-Step Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Repeated model refinement without useful progress.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Rejection under Nonpositive Actual Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary mechanism forcing null steps under a positive-threshold agreement test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_k>0\) be predicted reduction, \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(y_k)\) actual reduction, and accept a serious step only if \(A_k/\Delta_k\ge\eta\), where \(\eta>0\). If \(f(y_k)\ge f(x_k)\), then \(A_k/\Delta_k\le0<\eta\), so the trial is rejected. If rejection leaves \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), indefinite recurrence keeps the stability center fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trials that fail to reduce the objective are necessarily rejected by a positive-threshold agreement test despite positive predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: A rejected trial leaves the stability center unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(y_k)\ge f(x_k)\implies x_{k+1}=x_k\text{ under the stated test}.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Rejection under Nonpositive Actual Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite Null Steps Are Not a Failure Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating repeated rejection from genuine nonstationary stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Infinitely many rejected trials with \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) do not alone imply algorithmic failure. If a valid method-specific stationarity measure \(s_k\) tends to zero along those null steps, the iterations may be successfully certifying stationarity at the fixed center. A nonstationary-stagnation claim therefore requires an additional condition such as \(\liminf s_k>0\), persistent model error, or failure of the method's established null-step convergence alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated null steps may certify stationarity; genuine stagnation requires a nonvanishing valid error or stationarity measure.
assumptions_latex: \(s_k\ge0\) is a valid stationarity measure for the specified bundle method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Infinitely many null steps alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{nonstationary stagnation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Null Steps Are Not a Failure Certificate
Null-Step Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite rejected-step refinement without stationarity or meaningful model improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\) be the stability center of a bundle method, and call iteration \(k\) a null step when its trial point is rejected and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Null-step stagnation occurs on an infinite set \(K\) when \(x_k=\bar x\) for all \(k\in K\), the stationarity certificate \(s_k\) satisfies \(\inf_{k\in K}s_k>0\), and model refinement fails to close the relevant error, for example \(\inf_{k\in K}[f(y_k)-m_k(y_k;\bar x)]>0\). Thus infinitely many added cuts neither produce a serious step nor certify stationarity at the center.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-step stagnation means repeated rejected trials refine the bundle without moving the center, closing model error, or certifying stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Each null step keeps the stability center fixed.
\(s_k\) is a valid nonnegative stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The null-step sequence yields neither a serious step nor stationarity at \(\bar x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the proposed conjunction of a fixed center, positive stationarity certificate, and uniformly positive model gap is a bespoke stagnation definition with no source. The certificate and the model orientation needed to interpret the gap must be specified.

children.title: Bundle Memory Growth
children.top_down_role: Uncontrolled storage and subproblem expansion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct storage safeguard for an explicit affine-cut bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(M\ge1\). If after every oracle call the method retains at most \(M\) raw affine cuts and at most one aggregate cut, then \[|B_k|\le M+1\] for every \(k\). Storing one scalar and one vector in \(\mathbb R^n\) per element uses at most \((M+1)(n+1)\) real numbers, excluding fixed overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard raw-cut cap plus one aggregate gives a uniform bundle-storage bound independent of the number of oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: At most \(M\) raw cuts and one aggregate cut are retained.
Each affine cut stores one scalar and one n-dimensional slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |B_k|\le M+1\quad\text{and explicit cut storage is }O(Mn).
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Memory Retention Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact storage growth for a bundle represented as stored oracle records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\) be an ordered or multiplicity-preserving container of bundle records. If each of \(N_k\) oracle calls appends exactly one record and no record is deleted, merged, or aggregated, then \[|B_k|=|B_0|+N_k.\] If each record stores one scalar and one vector in \(\mathbb R^n\), explicit cut storage is exactly \((n+1)(|B_0|+N_k)\) real numbers, excluding fixed container and solver overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a record container that retains every oracle output, bundle count and explicit cut storage grow linearly with oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one record is appended per oracle call.
No record is deleted, merged, or aggregated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |B_k|=|B_0|+N_k\quad\text{and storage is }\Theta(n(|B_0|+N_k)).

notation.meaning: number of oracle calls through iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity-Preserving Full-Memory Growth
Bundle Memory Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and subproblem-size growth when bundle elements are retained without deletion or aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\) be the bundle after iteration \(k\), with one affine model element added per oracle call and none deleted or aggregated. After \(N_k\) oracle calls, \(|B_k|=|B_0|+N_k\). Storing each element's point, scalar value, and subgradient in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) requires \(\Theta(n|B_k|)\) real numbers, and a master problem with one constraint or multiplier per element has dimension or constraint count \(\Theta(|B_k|)\). Hence unrestricted retention causes linear memory growth in oracle calls and monotonically enlarges the bundle subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without deletion or aggregation, bundle size grows by one per oracle call, requiring linear-in-calls storage and an increasingly large master problem.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one bundle element is added per oracle call.
No element is deleted, merged, or aggregated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|B_k|=|B_0|+N_k\) and storage is \(\Theta(n(|B_0|+N_k))\).

notation.meaning: number of oracle calls through iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct counting argument is plausible and complexity_bound is appropriate, but no source is cited. Exact equality requires the bundle to retain one distinct stored record per oracle call rather than being a mathematical set that may collapse duplicates, and the master-problem size statement depends on its formulation.

children.title: Aggregation Information Loss
children.top_down_role: Compression that removes information needed for fidelity or identification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fidelity diagnostic between full and compressed cut models on a prescribed region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty region \(D\), define \[\delta_D(m,\widetilde m)=\sup_{y\in D}[m(y)-\widetilde m(y)]\in[0,+\infty].\] Under compressed-model domination, \(\delta_D=0\) exactly when the compressed and full models agree throughout \(D\); \(\delta_D>0\) certifies regional information loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The supremum pointwise model gap exactly detects whether aggregation preserved the full model on a specified region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_D=0\iff m=\widetilde m\text{ on }D.
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Aggregation-Loss Measure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Center Match with Regional and Slope Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional example separating center preservation from regional fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell_1(y)=y\), \(\ell_2(y)=-y\), and aggregate them with weights \(1/2,1/2\). Then \[m(y)=\max\{y,-y\}=|y|,\qquad\bar\ell(y)=0.\] At \(y=0\), both models have value zero and the aggregate slope zero belongs to \(\partial m(0)\). Nevertheless \(m(y)-\bar\ell(y)=|y|>0\) for every \(y\ne0\), and the individual slopes \(1\) and \(-1\) are not recoverable from the aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Center value and an aggregate subgradient can be preserved while all off-center V-shaped growth and the original slopes are lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m(0)=\bar\ell(0)\text{ but }m(y)>\bar\ell(y)\text{ for }y\ne0.
knowledge_statements.title: Center Match with Regional and Slope Loss

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise effect of replacing discarded affine cuts by one convex aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) and \(J\) partition a finite cut index set, let \(m(y)=\max_{i\in R\cup J}\ell_i(y)\), and let \(\bar\ell(y)=\sum_{j\in J}\alpha_j\ell_j(y)\), where \(\alpha_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j\in J}\alpha_j=1\). For \[\widetilde m(y)=\max\{\max_{i\in R}\ell_i(y),\bar\ell(y)\},\] one has \(\widetilde m(y)\le m(y)\) for every \(y\). Equality at one point does not imply equality elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing discarded cuts by a convex aggregate can only lower the maximum-of-cuts model, and a pointwise match need not preserve regional fidelity.
assumptions_latex: The aggregate uses convex weights over the discarded cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde m\le m\quad\text{pointwise}.
knowledge_statements.title: Compressed-Model Domination
Aggregation Information Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a compressed bundle to preserve cuts needed for model fidelity or active-structure identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the full bundle model be \(m_k(y)=\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(y)\), and let aggregation replace a discarded subset by a single affine function \(\bar\ell(y)=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i\ell_i(y)\), where \(\alpha_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\). The compressed model \(\widetilde m_k\) loses required information on a region \(D_k\) if \(\sup_{y\in D_k}[m_k(y)-\widetilde m_k(y)]>\varepsilon_k\), or if distinct active slopes needed for identification are absent from the compressed bundle. In either case, matching the aggregate value at the current center does not preserve regional fidelity or active-face geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation loses information when the compressed model departs materially from the full bundle or removes distinct slopes needed to identify active structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Center-value preservation alone does not guarantee fidelity on \(D_k\) or preservation of active-face information.

notation.meaning: region where model fidelity is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, but \(\widetilde m_k\) is not explicitly constructed from the retained cuts and aggregate, and the weights are indexed over the full bundle despite the text referring to a discarded subset. A source is needed for the regional-fidelity threshold and the claim about slopes required for active-structure identification.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Bundle Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability caused by redundant or poorly scaled bundle information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational diagnostic after fixing an active KKT formulation and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an active-set KKT matrix \(K_A\), a row-scaling convention, and the Euclidean norm. If \(K_A\) is nonsingular, the local linear-system sensitivity is governed by \(\kappa_2(K_A)=\sigma_{\max}(K_A)/\sigma_{\min}(K_A)\). A sequence with \(\sigma_{\min}(K_A)\downarrow0\) and bounded \(\sigma_{\max}(K_A)\) is increasingly ill-conditioned; \(\sigma_{\min}(K_A)=0\) certifies singularity of that representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once formulation and scaling are fixed, the smallest singular value gives a precise diagnostic for active bundle-system ill-conditioning.
assumptions_latex: The active KKT formulation and row scaling are fixed.
Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_{\min}(K_A)\downarrow0\implies\kappa_2(K_A)\to\infty\text{ when }\sigma_{\max}(K_A)\text{ stays bounded away from zero}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Active-System Conditioning Diagnostic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy pathology in an epigraph proximal bundle subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two active epigraph constraints are identical: \[a_i+\langle g_i,d\rangle\le r,\qquad a_j+\langle g_j,d\rangle\le r,\qquad(a_i,g_i)=(a_j,g_j).\] Replacing their nonnegative multipliers \((\lambda_i,\lambda_j)\) by any nonnegative pair having the same sum leaves the KKT equations unchanged. Thus a strongly convex proximal term may determine a unique primal displacement while the individual duplicate-cut multipliers remain nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate cuts can leave the primal trial point unique while making their separate dual weights nonidentifiable.
assumptions_latex: The two active affine constraints are identical.
The formulation assigns one multiplier to each stored cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\text{ may be unique while }(\lambda_i,\lambda_j)\text{ is nonunique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Cuts Destroy Multiplier Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning Depends on Formulation and Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on treating a bundle KKT condition number as intrinsic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplying any bundle inequality by a positive scalar preserves its feasible set and primal optimizer but rescales its KKT row and associated multiplier. The singular values and condition number of the resulting KKT matrix can therefore change under equivalent positive rescalings. Any quantitative conditioning claim must specify the formulation, row scaling, norm, and active-set convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent constraint scaling can leave the primal bundle problem unchanged while changing its KKT condition number.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning is measured for a specified KKT matrix representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa(K)\text{ is representation dependent even when the primal problem is unchanged}.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Depends on Formulation and Scaling
Ill-Conditioned Bundle Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning failure in proximal bundle quadratic subproblems with redundant active cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the bundle subproblem 
\[\min_{d,r}\; r+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert d\rVert^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_i+\langle g_i,d\rangle\le r,\quad i=1,\ldots,m.\]
If the active cut normals are nearly affinely dependent, the smallest singular value of the active constraint matrix approaches zero. Consequently, the condition number of the associated KKT system becomes arbitrarily large. In finite-precision arithmetic, computed primal-dual solutions may then have large relative error, unreliable multipliers, or violated cuts despite a small linear-system residual. Exact duplication makes the active KKT matrix singular unless redundant constraints are removed or regularization is added.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly dependent or badly scaled active cuts make a bundle KKT system singular or ill-conditioned, so finite-precision solutions and multipliers become unreliable.
assumptions_latex: \(t>0\) and the subproblem is solved through its active-set KKT system.
The bundle coefficients \(a_i\in\mathbb R\) and normals \(g_i\in\mathbb R^n\) are represented in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near affine dependence of active normals implies unbounded KKT conditioning; exact redundant dependence may imply singularity.
review_flags: exact conditioning formulation may depend on the chosen subproblem representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and failure-boundary placement fit the terminal container, but the asserted relation between affine dependence, the smallest singular value, and the condition number depends on the precise active KKT formulation and scaling. The claims about finite-precision relative error and residual reliability require an inspectable bundle-specific numerical-analysis source.

children.title: Stationarity-Convergence Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundaries preventing the desired criticality or sequence-convergence conclusions.

children.title: Stationarity-Measure Mismatch
children.top_down_role: A computable certificate does not represent the desired criticality notion.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Measure Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke residual can vanish without limiting-subdifferential criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(f(x)=-|x|\). At \(x=0\), the Clarke subdifferential is \(\partial_C f(0)=[-1,1]\), whereas the limiting subdifferential is \(\partial f(0)=\{-1,1\}\). Hence
\[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_C f(0))=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(0))=1.\]
Thus a method whose computable certificate is the Clarke residual may report zero stationarity although the desired limiting-criticality condition \(0\in\partial f(0)\) fails. Convergence of the computed residual alone therefore cannot establish the stronger criticality notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minus absolute value at zero, Clarke stationarity holds but limiting stationarity fails, so a Clarke-based certificate can certify the wrong notion.
assumptions_latex: The desired criticality notion is \(0\in\partial f(x)\), using the Mordukhovich limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing Clarke residual does not, in general, imply limiting-subdifferential stationarity.

children.title: Nonisolated Cluster Behavior
children.top_down_role: Multiple accumulation points obstruct full-sequence conclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Cluster Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point stationarity does not imply convergence of the entire iterate sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), and define \(x_{2k}=1\) and \(x_{2k+1}=-1\). Then \(f(x_k)=0\) and \(f'(x_k)=0\) for every \(k\). The cluster set is \(\{-1,1\}\), so every accumulation point is stationary and all objective values converge, but \((x_k)\) does not converge. Therefore, a convergence theorem establishing only boundedness, convergence of objective values, and stationarity of every cluster point cannot establish full-sequence convergence without an additional mechanism such as cluster-point uniqueness, isolation, or a finite-length property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence may alternate between two stationary minimizers while objective values and stationarity residuals converge, preventing full-sequence convergence.
assumptions_latex: Only cluster-point stationarity and convergence of \(f(x_k)\) are asserted.
No uniqueness, isolation, or finite-length condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stationarity of all cluster points does not imply convergence of the full sequence.

children.title: Loss of Level Boundedness
children.top_down_role: Failure of compactness for serious or trial sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Level Boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Without bounded lower-level sets, descent does not ensure bounded iterates or accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=e^{-x}\) on \(\mathbb R\), and take \(x_k=k\). Then \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k)\downarrow0=\inf f\), but \(x_k\to+\infty\), so the sequence has no accumulation point. Moreover, each initial lower-level set
\[\{x\in\mathbb R:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}=[x_0,\infty)\]
is unbounded. Hence monotone decrease and convergence of objective values alone do not provide compactness of serious or trial iterates. A bounded-level-set assumption, coercivity, or an explicit boundedness safeguard is required for cluster-point arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exponential objective, objective values decrease to the infimum while iterates escape to infinity, showing why level boundedness is needed.
assumptions_latex: The convergence argument derives boundedness only from descent within the initial lower-level set.
No independent trust-region or iterate-boundedness condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of level boundedness permits descending sequences with no convergent subsequence.

children.title: Inexactness Accumulation
children.top_down_role: Oracle and inner-solver errors overwhelm model improvement.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If neither summability nor sufficient relative domination of the errors is imposed, the perturbed decrease inequality alone need not imply \(\Delta_k\to 0\).

notation.meaning: predicted model improvement or stationarity decrement

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the conclusions follow by summing or rearranging the displayed inequality
method-specific error decomposition still requires source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent oracle or inner-solver errors can consume the guaranteed model improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose accepted iterations satisfy the perturbed decrease inequality
\[F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-c\Delta_k+\eta_k,\]
where \(c>0\), \(\Delta_k\ge 0\) is the predicted stationarity-producing decrease, and \(\eta_k\ge 0\) collects oracle and subproblem errors. If \(F\) is bounded below and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty\), summation implies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\Delta_k<\infty\), hence \(\Delta_k\to 0\). Alternatively, if there are \(K\in\mathbb N\) and \(\theta<c\) such that \(\eta_k\le\theta\Delta_k\) for every \(k\ge K\), then the same inequality yields eventual decrease by at least \((c-\theta)\Delta_k\), and again \(\Delta_k\to 0\). If neither form of error control is available, \(\eta_k\) may equal or exceed \(c\Delta_k\) indefinitely, so the inequality alone yields neither summability nor vanishing of \(\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable errors or errors eventually dominated by the predicted improvement preserve the decrease argument; without either control, persistent errors can prevent the stationarity decrement from vanishing.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexactness Accumulation

children.title: Model-Validity Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Protective responses to unreliable local models or invalid approximation regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Validity Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable lower-model validity for weakly convex objectives and inexact cutting planes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(\rho\)-weakly convex. For every bundle point \(z_i\) with \(g_i\in\partial f(z_i)\) and oracle tolerance \(\varepsilon_i\ge0\), define
\[q_i(y)=f(z_i)+\langle g_i,y-z_i\rangle-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert y-z_i\rVert^2-\varepsilon_i,
\qquad m(y)=\max_i q_i(y).\]
A model-validity safeguard requires \(m(y)\le f(y)\) throughout the accepted trial region, up to a declared evaluation tolerance. A trial revealing a larger violation must not be accepted using that model; the method must instead correct or discard the offending cut, enlarge its error allowance, or contract the trial region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak-convexity cuts must remain valid lower models on the accepted trial region; detected violations trigger model repair or region contraction.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is an exact or tolerance-qualified subgradient at \(z_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The safeguarded model satisfies \(m(y)\le f(y)\) within its declared tolerance on every accepted trial region.
review_flags: bundle acceptance response is a synthesized safeguard condition

children.title: Stabilization Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Protective responses to ineffective regularization, acceptance control, or stabilization choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive proximal curvature enforces well-posed and sufficiently localized model steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the current model \(m_k\) be \(\rho_k\)-weakly convex, and consider
\[x_k^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\left\{m_k(y)+\frac{	au_k}{2}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.\]
A stabilization safeguard chooses \(\tau_k\geho_k+
u\) for a fixed margin \(\nu>0\). The stabilized objective is then \(\nu\)-strongly convex and has at most one minimizer. If the computed step exceeds the permitted radius, the subproblem is insufficiently solved, or actual reduction is too small relative to predicted reduction, \(\tau_k\) is increased before another trial. Decrease of \(\tau_k\) is permitted only after a successful, model-consistent trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose proximal curvature above model nonconvexity, and increase it after oversized, inaccurate, or poorly predicted trials to retain a unique localized step.
assumptions_latex: The model has a known or conservatively estimated weak-convexity modulus \(\rho_k\).
A fixed strong-convexity margin \(\nu>0\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilized subproblem is \(\nu\)-strongly convex whenever \(\tau_k\ge\rho_k+\nu\).
review_flags: adaptive update rule requires bundle-method source confirmation

However, the cited weak-convexity section does not adequately support the method-specific rules that increase or decrease \(\tau_k\) in response to radius, solve accuracy, and reduction-ratio tests. children.title: Bundle-Robustness Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Protective responses to bundle degeneration, memory pressure, compression loss, or poor conditioning.

assumptions_latex: All indices in \(I\) are active at \(y_k\), so their cut values coincide.
The aggregation weights form a convex combination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregation preserves the common active value and produces the convexly aggregated slope while permitting conditional bundle compression.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the convex aggregation identities are algebraically checkable
bundle pruning and scaling policy requires a method-specific source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling, pruning, and aggregation control bundle size without discarding the current aggregate certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For affine cuts \(\ell_i(y)=a_i+\langle g_i,y\rangle\), let \(I\ne\varnothing\) be active at a reference point \(y_k\), and let \(\lambda_i\ge 0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1\). Define the aggregate cut
\[\bar\ell(y)=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\ell_i(y).\]
Because all cuts indexed by \(I\) have the same value at \(y_k\), the aggregate satisfies \(\bar\ell(y_k)=\ell_i(y_k)\) for every \(i\in I\), and its slope is \(\bar g=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i\). A bundle-robustness safeguard may replace those active cuts by \(\bar\ell\), prune inactive nearly duplicate cuts, and rescale variables and constraints only when the aggregate cut and every cut required for current model validity are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate active cuts using convex multipliers, and prune or rescale only while retaining the aggregate certificate and all cuts required for current model validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Robustness Safeguards

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x_k)\) remain in a compact set, let \(F\) be bounded below there, and suppose
\[F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-c r_k^2+\eta_k,
\qquad c>0,
\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\]
Then \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}r_k^2<\infty\), and hence \(r_k\to 0\). If every convergent subsequence \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\) satisfies the consistency implication \(r_{k_j}\to 0\Rightarrow 0\in\partial F(\bar x)\), then every cluster point is stationary. Full-sequence convergence additionally requires a condition that rules out multiple cluster points, such as uniqueness of the cluster point or a finite-length estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact iterates, sufficient decrease, summable errors, and a consistent residual yield stationary cluster points; full convergence needs an additional mechanism that rules out multiple cluster points.
